1.24.s:
sūta uvāca
atha devo hṛṣīkeśo bhagavān puruṣottamaḥ /
tatāpa ghoraṃ putrārthaṃ nidānaṃ tapasastapaḥ //
1.24.d:
सूत उवाच
अथ देवो हृषीकेशो भगवान् पुरुषोत्तमः ।
तताप घोरं पुत्रार्थं निदानं तपसस्तपः ॥
1.24.m:
Sūta said:
Then the divine Hṛṣīkeśa, the blessed Supreme Spirit,
a primary source of austerity, performed terrible austerity for the sake of a son.

1.24.s:
svecchayāpyavatīrṇo 'sau kṛtakṛtyo 'pi viśvadhṛk /
cacāra svātmano mūlaṃ bodhayan bhāvamaiśvaram //
1.24.d:
स्वेच्छयाप्यवतीर्णो ऽसौ कृतकृत्यो ऽपि विश्वधृक् ।
चचार स्वात्मनो मूलं बोधयन् भावमैश्वरम् ॥
1.24.m:
Though descended by his own will, though fulfilled in all actions, the upholder of all
acted, teaching the sovereign state that is the source of his own self.

1.24.s:
jagāma yogibhirjuṣṭaṃ nānāpakṣisamākulam /
āśramaṃ tūpamanyorvai munīndrasya mahātmanaḥ //
1.24.d:
जगाम योगिभिर्जुष्टं नानापक्षिसमाकुलम् ।
आश्रमं तूपमन्योर्वै मुनीन्द्रस्य महात्मनः ॥
1.24.m:
He went to the hermitage of Upamanyu, the great-souled prince of sages,
frequented by yogins and filled with various birds.

1.24.s:
tapattrirājamārūḍhaḥ suparṇamatitejasam /
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiḥ śrīvatsakṛtalakṣaṇaḥ //
1.24.d:
तपत्त्रिराजमारूढः सुपर्णमतितेजसम् ।
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिः श्रीवत्सकृतलक्षणः ॥
1.24.m:
Mounted upon the bird-king Suparṇa of exceeding radiance,
conch, discus, and mace in hand, marked with the śrīvatsa,

1.24.s:
nānādrumalatākīrṇaṃ nānāpuṣpopaśobhitam /
ṛṣīṇāmāśramairjuṣṭaṃ vedaghoṣanināditam //
1.24.d:
नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णं नानापुष्पोपशोभितम् ।
ऋषीणामाश्रमैर्जुष्टं वेदघोषनिनादितम् ॥
1.24.m:
overspread with various trees and creepers, adorned with diverse flowers,
frequented by the hermitages of ṛṣis, echoing with the recitation of the Vedas,

1.24.s:
siṃharkṣaśarabhākīrṇaṃ śārdūlagajasaṃyutam /
vimalasvādupānīyaiḥ sarobhirupaśobhitam //
1.24.d:
सिंहर्क्षशरभाकीर्णं शार्दूलगजसंयुतम् ।
विमलस्वादुपानीयैः सरोभिरुपशोभितम् ॥
1.24.m:
crowded with lions, bears, and śarabhas, filled with tigers and elephants,
adorned with lakes of clear, sweet water,

1.24.s:
ārāmairvividhairjuṣṭaṃ devatāyatanaiḥ śubhaiḥ /
ṛṣikairṛṣiputraiśca mahāmunigaṇaistathā //
1.24.d:
आरामैर्विविधैर्जुष्टं देवतायतनैः शुभैः ।
ऋषिकैरृषिपुत्रैश्च महामुनिगणैस्तथा ॥
1.24.m:
frequented by various groves, with auspicious shrines of deities,
by ṛṣis, sons of ṛṣis, and hosts of great sages,

1.24.s:
vedādhyayanasaṃpannaiḥ sevitaṃ cāgnihotribhiḥ /
yogibhirdhyānaniratairnāsāgragatalocanaiḥ //
1.24.d:
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नैः सेवितं चाग्निहोत्रिभिः ।
योगिभिर्ध्याननिरतैर्नासाग्रगतलोचनैः ॥
1.24.m:
served by those accomplished in Vedic study and maintainers of sacred fires,
by yogins dedicated to meditation with eyes fixed on the tip of the nose,

1.24.s:
upetaṃ sarvataḥ puṇyaṃ jñānibhistattvadarśibhiḥ /
nadībhirabhito juṣṭaṃ jāpakairbrahmavādibhiḥ //
1.24.d:
उपेतं सर्वतः पुण्यं ज्ञानिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ।
नदीभिरभितो जुष्टं जापकैर्ब्रह्मवादिभिः ॥
1.24.m:
sacred, attended on all sides by the wise who perceive reality,
frequented round about by rivers, by silent chanters and expounders of the Veda,

1.24.s:
sevitaṃ tāpasaiḥ puṇyairīśārādhanatatparaiḥ /
praśāntaiḥ satyasaṃkalpairniḥ śokairnirupadravaiḥ //
1.24.d:
सेवितं तापसैः पुण्यैरीशाराधनतत्परैः ।
प्रशान्तैः सत्यसंकल्पैर्निः शोकैर्निरुपद्रवैः ॥
1.24.m:
served by holy ascetics devoted to the worship of the Lord,
peaceful, of true resolve, free from grief and free from adversity,

1.24.s:
bhasmāvadātasarvāṅgai rudrajāpyaparāyaṇaiḥ /
muṇḍitairjaṭilaiḥ śuddhaistathānyaiśca śikhājaṭaiḥ /
sevitaṃ tāpasairnitya jñānibhirbrahmacāribhiḥ //
1.24.d:
भस्मावदातसर्वाङ्गै रुद्रजाप्यपरायणैः ।
मुण्डितैर्जटिलैः शुद्धैस्तथान्यैश्च शिखाजटैः ।
सेवितं तापसैर्नित्य ज्ञानिभिर्ब्रह्मचारिभिः ॥
1.24.m:
their limbs whitened with ashes, dedicated to the silent recitation of Rudra,
some shaven, some matted-haired, pure, others with braided tufts of hair,
served constantly by ascetics, the wise and celibate students.

1.24.s:
tatrāśramavare ramye siddhāśramavibhūṣite /
gaṅgā bhagavatī nityaṃ vahatyevāghanāśinī //
1.24.d:
तत्राश्रमवरे रम्ये सिद्धाश्रमविभूषिते ।
गङ्गा भगवती नित्यं वहत्येवाघनाशिनी ॥
1.24.m:
There in that delightful, excellent hermitage, adorned by the hermitage of perfected ones,
the blessed Gaṅgā flows perpetually, destroying sins.

1.24.s:
sa tānanviṣya viśvātmā tāpasān vītakalmaṣān /
praṇāmenātha vacasā pūjayāmāsa mādhavaḥ //
1.24.d:
स तानन्विष्य विश्वात्मा तापसान् वीतकल्मषान् ।
प्रणामेनाथ वचसा पूजयामास माधवः ॥
1.24.m:
Seeking out those sinless ascetics, Mādhava,
the Self of all, honored them with obeisance and words.

1.24.s:
te te dṛṣṭvā jagadyoniṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam /
praṇemurbhaktisaṃyuktā yogināṃ paramaṃ gurum //
1.24.d:
ते ते दृष्ट्वा जगद्योनिं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् ।
प्रणेमुर्भक्तिसंयुक्ता योगिनां परमं गुरुम् ॥
1.24.m:
Seeing the source of the world bearing the conch, discus, and mace,
they bowed with devotion to the supreme teacher of yogins.

1.24.s:
stuvanti vaidikairmantraiḥ kṛtvā hṛdi sanātanam /
procuranyonyamavyaktamādidevaṃ mahāmunim //
1.24.d:
स्तुवन्ति वैदिकैर्मन्त्रैः कृत्वा हृदि सनातनम् ।
प्रोचुरन्योन्यमव्यक्तमादिदेवं महामुनिम् ॥
1.24.m:
Praising him with Vedic mantras, holding the eternal one in their hearts,
they spoke to one another of that unmanifest primal god, the great sage:

1.24.s:
ayaṃ sa bhagavānekaḥ sākṣānnārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ /
agacchatyadhunā devaḥ purāṇapuruṣaḥ svayam //
1.24.d:
अयं स भगवानेकः साक्षान्नारायणः परः ।
अगच्छत्यधुना देवः पुराणपुरुषः स्वयम् ॥
1.24.m:
“This is the one blessed Lord, the supreme Nārāyaṇa manifest;
now the god, the ancient person himself, approaches.

1.24.s:
ayamevāvyayaḥ straṣṭā saṃhartā caiva rakṣakaḥ /
amūrto mūrtimān bhūtvā munīn draṣṭumihāgataḥ //
1.24.d:
अयमेवाव्ययः स्त्रष्टा संहर्ता चैव रक्षकः ।
अमूर्तो मूर्तिमान् भूत्वा मुनीन् द्रष्टुमिहागतः ॥
1.24.m:
He alone is the imperishable creator, destroyer, and protector;
becoming embodied though formless, he has come here to see the sages.

1.24.s:
eṣa dhātā vidhātā ca samāgacchati sarvagaḥ /
anādirakṣayo 'nanto mahābhūto maheśvaraḥ //
1.24.d:
एष धाता विधाता च समागच्छति सर्वगः ।
अनादिरक्षयो ऽनन्तो महाभूतो महेश्वरः ॥
1.24.m:
He, the supporter and ordainer, the all-pervading one, approaches;
beginningless, indestructible, endless, the great entity, the great lord.”

1.24.s:
śrutvā śrutvā haristeṣāṃ vacāṃsi vacanātigaḥ /
yayau sa tūrṇaṃ govindaḥ sthānaṃ tasya mahātmanaḥ //
1.24.d:
श्रुत्वा श्रुत्वा हरिस्तेषां वचांसि वचनातिगः ।
ययौ स तूर्णं गोविन्दः स्थानं तस्य महात्मनः ॥
1.24.m:
Hearing their words again and again, Hari, beyond the realm of speech,
Govinda went swiftly to the dwelling of that great soul.

1.24.s:
upaspṛśyātha bhāvena tīrthe tīrthe sa yādavaḥ /
cakāra devakīsūnurdevarṣipitṛtarpaṇam //
1.24.d:
उपस्पृश्याथ भावेन तीर्थे तीर्थे स यादवः ।
चकार देवकीसूनुर्देवर्षिपितृतर्पणम् ॥
1.24.m:
Having sipped water with devotion at each holy ford, the Yādava,
the son of Devakī, performed libations to the gods, ṛṣis, and ancestors.

1.24.s:
nadīnāṃ tīrasaṃsthāni sthāpitāni munīśvaraiḥ /
liṅgāni pūjayāmāsa śaṃbhoramitatejasaḥ //
1.24.d:
नदीनां तीरसंस्थानि स्थापितानि मुनीश्वरैः ।
लिङ्गानि पूजयामास शंभोरमिततेजसः ॥
1.24.m:
He worshipped the liṅgas of Śambhu of immeasurable splendor
which were situated on the banks of rivers and established by sovereign sages.

1.24.s:
dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā samāyāntaṃ yatra yatra janārdanam /
pūjayāñcakrire puṣpairakṣataistatra vāsinaḥ //
1.24.d:
दृष्ट्वा दृष्ट्वा समायान्तं यत्र यत्र जनार्दनम् ।
पूजयाञ्चक्रिरे पुष्पैरक्षतैस्तत्र वासिनः ॥
1.24.m:
Seeing Janārdana approaching wherever he went,
the inhabitants there worshipped him with flowers and unbroken grains.

1.24.s:
samīkṣya vāsudevaṃ taṃ śārṅgaśaṅkhāsidhāriṇam /
tasthire niścalāḥ sarve śubhāṅgaṃ tannivāsinaḥ //
1.24.d:
समीक्ष्य वासुदेवं तं शार्ङ्गशङ्खासिधारिणम् ।
तस्थिरे निश्चलाः सर्वे शुभाङ्गं तन्निवासिनः ॥
1.24.m:
Beholding Vāsudeva of auspicious limbs, holding bow, conch, and sword,
all the dwellers of that place stood motionless.

1.24.s:
yāni tatrārurukṣūṇāṃ mānasāni janārdanam /
dṛṣṭvā samīhitānyāsan niṣkrāmanti purāhiram //
1.24.d:
यानि तत्रारुरुक्षूणां मानसानि जनार्दनम् ।
दृष्ट्वा समीहितान्यासन् निष्क्रामन्ति पुराहिरम् ॥
1.24.m:
The desires that arose in the minds of those who longed to attain Janārdana
upon seeing him, were realized before Hari.

1.24.s:
athāvagāhya gaṅgāyāṃ kṛtvā devāditarpaṇam /
ādāya puṣpavaryāṇi munīndrasyāviśad gṛham //
1.24.d:
अथावगाह्य गङ्गायां कृत्वा देवादितर्पणम् ।
आदाय पुष्पवर्याणि मुनीन्द्रस्याविशद् गृहम् ॥
1.24.m:
Then, having bathed in the Gaṅgā and performed libations to the gods and others,
taking choice flowers, he entered the dwelling of the prince of sages.

1.24.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ yogināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhasmoddhūlitavigraham /
jaṭācīradharaṃ śāntaṃ nanāma śirasā munim //
1.24.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं योगिनां श्रेष्ठं भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहम् ।
जटाचीरधरं शान्तं ननाम शिरसा मुनिम् ॥
1.24.m: Seeing him, the foremost of yogins, his body smeared with ashes, / wearing matted locks and bark garments, tranquil, he bowed his head to the sage.

1.24.s:
ālokya kṛṣṇamāyāntaṃ pūjayāmāsa tattvavit /
āsane cāsayāmāsa yogināṃ prathamātithim //
1.24.d:
आलोक्य कृष्णमायान्तं पूजयामास तत्त्ववित् ।
आसने चासयामास योगिनां प्रथमातिथिम् ॥
1.24.m: Beholding Kṛṣṇa arriving, the knower of truth honored him, / and seated the foremost guest among yogins upon a seat.

1.24.s:
uvāca vacasāṃ yoniṃ jānīmaḥ paramaṃ padam /
viṣṇumavyaktasaṃsthānaṃ śiṣyabhāvena saṃsthitam //
1.24.d:
उवाच वचसां योनिं जानीमः परमं पदम् ।
विष्णुमव्यक्तसंस्थानं शिष्यभावेन संस्थितम् ॥
1.24.m: He said: “We recognize the source of speech, the supreme state, / Viṣṇu, whose abode is the unmanifest, standing in the guise of a disciple.

1.24.s:
svāgataṃ te hṛṣīkeśa saphalāni tapāṃsi naḥ /
yad sākṣādeva viśvātmā madgehaṃ viṣṇurāgataḥ //
1.24.d:
स्वागतं ते हृषीकेश सफलानि तपांसि नः ।
यद् साक्षादेव विश्वात्मा मद्गेहं विष्णुरागतः ॥
1.24.m: Welcome to you, Hṛṣīkeśa! Our austerities bear fruit, / since Viṣṇu, the Soul of All, has arrived in person at my home.

1.24.s:
tvāṃ na paśyanti munayo yatanto 'pi hi yoginaḥ /
tādṛśasyātha bhavataḥ kimāgamanakāraṇam //
1.24.d:
त्वां न पश्यन्ति मुनयो यतन्तो ऽपि हि योगिनः ।
तादृशस्याथ भवतः किमागमनकारणम् ॥
1.24.m: Even striving yogin sages do not behold you; / what, then, is the cause of the arrival of one such as you?”

1.24.s:
śrutvopamanyostad vākyaṃ bhagavān keśimardanaḥ /
vyājahāra mahāyogī vacanaṃ praṇipatya tam //
1.24.d:
श्रुत्वोपमन्योस्तद् वाक्यं भगवान् केशिमर्दनः ।
व्याजहार महायोगी वचनं प्रणिपत्य तम् ॥
1.24.m: Having heard those words of Upamanyu, the Lord, the crusher of Keśin, / the great yogin, bowed down to him and uttered these words:

1.24.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca
bhagavan draṣṭumicchāmi girīśaṃ kṛttivāsasam /
saṃprāpto bhavataḥ sthānaṃ bhagavaddarśanotsukaḥ //
1.24.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच
भगवन् द्रष्टुमिच्छामि गिरीशं कृत्तिवाससम् ।
संप्राप्तो भवतः स्थानं भगवद्दर्शनोत्सुकः ॥
1.24.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / “O Lord, I wish to see the Lord of the Mountain, clad in animal skins. / Desirous of the sight of the Lord, I have arrived at your abode.

1.24.s:
kathaṃ sa bhagavānīśo dṛśyo yogavidāṃ varaḥ /
mayācireṇa kutrāhaṃ drakṣyāmi tamumāpatim //
1.24.d:
कथं स भगवानीशो दृश्यो योगविदां वरः ।
मयाचिरेण कुत्राहं द्रक्ष्यामि तमुमापतिम् ॥
1.24.m: How may that Lord, the ruler, the best of knowers of yoga, be seen / by me without delay? Where shall I behold that husband of Umā?”

1.24.s:
ityāha bhagavānukto dṛśyate parameśvaraḥ /
bhaktyā cogreṇa tapasā tatkuruṣveha yatnataḥ //
1.24.d:
इत्याह भगवानुक्तो दृश्यते परमेश्वरः ।
भक्त्या चोग्रेण तपसा तत्कुरुष्वेह यत्नतः ॥
1.24.m: Thus addressed, the Lord [sage] said: “The Supreme Lord is beheld / through devotion and fierce austerity. Therefore, undertake that here with effort.

1.24.s:
iheśvaraṃ devadevaṃ munīndrā brahmavādinaḥ /
dhyāyanto 'trāsate devaṃ jāpinastāpasāśca ye //
1.24.d:
इहेश्वरं देवदेवं मुनीन्द्रा ब्रह्मवादिनः ।
ध्यायन्तो ऽत्रासते देवं जापिनस्तापसाश्च ये ॥
1.24.m: Here the foremost of sages who discourse on Brahman reside, / meditating upon the Lord, the God of gods, as do ascetics chanting prayers.

1.24.s:
iha devaḥ sapatnīko bhagavān vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ /
krīḍate vividhairbhūtairyogibhiḥ parivāritaḥ //
1.24.d:
इह देवः सपत्नीको भगवान् वृषभध्वजः ।
क्रीडते विविधैर्भूतैर्योगिभिः परिवारितः ॥
1.24.m: Here the divine, glorious one whose banner bears a bull, with his consort, / plays, surrounded by various spirits and yogins.

1.24.s:
ihāśrame purā rudrāt tapastaptvā sudāruṇam /
lebhe maheśvarād yogaṃ vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ //
1.24.d:
इहाश्रमे पुरा रुद्रात् तपस्तप्त्वा सुदारुणम् ।
लेभे महेश्वराद् योगं वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः ॥
1.24.m: Formerly, in this hermitage, having performed terrible austerity toward Rudra, / the venerable sage Vasiṣṭha obtained yoga from the Great Lord.

1.24.s:
ihaiva bhagavān vyasaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ /
dṛṣṭvā taṃ paramaṃ jñānaṃ labdhavānīśvareśvaram //
1.24.d:
इहैव भगवान् व्यसः कृष्णद्वैपायनः प्रभुः ।
दृष्ट्वा तं परमं ज्ञानं लब्धवानीश्वरेश्वरम् ॥
1.24.m: Right here the glorious master Vyāsa, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, / having beheld him, attained the supreme knowledge from the Lord of lords.

1.24.s:
ihāśramavare ramye tapastaptvā kapardinaḥ /
avindat putrakān rudrāt surabhirbhaktisaṃyutā //
1.24.d:
इहाश्रमवरे रम्ये तपस्तप्त्वा कपर्दिनः ।
अविन्दत् पुत्रकान् रुद्रात् सुरभिर्भक्तिसंयुता ॥
1.24.m: Having performed austerity toward the braided-haired one in this lovely, excellent hermitage, / Surabhi, endowed with devotion, obtained sons from Rudra.

1.24.s:
ihaiva devatāḥ pūrvaṃ kālād bhītā maheśvaram /
dṛṣṭavanto haraṃ śrīmannirbhayā nirvṛtiṃ yayuḥ //
1.24.d:
इहैव देवताः पूर्वं कालाद् भीता महेश्वरम् ।
दृष्टवन्तो हरं श्रीमन्निर्भया निर्वृतिं ययुः ॥
1.24.m: Right here formerly, the gods, terrified of time, / beheld the Great Lord Hara, O glorious one, and went to rest, free from fear.

1.24.s:
ihārādhya mahādevaṃ sāvarṇistapatāṃ varaḥ /
labdhavān paramaṃ yogaṃ granthakāratvamuttamam //
1.24.d:
इहाराध्य महादेवं सावर्णिस्तपतां वरः ।
लब्धवान् परमं योगं ग्रन्थकारत्वमुत्तमम् ॥
1.24.m: Having propitiated Mahādeva here, Sāvarṇi, the best of the ascetic, / obtained supreme yoga and the excellent authorship of a treatise.

1.24.s:
pravartayāmāsa śubhāṃ kṛtvā vai saṃhitāṃ dvijaḥ /
paurāṇikīṃ supuṇyārthāṃ sacchiṣyeṣu dvijātiṣu //
1.24.d:
प्रवर्तयामास शुभां कृत्वा वै संहितां द्विजः ।
पौराणिकीं सुपुण्यार्थां सच्छिष्येषु द्विजातिषु ॥
1.24.m: Having composed an auspicious collection concerning Purāṇas, bringing great merit, / that twice-born man set it forth among the twice-born who were his good disciples.

1.24.s:
ihaiva saṃhitāṃ dṛṣṭvā kāpeyaḥ śāṃśapāyanaḥ /
mahādevaṃ cakāremāṃ paurāṇīṃ tanniyogataḥ /
dvādaśaiva sahastrāṇi ślokānāṃ puruṣottama //
1.24.d:
इहैव संहितां दृष्ट्वा कापेयः शांशपायनः ।
महादेवं चकारेमां पौराणीं तन्नियोगतः ।
द्वादशैव सहस्त्राणि श्लोकानां पुरुषोत्तम ॥
1.24.m: Right here, having seen that compilation, Śāṃśapāyana of the Kapi gotra / made this Purāṇic [compilation] of twelve thousand verses / by the command of Mahādeva, O Supreme Spirit.

1.24.s:
iha pravartitā puṇyā dvyaṣṭasāhastrikottarā /
vāyavīyottaraṃ nāma purāṇaṃ vedasaṃmitam /
ihaiva khyāpitaṃ śiṣyaiḥ śāṃśapāyanabhāṣitam //
1.24.d:
इह प्रवर्तिता पुण्या द्व्यष्टसाहस्त्रिकोत्तरा ।
वायवीयोत्तरं नाम पुराणं वेदसंमितम् ।
इहैव ख्यापितं शिष्यैः शांशपायनभाषितम् ॥
1.24.m: Here was set forth that meritorious Purāṇa named Vāyavīyottara, / consisting of sixteen thousand verses, equal to the Vedas; / spoken by Śāṃśapāyana, it was proclaimed right here by disciples.

1.24.s:
yājñavalkyo mahāyogī dṛṣṭvātra tapasā haram /
cakāra tanniyogena yogaśāstramanuttamam //
1.24.d:
याज्ञवल्क्यो महायोगी दृष्ट्वात्र तपसा हरम् ।
चकार तन्नियोगेन योगशास्त्रमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.24.m: Having seen Hara here through austerity, the great yogin Yājñavalkya / composed the unsurpassed treatise on yoga by his command.

1.24.s:
ihaiva bhṛguṇā pūrvaṃ taptvā vai paramaṃ tapaḥ /
śukro maheśvarāt putro labdho yogavidāṃ varaḥ //
1.24.d:
इहैव भृगुणा पूर्वं तप्त्वा वै परमं तपः ।
शुक्रो महेश्वरात् पुत्रो लब्धो योगविदां वरः ॥
1.24.m: Right here formerly, having performed supreme austerity, / Bhṛgu obtained from the Great Lord his son Śukra, the best among knowers of yoga.

1.24.s:
tasmādihaiva deveśaṃ tapastaptvā maheśvaram /
draṣṭumarhasi viśveśamugraṃ bhīmaṃ kapardinam //
1.24.d:
तस्मादिहैव देवेशं तपस्तप्त्वा महेश्वरम् ।
द्रष्टुमर्हसि विश्वेशमुग्रं भीमं कपर्दिनम् ॥
1.24.m: Therefore, having performed austerity right here, you ought to behold / the Lord of gods, the Great Lord, the Lord of all, fierce, formidable, the braided-haired one.”

1.24.s:
evamuktvā dadau jñānamupamanyurmahāmuniḥ /
vrataṃ pāśupataṃ yogaṃ kṛṣṇāyākliṣṭakarmaṇe //
1.24.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ददौ ज्ञानमुपमन्युर्महामुनिः ।
व्रतं पाशुपतं योगं कृष्णायाक्लिष्टकर्मणे ॥
1.24.m: Having spoken thus, the great sage Upamanyu gave knowledge, / the Pāśupata vow, and yoga to Kṛṣṇa, whose deeds are unwearied.

1.24.s:
sa tena munivaryeṇa vyāhṛto madhusūdanaḥ /
tatraiva tapasā devaṃ rudramārādhayat prabhuḥ //
1.24.d:
स तेन मुनिवर्येण व्याहृतो मधुसूदनः ।
तत्रैव तपसा देवं रुद्रमाराधयत् प्रभुः ॥
1.24.m: Instructed by that best of sages, the Lord Madhusūdana, / right there through austerity, propitiated the divine Rudra.

1.24.s:
bhasmauddhūlitasarvāṅgo muṇḍo valkalasaṃyutaḥ /
jajāpa rudramaniśaṃ śivaikāhitamānasaḥ //
1.24.d:
भस्मौद्धूलितसर्वाङ्गो मुण्डो वल्कलसंयुतः ।
जजाप रुद्रमनिशं शिवैकाहितमानसः ॥
1.24.m: His entire body smeared with ashes, his head shaved, wearing bark garments, / he incessantly recited prayers to Rudra, his mind fixed exclusively on Śiva.

1.24.s:
tato bahutithe kāle somaḥ somārdhabhūṣaṇaḥ /
adṛśyata mahādevo vyomni devyā maheśvaraḥ //
1.24.d:
ततो बहुतिथे काले सोमः सोमार्धभूषणः ।
अदृश्यत महादेवो व्योम्नि देव्या महेश्वरः ॥
1.24.m: Then, after a great length of time, the Moon-crowned, adorned with the half-moon, / Mahādeva, the Great Lord, was seen in the sky along with the Goddess.

1.24.s:
kirīṭinaṃ gadinaṃ citramālaṃ
pinākinaṃ śūlinaṃ devadevam /
śārdūlacarmāmbarasaṃvṛtāṅgaṃ
devyā mahādevamasau dadarśa //
1.24.d:
किरीटिनं गदिनं चित्रमालं
पिनाकिनं शूलिनं देवदेवम् ।
शार्दूलचर्माम्बरसंवृताङ्गं
देव्या महादेवमसौ ददर्श ॥
1.24.m: Crowned, bearing a mace, with a varied garland, / wielding the Pināka, holding a trident, the God of gods, / his limbs covered with a tiger skin as a garment— / he beheld that Mahādeva along with the Goddess;

1.24.s:
paraśvadhāsaktakaraṃ trinetraṃ
nṛsiṃhacarmāvṛtasarvagātram /
samudgirantaṃ praṇavaṃ bṛhantaṃ
sahastrasūryapratimaṃ dadarśa //
1.24.d:
परश्वधासक्तकरं त्रिनेत्रं
नृसिंहचर्मावृतसर्वगात्रम् ।
समुद्गिरन्तं प्रणवं बृहन्तं
सहस्त्रसूर्यप्रतिमं ददर्श ॥
1.24.m: his hand resting on an axe, three-eyed, / his entire body covered in the skin of a man-lion, / uttering the great sacred syllable Oṃ, / resembling a thousand suns—[thus] he beheld him;

1.24.s:
prabhuṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣaṃ purastāt
sanātanaṃ yoginamīśitāram /
aṇoraṇīyāṃsamanantaśaktiṃ
prāṇeśvaraṃ śaṃbhumasau dadarśa //
1.24.d:
प्रभुं पुराणं पुरुषं पुरस्तात्
सनातनं योगिनमीशितारम् ।
अणोरणीयांसमनन्तशक्तिं
प्राणेश्वरं शंभुमसौ ददर्श ॥
1.24.m: the master, the ancient Person before him, / the eternal yogin, the ruler, / subtler than the subtle, of infinite power, / the Lord of breath, Śambhu—[thus] he beheld him;

1.24.s:
na yasya devā na pitāmaho 'pi
nendro na cāgnirvaruṇo na mṛtyuḥ /
prabhāvamadyāpi vadanti rudraṃ
tamādidevaṃ purato dadarśa //
1.24.d:
न यस्य देवा न पितामहो ऽपि
नेन्द्रो न चाग्निर्वरुणो न मृत्युः ।
प्रभावमद्यापि वदन्ति रुद्रं
तमादिदेवं पुरतो ददर्श ॥
1.24.m: whose power not even the gods, nor the Grandfather, / nor Indra, nor Agni, Varuṇa, nor Death / can describe even today—that primeval god, Rudra, / he beheld before him.

1.24.s:
tadānvapaśyad giriśasya vāme
svātmānamavyaktamanantarūpam /
stuvantamīśaṃ bahubhirvacobhiḥ
śaṅkhāsicakrārpitahastamādyam //
1.24.d:
तदान्वपश्यद् गिरिशस्य वामे
स्वात्मानमव्यक्तमनन्तरूपम् ।
स्तुवन्तमीशं बहुभिर्वचोभिः
शङ्खासिचक्रार्पितहस्तमाद्यम् ॥
1.24.m: Then he saw on the left of the Mountain Dweller / his own self, unmanifest, of endless forms, / praising the Lord with many words, / the primeval one whose hands bore the conch, sword, and discus.

1.24.s:
kṛtāñjaliṃ dakṣiṇataḥ sureśaṃ
haṃsādhirūḍhaṃ puruṣaṃ dadarśa /
stuvānamīśasya paraṃ prabhāvaṃ
pitāmahaṃ lokaguruṃ divastham //
1.24.d:
कृताञ्जलिं दक्षिणतः सुरेशं
हंसाधिरूढं पुरुषं ददर्श ।
स्तुवानमीशस्य परं प्रभावं
पितामहं लोकगुरुं दिवस्थम् ॥
1.24.m: On the right he saw the Lord of the gods, his hands joined in reverence, / the Person mounted upon a goose, / standing in heaven, praising the supreme majesty of the Lord— / the Grandfather, the teacher of the world.

1.24.s:
gaṇeśvarānarkasahastrakalpān
nandīśvarādīnamitaprabhāvān /
trilokabhartuḥ purato 'nvapaśyat
kumāramagnipatimaṃ saśākham //
1.24.d:
गणेश्वरानर्कसहस्त्रकल्पान्
नन्दीश्वरादीनमितप्रभावान् ।
त्रिलोकभर्तुः पुरतो ऽन्वपश्यत्
कुमारमग्निपतिमं सशाखम् ॥
1.24.m: The lords of the troops, resembling a thousand suns, / Nandīśvara and others of boundless majesty, / he saw before the sustainer of the three worlds, / as well as Kumāra, resembling fire, with Śākha.

1.24.s:
marīcimatriṃ pulahaṃ pulastyaṃ
pracetasaṃ dakṣamathāpi kaṇvam /
parāśaraṃ tatparato vasiṣṭhaṃ
svāyaṃbhuvaṃ cāpi manuṃ dadarśa //
1.24.d:
मरीचिमत्रिं पुलहं पुलस्त्यं
प्रचेतसं दक्षमथापि कण्वम् ।
पराशरं तत्परतो वसिष्ठं
स्वायंभुवं चापि मनुं ददर्श ॥
1.24.m: He saw Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, / Pracetas, Dakṣa, and also Kaṇva, / Parāśara, and beyond him Vasiṣṭha, / and Svāyambhuva Manu.

1.24.s:
tuṣṭāva mantrairamarapradhānaṃ
baddhāñjalirviṣṇurudārabuddhiḥ /
praṇamya devyā giriśaṃ sabhaktyā
svātmanyathātmānamasau vicintya //
1.24.d:
तुष्टाव मन्त्रैरमरप्रधानं
बद्धाञ्जलिर्विष्णुरुदारबुद्धिः ।
प्रणम्य देव्या गिरिशं सभक्त्या
स्वात्मन्यथात्मानमसौ विचिन्त्य ॥
1.24.m: The noble-minded Viṣṇu praised the foremost of the immortals with mantras, / with hands joined in reverence, / having bowed with devotion to the Mountain Dweller with the Goddess, / and contemplating that Self within his own self:

1.24.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca
namo 'stu te śāśvata sarvayone
brahmādhipaṃ tvāmṛṣayo vadanti /
tapaśca sattvaṃ ca rajastamaśca
tvāmeva sarva pravadanti santaḥ //
1.24.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच
नमो ऽस्तु ते शाश्वत सर्वयोने
ब्रह्माधिपं त्वामृषयो वदन्ति ।
तपश्च सत्त्वं च रजस्तमश्च
त्वामेव सर्व प्रवदन्ति सन्तः ॥
1.24.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / “Salutation to you, eternal one, womb of all! / The sages declare you to be the ruler of Brahman. / You are austerity, goodness, passion, and darkness; / the virtuous declare that you are indeed everything.

1.24.s:
tvaṃ brahmā hariratha viśvayoniragniḥ
saṃhartā dinakaramaṇḍalādhivāsaḥ /
prāṇastvaṃ hutavahavāsavādibheda-
satvāmekaṃ śaraṇamupaimi devamīśam //
1.24.d:
त्वं ब्रह्मा हरिरथ विश्वयोनिरग्निः
संहर्ता दिनकरमण्डलाधिवासः ।
प्राणस्त्वं हुतवहवासवादिभेद-
सत्वामेकं शरणमुपैमि देवमीशम् ॥
1.24.m: You are Brahmā, Hari, the source of the universe, and Agni; / you are the destroyer, whose dwelling is the disc of the sun; / you are breath, divided as the fire, Indra, and the rest; / to you, the one God and Lord, I resort for refuge.

1.24.s:
sāṃkhyāstvāṃ viguṇamathāhurekarūpaṃ
yogāstvāṃ satatamupāsate hṛdistham /
vedāstvāmabhidadhatīha rudramagniṃ
tvāmekaṃ śaraṇamupaimi devamīśam //
1.24.d:
सांख्यास्त्वां विगुणमथाहुरेकरूपं
योगास्त्वां सततमुपासते हृदिस्थम् ।
वेदास्त्वामभिदधतीह रुद्रमग्निं
त्वामेकं शरणमुपैमि देवमीशम् ॥
1.24.m: The Sāṃkhyas declare you to be devoid of qualities and of a single form; / yogins perpetually worship you residing within the heart; / the Vedas declare you to be Rudra and fire here; / to you, the one God and Lord, I resort for refuge.

1.24.s:
tvātpāde kusumamathāpi patramekaṃ
dattvāsau bhavati vimuktaviśvabandhaḥ /
sarvāghaṃ praṇudati siddhayogijuṣṭaṃ
smṛtvā te padayugalaṃ bhavatprasādāt //
1.24.d:
त्वात्पादे कुसुममथापि पत्रमेकं
दत्त्वासौ भवति विमुक्तविश्वबन्धः ।
सर्वाघं प्रणुदति सिद्धयोगिजुष्टं
स्मृत्वा ते पदयुगलं भवत्प्रसादात् ॥
1.24.m: By offering a single flower or even a leaf at your feet, / a person becomes freed from all bonds; / remembering your pair of feet attended by perfected yogins, / he casts off every sin through your grace.

1.24.s:
yasyāśeṣavibhāgahīnamamalaṃ hṛdyantarāvasthitaṃ
tattvaṃ jyotiranantamekamacalaṃ satyaṃ paraṃ sarvagam /
sthānaṃ prāhuranādimadhyanidhanaṃ yasmādidaṃ jāyate
nityaṃ tvāmahamupaimi satyavibhavaṃviśveśvarantaṃśivam //
1.24.d:
यस्याशेषविभागहीनममलं हृद्यन्तरावस्थितं
तत्त्वं ज्योतिरनन्तमेकमचलं सत्यं परं सर्वगम् ।
स्थानं प्राहुरनादिमध्यनिधनं यस्मादिदं जायते
नित्यं त्वामहमुपैमि सत्यविभवंविश्वेश्वरन्तंशिवम् ॥
1.24.m: Whose pure reality, devoid of all divisions, residing within the heart, / the teachers declare to be the eternal, unmoving, supreme, all-pervading, boundless light, / the truth, the station without beginning, middle, or end, from which this [world] arises— / to you, that Śiva, the eternal Lord of all, whose power is real, I continually resort.”

1.24.s:
oṃ namo nīlakaṇṭhāya trinetrāya ca raṃhase /
mahādevāya te nityamīśānāya namo namaḥ //
1.24.d:
ओं नमो नीलकण्ठाय त्रिनेत्राय च रंहसे ।
महादेवाय ते नित्यमीशानाय नमो नमः ॥
1.24.m: Om. Homage to the blue-throated one, to the three-eyed one, and to the swift one! / Homage, homage to you, Mahādeva, the eternal sovereign lord!

1.24.s:
namaḥ pinākine tubhyaṃ namo muṇḍāya daṇḍine /
namaste vajrahastāya digvastrāya kapardine //
1.24.d:
नमः पिनाकिने तुभ्यं नमो मुण्डाय दण्डिने ।
नमस्ते वज्रहस्ताय दिग्वस्त्राय कपर्दिने ॥
1.24.m: Homage to you who bear the Pināka, homage to the shaven-headed, to the staff-bearer! / Homage to you whose hand holds a thunderbolt, whose garment is space, and who wear matted hair!

1.24.s:
namo bhairavanādāya kālarūpāya daṃṣṭriṇe /
nāgayajñopavītāya namaste vahniretase //
1.24.d:
नमो भैरवनादाय कालरूपाय दंष्ट्रिणे ।
नागयज्ञोपवीताय नमस्ते वह्निरेतसे ॥
1.24.m: Homage to the one of terrifying roar, to the form of time, to the fanged one! / Homage to you whose sacred thread is a serpent, whose seed is fire!

1.24.s:
namo 'stu te girīśāya svāhākārāya te namaḥ /
namo muktāṭṭahāsāya bhīmāya ca namo namaḥ //
1.24.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते गिरीशाय स्वाहाकाराय ते नमः ।
नमो मुक्ताट्टहासाय भीमाय च नमो नमः ॥
1.24.m: Homage be to you, Lord of the Mountains, homage to you who are the Svāhā-call! / Homage to the one whose loud laughter is unleashed, and homage, homage to the terrible one!

1.24.s:
namaste kāmanāśāya namaḥ kālapramāthine /
namo bhairavaveṣāya harāya ca niṣaṅgiṇe //
1.24.d:
नमस्ते कामनाशाय नमः कालप्रमाथिने ।
नमो भैरववेषाय हराय च निषङ्गिणे ॥
1.24.m: Homage to you, destroyer of Kāma, homage to the crusher of death! / Homage to the one of terrifying guise, to Hara, and to the bearer of quivers!

1.24.s:
namo 'stu te tryambakāya namaste kṛttivāsase /
namo 'mbikādhipataye paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ //
1.24.d:
नमो ऽस्तु ते त्र्यम्बकाय नमस्ते कृत्तिवाससे ।
नमो ऽम्बिकाधिपतये पशूनां पतये नमः ॥
1.24.m: Homage be to you, Tryambaka, homage to you who are clad in animal skin! / Homage to the lord of Ambikā, homage to the lord of beasts!

1.24.s:
namaste vyomarūpāya vyomādhipataye namaḥ /
naranārīśarīrāya sāṃkhyayogapravartine //
1.24.d:
नमस्ते व्योमरूपाय व्योमाधिपतये नमः ।
नरनारीशरीराय सांख्ययोगप्रवर्तिने ॥
1.24.m: Homage to you whose form is space, homage to the lord of space, / to the one whose body is man and woman, to the promoter of Sāṅkhya and Yoga!

1.24.s:
namo daivatanāthāya devānugataliṅgine /
kumāragurave tubhyaṃ devadevāya te namaḥ //
1.24.d:
नमो दैवतनाथाय देवानुगतलिङ्गिने ।
कुमारगुरवे तुभ्यं देवदेवाय ते नमः ॥
1.24.m: Homage to the lord of deities, to the one whose emblem is attended by the gods, / to you the teacher of Kumāra, homage to you the God of gods!

1.24.s:
tamo yajñādhipataye namaste brahmacāriṇe /
mṛgavyādhāya mahate brahmādhipataye namaḥ //
1.24.d:
तमो यज्ञाधिपतये नमस्ते ब्रह्मचारिणे ।
मृगव्याधाय महते ब्रह्माधिपतये नमः ॥
1.24.m: Homage to the lord of sacrifice, homage to you who practice celibacy! / Homage to the great deer-hunter, to the lord of Brahman!

1.24.s:
namo haṃsāya viśvāya mohanāya namo namaḥ /
yogine yogagamyāya yogamāyāya te namaḥ //
1.24.d:
नमो हंसाय विश्वाय मोहनाय नमो नमः ।
योगिने योगगम्याय योगमायाय ते नमः ॥
1.24.m: Homage to the Swan, to the All, homage, homage to the bewitcher! / Homage to you, the yogin, accessible through yoga, the yoga-illusion!

1.24.s:
namaste prāṇapālāya ghaṇṭānādapriyāya ca /
kapāline namastubhyaṃ jyotiṣāṃ pataye namaḥ //
1.24.d:
नमस्ते प्राणपालाय घण्टानादप्रियाय च ।
कपालिने नमस्तुभ्यं ज्योतिषां पतये नमः ॥
1.24.m: Homage to you, protector of the vital breath, and lover of the ringing bell! / Homage to you, the skull-bearer, homage to the lord of lights!

1.24.s:
namo namo namastubhyaṃ bhūya eva namo namaḥ /
mahyaṃ sarvātmanā kāmān prayaccha parameśvara //
1.24.d:
नमो नमो नमस्तुभ्यं भूय एव नमो नमः ।
मह्यं सर्वात्मना कामान् प्रयच्छ परमेश्वर ॥
1.24.m: Homage, homage, homage to you, again and yet again homage, homage! / Bestow desires upon me with all your soul, O supreme lord!

1.24.s:
evaṃ hi bhaktyā deveśamabhiṣṭūya sa mādhavaḥ /
papāta pādayorviprā devadevyoḥ sa daṇḍavat //
1.24.d:
एवं हि भक्त्या देवेशमभिष्टूय स माधवः ।
पपात पादयोर्विप्रा देवदेव्योः स दण्डवत् ॥
1.24.m: Having thus praised the Lord of gods with devotion, that Mādhava / fell prostrate like a staff at the feet of the God and Goddess, O brahmins.

1.24.s:
utthāpya bhagavān somaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ keśiniṣūdanam /
babhāṣe madhuraṃ vākyaṃ meghagambhīraniḥ svanaḥ //
1.24.d:
उत्थाप्य भगवान् सोमः कृष्णं केशिनिषूदनम् ।
बभाषे मधुरं वाक्यं मेघगम्भीरनिः स्वनः ॥
1.24.m: Raising up Kṛṣṇa, the slayer of Keśin, the blessed lord with Umā, / with a voice deep as a thundercloud, spoke sweet words:

1.24.s:
kimarthaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa tapastaptaṃ tvayāvyaya /
tvameva dātā sarveṣāṃ kāmānāṃ kāmināmiha //
1.24.d:
किमर्थं पुण्डरीकाक्ष तपस्तप्तं त्वयाव्यय ।
त्वमेव दाता सर्वेषां कामानां कामिनामिह ॥
1.24.m: "For what purpose, O lotus-eyed one, has austerity been performed by you, the imperishable? / You alone here are the giver of all desires to those who have desires.

1.24.s:
tvaṃ hi sā paramā mūrtirmama nārāyaṇāhvayā /
nānavāptaṃ tvayā tāta vidyate puruṣottama //
1.24.d:
त्वं हि सा परमा मूर्तिर्मम नारायणाह्वया ।
नानवाप्तं त्वया तात विद्यते पुरुषोत्तम ॥
1.24.m: For you are that supreme manifestation of mine named Nārāyaṇa; / there is nothing unattained by you, dear one, O Supreme Spirit.

1.24.s:
vettha nārāyaṇānantamātmānaṃ parameśvaram /
mahādevaṃ mahāyogaṃ svena yogena keśava //
1.24.d:
वेत्थ नारायणानन्तमात्मानं परमेश्वरम् ।
महादेवं महायोगं स्वेन योगेन केशव ॥
1.24.m: You know Nārāyaṇa, the endless Self, the supreme lord, / Mahādeva, the great yoga, through your own yoga, O Keśava."

1.24.s:
śrutvā tadvacanaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ prahasan vai vṛṣadhvajam /
uvāca vīkṣya viśveśaṃ devīṃ ca himaśailajām //
1.24.d:
श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं कृष्णः प्रहसन् वै वृषध्वजम् ।
उवाच वीक्ष्य विश्वेशं देवीं च हिमशैलजाम् ॥
1.24.m: Hearing those words, Kṛṣṇa, laughing, looking upon the bull-bannered / Lord of the Universe and the goddess born of the mountain of snow, said:

1.24.s:
jñātaṃ hi bhavatā sarvaṃ svena yogena śaṅkara /
icchāmyātmasamaṃ putraṃ tvadbhaktaṃ dehi śaṅkara //
1.24.d:
ज्ञातं हि भवता सर्वं स्वेन योगेन शङ्कर ।
इच्छाम्यात्मसमं पुत्रं त्वद्भक्तं देहि शङ्कर ॥
1.24.m: "Indeed, everything is known by you through your own yoga, O Śaṅkara. / I desire a son equal to myself, devoted to you; grant him, O Śaṅkara!"

1.24.s:
tathāstvityāha viśvātmā prahṛṣṭamanasā haraḥ /
devīmālokya girijāṃ keśavaṃ pariṣasvaje //
1.24.d:
तथास्त्वित्याह विश्वात्मा प्रहृष्टमनसा हरः ।
देवीमालोक्य गिरिजां केशवं परिषस्वजे ॥
1.24.m: "So be it," said Hara, the soul of the universe, with a delighted mind. / Looking at the goddess, daughter of the mountain, he embraced Keśava.

1.24.s:
tataḥ sā jagatāṃ mātā śaṅkarārdhaśarīriṇī /
vyājahāra hṛṣīkeśaṃ devī himagirīndrajā //
1.24.d:
ततः सा जगतां माता शङ्करार्धशरीरिणी ।
व्याजहार हृषीकेशं देवी हिमगिरीन्द्रजा ॥
1.24.m: Then she, the mother of the worlds, whose body forms half of Śaṅkara, / the goddess born of the king of snowy mountains, spoke to Hṛṣīkeśa:

1.24.s:
vatsa jāne tavānantāṃ niścalāṃ sarvadācyuta /
ananyāmīśvare bhaktimātmanyapi ca keśava //
1.24.d:
वत्स जाने तवानन्तां निश्चलां सर्वदाच्युत ।
अनन्यामीश्वरे भक्तिमात्मन्यपि च केशव ॥
1.24.m: "Child, I know your endless, unwavering devotion at all times, O Acyuta, / undivided toward the Lord and also toward yourself, O Keśava.

1.24.s:
tvaṃ hi nārāyaṇaḥ sākṣāt sarvātmā puruṣottamaḥ /
prārthito daivataiḥ pūrvaṃ saṃjāto daivakīsutaḥ //
1.24.d:
त्वं हि नारायणः साक्षात् सर्वात्मा पुरुषोत्तमः ।
प्रार्थितो दैवतैः पूर्वं संजातो दैवकीसुतः ॥
1.24.m: For you are Nārāyaṇa manifest, the Soul of all, the Supreme Spirit, / formerly petitioned by the deities, born as the son of Devakī.

1.24.s:
paśya tvamātmanātmānamātmīyamamalaṃ padam /
nāvayorvidyate bheda evaṃ paśyanti sūrayaḥ //
1.24.d:
पश्य त्वमात्मनात्मानमात्मीयममलं पदम् ।
नावयोर्विद्यते भेद एवं पश्यन्ति सूरयः ॥
1.24.m: See yourself by yourself, your own stainless abode; / between the two of us no difference exists—thus the wise perceive.

1.24.s:
imānimān varāniṣṭān matto gṛhṇīṣva keśava /
sarvajñatvaṃ tathaiśvaryaṃ jñānaṃ tat pārameśvaram /
īśvare niścalāṃ bhaktimātmanyapi paraṃ balam //
1.24.d:
इमानिमान् वरानिष्टान् मत्तो गृह्णीष्व केशव ।
सर्वज्ञत्वं तथैश्वर्यं ज्ञानं तत् पारमेश्वरम् ।
ईश्वरे निश्चलां भक्तिमात्मन्यपि परं बलम् ॥
1.24.m: Receive from me these desired boons, O Keśava: / omniscience, likewise sovereignty, that knowledge belonging to the supreme lord, / unwavering devotion toward the Lord, and supreme power in yourself as well."

1.24.s:
evamuktastayā kṛṣṇo mahādevyā janārdanaḥ /
āśiṣaṃ śirasāhṛṅṇād devo 'pyāha maheśvaraḥ //
1.24.d:
एवमुक्तस्तया कृष्णो महादेव्या जनार्दनः ।
आशिषं शिरसाहृङ्णाद् देवो ऽप्याह महेश्वरः ॥
1.24.m: Addressed thus by that Great Goddess, Kṛṣṇa Janārdana / accepted the blessing with his head, and the divine Maheśvara also spoke.

1.24.s:
pragṛhya kṛṣṇaṃ bhagavānatheśaḥ
kareṇa devyā saha devadevaḥ /
saṃpūjyamāno munibhiḥ sureśai-
r jagāma kailāsagiriṃ girīśaḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapūrāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge caturviśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.24.d:
प्रगृह्य कृष्णं भगवानथेशः
करेण देव्या सह देवदेवः ।
संपूज्यमानो मुनिभिः सुरेशै-
र् जगाम कैलासगिरिं गिरीशः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपूराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे चतुर्विशो ऽध्यायः
1.24.m:
Taking Kṛṣṇa by the hand along with the goddess, / the blessed Lord, the God of gods, / worshipped by sages and chiefs of gods, / the Lord of the Mountains departed for Mount Kailāsa.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the auspicious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.25.s:
sūta uvāca
praviśya meruśikharaṃ kailāsaṃ kanakaprabham /
rarāma bhagavān somaḥ keśavena maheśvaraḥ //
1.25.d:
सूत उवाच
प्रविश्य मेरुशिखरं कैलासं कनकप्रभम् ।
रराम भगवान् सोमः केशवेन महेश्वरः ॥
1.25.m: Sūta said: / Having entered Kailāsa, a peak of Meru shining like gold, / the blessed Lord with Umā, Maheśvara, disported with Keśava.

1.25.s:
apaśyaṃstaṃ mahātmānaṃ kailāsagirivāsinaḥ /
pūjayāñcakrire kṛṣṇaṃ devadevamathācyutam //
1.25.d:
अपश्यंस्तं महात्मानं कैलासगिरिवासिनः ।
पूजयाञ्चक्रिरे कृष्णं देवदेवमथाच्युतम् ॥
1.25.m: The inhabitants of Mount Kailāsa saw that great-souled one; / they worshipped Kṛṣṇa, the God of gods, Acyuta:

1.25.s:
caturbāhumudārāṅgaṃ kālameghasamaprabham /
kirīṭinaṃ śārṅgapāṇi śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam //
1.25.d:
चतुर्बाहुमुदाराङ्गं कालमेघसमप्रभम् ।
किरीटिनं शार्ङ्गपाणि श्रीवत्साङ्कितवक्षसम् ॥
1.25.m: four-armed, noble-limbed, shining like a dark cloud, / diademed, holding the Śārṅga bow in hand, his chest marked with the Śrīvatsa,

1.25.s:
dīrghabāhuṃ viśālākṣaṃ pītavāsasamacyutam /
dadhānamurasā mālāṃ vaijayantīmanuttamām //
1.25.d:
दीर्घबाहुं विशालाक्षं पीतवाससमच्युतम् ।
दधानमुरसा मालां वैजयन्तीमनुत्तमाम् ॥
1.25.m: long-armed, wide-eyed, clad in yellow garments, Acyuta, / wearing upon his chest the supreme Vaijayantī garland,

1.25.s:
bhrājamānaṃ śriyā divyaṃ yuvānamatikomalam /
padmāṅghrinayanaṃ cāru susmitaṃ sugatipradam //
1.25.d:
भ्राजमानं श्रिया दिव्यं युवानमतिकोमलम् ।
पद्माङ्घ्रिनयनं चारु सुस्मितं सुगतिप्रदम् ॥
1.25.m: radiant with splendor, divine, youthful, exceedingly tender, / with lotus-like feet and eyes, handsome, smiling sweetly, granting the good path.

1.25.s:
kadācit tatra līlārthaṃ devakīnandavardhanaḥ /
bhrājamānaḥ śrīyā kṛṣṇaścacāra girikandare //
1.25.d:
कदाचित् तत्र लीलार्थं देवकीनन्दवर्धनः ।
भ्राजमानः श्रीया कृष्णश्चचार गिरिकन्दरे ॥
1.25.m: Once, for the sake of play, Kṛṣṇa, who increases the joy of Devakī, / shining with splendor, wandered in a mountain cave.

1.25.s:
gandharvāpsarasāṃ mukhyā nāgakanyāśca kṛtsnaśaḥ /
siddhā yakṣāśca gandharvāstatra tatra jaganmayam //
1.25.d:
गन्धर्वाप्सरसां मुख्या नागकन्याश्च कृत्स्नशः ।
सिद्धा यक्षाश्च गन्धर्वास्तत्र तत्र जगन्मयम् ॥
1.25.m: The foremost of Gandharvas and Apsarases, and all the Nāga maidens, / the Siddhas, Yakṣas, and Gandharvas, everywhere seeing him whose essence is the world,

1.25.s:
dṛṣṭvāścaryaṃ paraṃ gatvā harṣādutphullocanāḥ /
mumucuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi tasya mūrdhni mahātmanaḥ //
1.25.d:
दृष्ट्वाश्चर्यं परं गत्वा हर्षादुत्फुल्लोचनाः ।
मुमुचुः पुष्पवर्षाणि तस्य मूर्ध्नि महात्मनः ॥
1.25.m: went into supreme wonder, their eyes blossoming with joy, / and showered down rains of flowers on the head of that great-souled one.

1.25.s:
gandharvakanyakā divyāstadvadapsarasāṃ varāḥ /
dṛṣṭvā cakamire kṛṣṇaṃ strastavastravibhūṣaṇāḥ //
1.25.d:
गन्धर्वकन्यका दिव्यास्तद्वदप्सरसां वराः ।
दृष्ट्वा चकमिरे कृष्णं स्त्रस्तवस्त्रविभूषणाः ॥
1.25.m: Divine Gandharva maidens, and likewise the best among Apsarases, / seeing Kṛṣṇa, desired him, their garments and ornaments slipping off.

1.25.s:
kāścid gāyanti vividhāṃ gītiṃ gītaviśāradāḥ /
saṃprekṣya devakīsūnuṃ sundaryaḥ kāmamohitāḥ //
1.25.d:
काश्चिद् गायन्ति विविधां गीतिं गीतविशारदाः ।
संप्रेक्ष्य देवकीसूनुं सुन्दर्यः काममोहिताः ॥
1.25.m: Some, skilled in music, sang various songs, / the beautiful women bewildered by love upon beholding the son of Devakī.

1.25.s:
kāścidvilāsabahulā nṛtyanti sma tadagrataḥ /
saṃprekṣya saṃsthitāḥ kāścit papustadvadanāmṛtam //
1.25.d:
काश्चिद्विलासबहुला नृत्यन्ति स्म तदग्रतः ।
संप्रेक्ष्य संस्थिताः काश्चित् पपुस्तद्वदनामृतम् ॥
1.25.m: Some, full of coquetry, danced before him; / others stood gazing and drank the nectar of his face.

1.25.s:
kāścid bhūṣaṇavaryāṇi svāṅgādādāya sādaram /
bhūṣayāñcakrire kṛṣṇaṃ kāminyo lokabhūṣaṇam //
1.25.d:
काश्चिद् भूषणवर्याणि स्वाङ्गादादाय सादरम् ।
भूषयाञ्चक्रिरे कृष्णं कामिन्यो लोकभूषणम् ॥
1.25.m: Taking the finest ornaments from their own bodies, some women in love / respectfully adorned Kṛṣṇa, the ornament of the worlds.

1.25.s:
kāścid bhūṣaṇavaryāṇi samādāya tadaṅgataḥ /
svātmānaṃ būṣayāmāsuḥ svātmagairapi mādhavam //
1.25.d:
काश्चिद् भूषणवर्याणि समादाय तदङ्गतः ।
स्वात्मानं बूषयामासुः स्वात्मगैरपि माधवम् ॥
1.25.m: Some, taking the finest ornaments from his limbs, / adorned themselves, and with ornaments from their own bodies [they adorned] Mādhava.

1.25.s:
kāścidāgatya kṛṣṇasya samīpaṃ kāmamohitāḥ /
cucumburvadanāmbhojaṃ harermugdhamṛgekṣaṇāḥ //
1.25.d:
काश्चिदागत्य कृष्णस्य समीपं काममोहिताः ।
चुचुम्बुर्वदनाम्भोजं हरेर्मुग्धमृगेक्षणाः ॥
1.25.m: Some, bewildered by desire, approached Kṛṣṇa / and kissed the lotus face of Hari, their eyes like bewildered deer.

1.25.s:
pragṛhya kāścid govindaṃ kareṇa bhavanaṃ svakam /
prāpayāmāsurlokādiṃ māyayā tasya mohitāḥ //
1.25.d:
प्रगृह्य काश्चिद् गोविन्दं करेण भवनं स्वकम् ।
प्रापयामासुर्लोकादिं मायया तस्य मोहिताः ॥
1.25.m: Taking Govinda by the hand, some led him to their own home, / bewildered by his illusory creative power, though he is the source of the worlds.

1.25.s:
tāsāṃ sa bhagavān kṛṣṇaḥ kāmān kamalalocanaḥ /
bahūni kṛtvā rūpāṇi pūrayāmāsa līlayā //
1.25.d:
तासां स भगवान् कृष्णः कामान् कमललोचनः ।
बहूनि कृत्वा रूपाणि पूरयामास लीलया ॥
1.25.m: Assuming many forms in play, the blessed Kṛṣṇa, / lotus-eyed, fulfilled their desires.

1.25.s:
evaṃ vai suciraṃ kālaṃ devadevapure hariḥ /
reme nārāyaṇaḥ śrīmān māyayā mohayañjagat //
1.25.d:
एवं वै सुचिरं कालं देवदेवपुरे हरिः ।
रेमे नारायणः श्रीमान् मायया मोहयञ्जगत् ॥
1.25.m: Thus for a very long time in the city of the God of gods Hari, / the glorious Nārāyaṇa, took delight, bewitching the world through his illusory creative power.

1.25.s:
gate bahutithe kāle dvāravatyāṃ nivāsinaḥ /
babhūvurvihvalā bhītā govindavirahe janāḥ //
1.25.d:
गते बहुतिथे काले द्वारवत्यां निवासिनः ।
बभूवुर्विह्वला भीता गोविन्दविरहे जनाः ॥
1.25.m: When a long time had passed, the inhabitants dwelling in Dvāravatī / became distressed and frightened in separation from Govinda.

1.25.s:
tataḥ suparṇo balavān pūrvameva visajitaḥ /
kṛṣṇena mārgamāṇastaṃ himavantaṃ yayau girim //
1.25.d:
ततः सुपर्णो बलवान् पूर्वमेव विसजितः ।
कृष्णेन मार्गमाणस्तं हिमवन्तं ययौ गिरिम् ॥
1.25.m: Then the powerful Suparṇa, who had been dispatched earlier / by Kṛṣṇa, searching for him, went to the Himavant mountain.

1.25.s:
adṛṣṭvā tatra govindaṃ praṇamya śirasā munim /
ājagāmopamanyuṃ taṃ purīṃ dvāravatīṃ punaḥ //
1.25.d:
अदृष्ट्वा तत्र गोविन्दं प्रणम्य शिरसा मुनिम् ।
आजगामोपमन्युं तं पुरीं द्वारवतीं पुनः ॥
1.25.m: Not seeing Govinda there, he bowed his head before that sage, / Upamanyu, and returned again to the city of Dvāravatī.

1.25.s:
tadantare mahādaityā rākṣasāścātibhīṣaṇāḥ /
ājagmurdvārakāṃ śubhrāṃ bhīṣayantaḥ sahastraśaḥ //
1.25.d:
तदन्तरे महादैत्या राक्षसाश्चातिभीषणाः ।
आजग्मुर्द्वारकां शुभ्रां भीषयन्तः सहस्त्रशः ॥
1.25.m: In the meantime, great Daityas and terrifying Rākṣasas / came by the thousands to radiant Dvārakā, spreading terror.

1.25.s:
sa tān suparṇo balavān kṛṣṇatulyaparākramaḥ /
hatvā yuddhena mahatā rakṣati sma purīṃ śubhām //
1.25.d:
स तान् सुपर्णो बलवान् कृष्णतुल्यपराक्रमः ।
हत्वा युद्धेन महता रक्षति स्म पुरीं शुभाम् ॥
1.25.m: That mighty Suparṇa, equal in prowess to Kṛṣṇa, / slew them in a great battle and protected the fair city.

1.25.s:
etasminneva kāle tu nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ /
dṛṣṭvā kailāsaśikhare kṛṣṇaṃ dvāravatīṃ gataḥ //
1.25.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु नारदो भगवानृषिः ।
दृष्ट्वा कैलासशिखरे कृष्णं द्वारवतीं गतः ॥
1.25.m: At that very time, the lordly sage Nārada, / having seen Kṛṣṇa upon the peak of Mount Kailāsa, went to Dvāravatī.

1.25.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā nāradamṛṣiṃ sarve tatra nivāsinaḥ /
procurnārāyaṇo nāthaḥ kutrāste bhagavān hariḥ //
1.25.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा नारदमृषिं सर्वे तत्र निवासिनः ।
प्रोचुर्नारायणो नाथः कुत्रास्ते भगवान् हरिः ॥
1.25.m: Seeing that sage Nārada, all the inhabitants there / said: “Where does our lord, the blessed Hari Nārāyaṇa, dwell?”

1.25.s:
sa tānuvāca bhagavān kailasaśikhare hariḥ /
ramate 'dya mahāyogīṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvāhamihāgataḥ //
1.25.d:
स तानुवाच भगवान् कैलसशिखरे हरिः ।
रमते ऽद्य महायोगीं तं दृष्ट्वाहमिहागतः ॥
1.25.m: The venerable one said to them: “Upon the peak of Mount Kailāsa Hari / delights today, that great yogin; having seen him, I have come here.”

1.25.s:
tasyopaśrutya vacanaṃ suparṇaḥ patatāṃ varaḥ /
jagāmākāśago viprāḥ kailāsaṃ girimuttamam //
1.25.d:
तस्योपश्रुत्य वचनं सुपर्णः पततां वरः ।
जगामाकाशगो विप्राः कैलासं गिरिमुत्तमम् ॥
1.25.m: Hearing his words, Suparṇa, the best of winged creatures, / flying through the sky, O brāhmaṇas, went to Mount Kailāsa, the excellent mountain.

1.25.s:
dadarśa devakīsūnuṃ bhavane ratnamaṇḍite /
varāsanasthaṃ govindaṃ devadevāntike harim //
1.25.d:
ददर्श देवकीसूनुं भवने रत्नमण्डिते ।
वरासनस्थं गोविन्दं देवदेवान्तिके हरिम् ॥
1.25.m: He beheld Devakī's son in a jewel-adorned palace, / Govinda seated upon an excellent throne, Hari near the God of gods,

1.25.s:
upāsyamānamamarairdivyastrībhiḥ samantataḥ /
mahādevagaṇaiḥ siddhairyogibhiḥ parivāritam //
1.25.d:
उपास्यमानममरैर्दिव्यस्त्रीभिः समन्ततः ।
महादेवगणैः सिद्धैर्योगिभिः परिवारितम् ॥
1.25.m: worshiped on all sides by immortals and celestial maidens, / and surrounded by Mahādeva’s attendants, Siddhas, and yogins.

1.25.s:
praṇamya daṇḍavad bhūmau suparṇaḥ śaṅkaraṃ śivam /
nivedayāmāsa hareḥ pravṛttiṃ dvārake pure //
1.25.d:
प्रणम्य दण्डवद् भूमौ सुपर्णः शङ्करं शिवम् ।
निवेदयामास हरेः प्रवृत्तिं द्वारके पुरे ॥
1.25.m: Bowing like a staff upon the ground before Śaṅkara, Śiva, / Suparṇa reported the events in the city of Dvārakā to Hari.

1.25.s:
tataḥ praṇamya śirasā śaṅkaraṃ nīlalohitam /
ājagāma purīṃ kṛṣṇaḥ so 'nujñāto hareṇa tu //
1.25.d:
ततः प्रणम्य शिरसा शङ्करं नीललोहितम् ।
आजगाम पुरीं कृष्णः सो ऽनुज्ञातो हरेण तु ॥
1.25.m: Then, bowing his head to Śaṅkara Nīlalohita, / Kṛṣṇa departed for the city, permitted by Hara.

1.25.s:
āruhya kaśyapasutaṃ strīgaṇairabhipūjitaḥ /
vacobhiramṛtāsvādairmānito madhusūdanaḥ //
1.25.d:
आरुह्य कश्यपसुतं स्त्रीगणैरभिपूजितः ।
वचोभिरमृतास्वादैर्मानितो मधुसूदनः ॥
1.25.m: Mounting the son of Kaśyapa, honored by crowds of women, / Madhusūdana was revered with words sweet as nectar.

1.25.s:
vīkṣya yāntamamitraghnaṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ varāḥ /
anvagacchan mahoyogaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam //
1.25.d:
वीक्ष्य यान्तममित्रघ्नं गन्धर्वाप्सरसां वराः ।
अन्वगच्छन् महोयोगं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् ॥
1.25.m: Seeing that slayer of foes depart, the foremost Gandharvas and Apsarases / followed him of great yoga, bearer of the conch, discus, and mace.

1.25.s:
visarjayitvā viśvātmā sarvā evāṅganā hariḥ /
yayau sa tūrṇaṃ govindo divyāṃ dvāravatīṃ purīm //
1.25.d:
विसर्जयित्वा विश्वात्मा सर्वा एवाङ्गना हरिः ।
ययौ स तूर्णं गोविन्दो दिव्यां द्वारवतीं पुरीम् ॥
1.25.m: Having dismissed all the women, Hari, the Self of the universe, / Govinda swiftly went to the celestial city of Dvāravatī.

1.25.s:
gate muraripau naiva kāminyo munipuṅgavāḥ /
niśeva candrarahitā vinā tena cakāśire //
1.25.d:
गते मुररिपौ नैव कामिन्यो मुनिपुङ्गवाः ।
निशेव चन्द्ररहिता विना तेन चकाशिरे ॥
1.25.m: When the enemy of Mura had gone, the enamored women, O foremost sages, / did not shine at all without him, like a night deprived of the moon.

1.25.s:
śrutvā paurajanāstūrṇaṃ kṛṣṇāgamanamuttamam /
maṇḍayāñcakrire divyāṃ purīṃ dvāravatīṃ śubhām //
1.25.d:
श्रुत्वा पौरजनास्तूर्णं कृष्णागमनमुत्तमम् ।
मण्डयाञ्चक्रिरे दिव्यां पुरीं द्वारवतीं शुभाम् ॥
1.25.m: Quickly hearing of Kṛṣṇa’s auspicious arrival, the citizens / adorned the splendid, fair city of Dvāravatī.

1.25.s:
patākābhirviśālābhirdhvajai ratnapariṣkṛtaiḥ /
lājādibhiḥ purīṃ ramyāṃ bhūṣayāñcakrire tadā //
1.25.d:
पताकाभिर्विशालाभिर्ध्वजै रत्नपरिष्कृतैः ।
लाजादिभिः पुरीं रम्यां भूषयाञ्चक्रिरे तदा ॥
1.25.m: With broad pennants and banners adorned with gems, / and with parched grain and the like, they decorated the charming city then.

1.25.s:
avādayanta vividhān vāditrān madhurasvanān /
śaṅkhān sahastraśo dadhmurvoṇāvādān vitenire //
1.25.d:
अवादयन्त विविधान् वादित्रान् मधुरस्वनान् ।
शङ्खान् सहस्त्रशो दध्मुर्वोणावादान् वितेनिरे ॥
1.25.m: They sounded various sweet-toned instruments, / blew conches by the thousands, and played upon lutes.

1.25.s:
praviṣṭamātre govinde purīṃ dvāravatīṃ śubhām /
agāyan madhuraṃ gānaṃ striyo yauvanaśālinaḥ //
1.25.d:
प्रविष्टमात्रे गोविन्दे पुरीं द्वारवतीं शुभाम् ।
अगायन् मधुरं गानं स्त्रियो यौवनशालिनः ॥
1.25.m: As soon as Govinda entered the fair city of Dvāravatī, / women endowed with youth sang sweet songs.

1.25.s:
dṛṣṭvā nanṛturīśānaṃ sthitāḥ prāsādamūrdhasu /
mumucuḥ puṣpavarṣāṇi vasudevasutopari //
1.25.d:
दृष्ट्वा ननृतुरीशानं स्थिताः प्रासादमूर्धसु ।
मुमुचुः पुष्पवर्षाणि वसुदेवसुतोपरि ॥
1.25.m: Seeing the Lord, standing on the roofs of palaces, they danced, / and showered rains of flowers upon the son of Vasudeva.

1.25.s:
praviśya bhavanaṃ kṛṣṇa āśīrvādābhivardhitaḥ /
varāsane mahāyogī bhāti devībhiranvitaḥ //
1.25.d:
प्रविश्य भवनं कृष्ण आशीर्वादाभिवर्धितः ।
वरासने महायोगी भाति देवीभिरन्वितः ॥
1.25.m: Entering his palace, hailed with blessings, / the great yogin Kṛṣṇa shone on an excellent throne, accompanied by his queens,

1.25.s:
suramye maṇḍape śubhre śaṅkhādyaiḥ parivāritaḥ /
ātmajairabhito mukhyaiḥ strīsahastraiśca saṃvṛtaḥ //
1.25.d:
सुरम्ये मण्डपे शुभ्रे शङ्खाद्यैः परिवारितः ।
आत्मजैरभितो मुख्यैः स्त्रीसहस्त्रैश्च संवृतः ॥
1.25.m: in a very charming, bright pavilion, surrounded by Śaṅkha and others, / encircled on all sides by his foremost sons and by thousands of women.

1.25.s:
tatrāsanavare ramye jāmbavatyā sahācyutaḥ /
bhrājate mālayā devo yathā devyā samanvitaḥ //
1.25.d:
तत्रासनवरे रम्ये जाम्बवत्या सहाच्युतः ।
भ्राजते मालया देवो यथा देव्या समन्वितः ॥
1.25.m: There upon an excellent, charming throne, Acyuta with Jāmbavatī, / the god shone with his garland, as if accompanied by the Goddess.

1.25.s:
ājagmurdevagandharvā draṣṭuṃ lokādimavyayam /
maharṣayaḥ pūrvajātā mārkaṇḍeyādayo dvijāḥ //
1.25.d:
आजग्मुर्देवगन्धर्वा द्रष्टुं लोकादिमव्ययम् ।
महर्षयः पूर्वजाता मार्कण्डेयादयो द्विजाः ॥
1.25.m: Gods and Gandharvas came to see the imperishable source of the worlds, / as did primeval great sages, Mārkaṇḍeya and other twice-born ones.

1.25.s:
tataḥ sa bhagavān kṛṣṇo mārkaṇḍeyaṃ samāgatam /
nanāmotthāya śirasā svāsanaṃ ca dadau hariḥ //
1.25.d:
ततः स भगवान् कृष्णो मार्कण्डेयं समागतम् ।
ननामोत्थाय शिरसा स्वासनं च ददौ हरिः ॥
1.25.m: Then the blessed Kṛṣṇa, rising, bowed with his head / to Mārkaṇḍeya who had arrived, and Hari gave him his own seat.

1.25.s:
saṃpūjya tānṛṣigaṇān praṇāmena mahābhujaḥ /
visarjayāmāsa harirdattvā tadabhivāñchitān //
1.25.d:
संपूज्य तानृषिगणान् प्रणामेन महाभुजः ।
विसर्जयामास हरिर्दत्त्वा तदभिवाञ्छितान् ॥
1.25.m: Having honored those hosts of sages with salutations, the mighty-armed / Hari dismissed them after granting what they desired.

1.25.s:
tadā madhyāhnasamaye devadevaḥ svayaṃ hariḥ /
snātvā śuklāmbaro bhānumupatiṣṭhat kṛtāñjaliḥ //
1.25.d:
तदा मध्याह्नसमये देवदेवः स्वयं हरिः ।
स्नात्वा शुक्लाम्बरो भानुमुपतिष्ठत् कृताञ्जलिः ॥
1.25.m: Then, at midday, the God of gods, Hari himself, / bathed, donned white garments, and stood with folded hands before the sun.

1.25.s:
jajāpa jāpyaṃ vidhivat prekṣamāṇo divākaram /
tarpayāmāsa deveśo deveśo devān munigaṇān pitṝn //
1.25.d:
जजाप जाप्यं विधिवत् प्रेक्षमाणो दिवाकरम् ।
तर्पयामास देवेशो देवेशो देवान् मुनिगणान् पितॄन् ॥
1.25.m: Looking toward the sun, he muttered prayers according to rule; / the Lord of gods propitiated the gods, hosts of sages, and the ancestors.

1.25.s:
praviśya devabhavanaṃ mārkaṇḍeyena caiva hi /
pūjayāmāsa liṅgasthaṃ bhūteśaṃ bhūtibhūṣaṇam //
1.25.d:
प्रविश्य देवभवनं मार्कण्डेयेन चैव हि ।
पूजयामास लिङ्गस्थं भूतेशं भूतिभूषणम् ॥
1.25.m: Entering the temple of the god along with Mārkaṇḍeya, / he worshiped the Lord of beings, adorned with ashes, present in the liṅga.

1.25.s:
samāpya niyamaṃ sarvaṃ niyantāsau nṛṇāṃ svayam /
bhojayitvā munivaraṃ brāhmaṇānabhipūjya ca //
1.25.d:
समाप्य नियमं सर्वं नियन्तासौ नृणां स्वयम् ।
भोजयित्वा मुनिवरं ब्राह्मणानभिपूज्य च ॥
1.25.m: Having completed all observances, he, the controller of men himself, / fed the foremost sage and honored the brāhmaṇas.

1.25.s:
kṛtvātmayogaṃ viprendrā mārkaṇḍeyena cācyutaḥ /
kathāḥ paurāṇikīḥ puṇyāścakre putrādibhirvṛtaḥ //
1.25.d:
कृत्वात्मयोगं विप्रेन्द्रा मार्कण्डेयेन चाच्युतः ।
कथाः पौराणिकीः पुण्याश्चक्रे पुत्रादिभिर्वृतः ॥
1.25.m: Fixing himself in meditation, O foremost of brāhmaṇas, Acyuta / recounted sacred ancient tales with Mārkaṇḍeya, surrounded by his sons and others.

1.25.s:
athaitat sarvamakhilaṃ dṛṣṭvā karma mahāmuniḥ /
mārkaṇḍeyo hasan kṛṣṇaṃ babhāṣe madhuraṃ vacaḥ //
1.25.d:
अथैतत् सर्वमखिलं दृष्ट्वा कर्म महामुनिः ।
मार्कण्डेयो हसन् कृष्णं बभाषे मधुरं वचः ॥
1.25.m: Then, seeing all this entire rite, the great sage / Mārkaṇḍeya smiled and spoke sweet words to Kṛṣṇa:

1.25.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
kaḥ samārādhyate devo bhavatā karmabhiḥ śubhaiḥ /
brūhi tvaṃ karmabhiḥ pūjyo yogināṃ dhyeya eva ca //
1.25.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
कः समाराध्यते देवो भवता कर्मभिः शुभैः ।
ब्रूहि त्वं कर्मभिः पूज्यो योगिनां ध्येय एव च ॥
1.25.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / “Which god is worshiped by you through auspicious rites? / Speak! You are the one to be worshiped through rites, and the one to be meditated upon by yogins.

1.25.s:
tvaṃ hi tat paramaṃ brahma nirvāṇamamalaṃ padam /
bhārāvataraṇārthāya jāto vṛṣṇikule prabhuḥ //
1.25.d:
त्वं हि तत् परमं ब्रह्म निर्वाणममलं पदम् ।
भारावतरणार्थाय जातो वृष्णिकुले प्रभुः ॥
1.25.m: For you are that supreme Brahman, the stainless abode of nirvāṇa; / the Lord born in the Vṛṣṇi lineage to remove the earth's burden.”

1.25.s:
tamabravīnmahābāhuḥ kṛṣṇo brahmavidāṃ varaḥ /
śṛṇvatāmeva putrāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ prahasanniva //
1.25.d:
तमब्रवीन्महाबाहुः कृष्णो ब्रह्मविदां वरः ।
शृण्वतामेव पुत्राणां सर्वेषां प्रहसन्निव ॥
1.25.m: To him the mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, foremost of knowers of Brahman, / spoke, as if smiling, while all his sons were listening:

1.25.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
bhavatā kathitaṃ sarvaṃ tathyameva na saṃśayaḥ /
tathāpi devamīśānaṃ pūjayāmi sanātanam //
1.25.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
भवता कथितं सर्वं तथ्यमेव न संशयः ।
तथापि देवमीशानं पूजयामि सनातनम् ॥
1.25.m: The Blessed Lord said: / “Everything stated by you is true indeed, there is no doubt; / nevertheless, I worship the eternal god, the Lord.

1.25.s:
na me viprāsti kartavyaṃ nānavāptaṃ kathañcana /
pūjayāmi tathāpīśaṃ jānannaitat paraṃ śivam //
1.25.d:
न मे विप्रास्ति कर्तव्यं नानवाप्तं कथञ्चन ।
पूजयामि तथापीशं जानन्नैतत् परं शिवम् ॥
1.25.m: There is nothing for me to do, O brāhmaṇa, nor anything unobtained; / nonetheless I worship the Lord, knowing this supreme Śiva.

1.25.s:
na vai paśyanti taṃ devaṃ māyayā mohitā janāḥ /
tato 'haṃ svātmano mūlaṃ jñāpayan pūjayāmi tam //
1.25.d:
न वै पश्यन्ति तं देवं मायया मोहिता जनाः ।
ततो ऽहं स्वात्मनो मूलं ज्ञापयन् पूजयामि तम् ॥
1.25.m: People deluded by māyā do not truly see that god; / therefore, making known the origin of my own self, I worship him.

1.25.s:
na ca liṅgārcanāt puṇyaṃ lokesmin bhītināśanam /
tathā liṅge hitāyaiṣāṃ lokānāṃ pūjayecchivam //
1.25.d:
न च लिङ्गार्चनात् पुण्यं लोकेस्मिन् भीतिनाशनम् ।
तथा लिङ्गे हितायैषां लोकानां पूजयेच्छिवम् ॥
1.25.m: And in this world there is no merit higher than worship of the liṅga, destroying fear; / thus, for the welfare of these worlds, one should worship Śiva in the liṅga.

1.25.s:
yo 'haṃ talliṅgamityāhurvedavādavido janāḥ /
tato 'hamātmamīśānaṃ pūjayāmyātmanaiva tu //
1.25.d:
यो ऽहं तल्लिङ्गमित्याहुर्वेदवादविदो जनाः ।
ततो ऽहमात्ममीशानं पूजयाम्यात्मनैव तु ॥
1.25.m: Those who know the teachings of the Veda declare that I am that liṅga; / therefore I worship the Lord, the Self, through my own self alone.

1.25.s:
tasyaiva paramā mūrtistanmayo 'haṃ na saṃśayaḥ /
nāvayordyite bhedo vedeṣvevaṃ viniścayaḥ //
1.25.d:
तस्यैव परमा मूर्तिस्तन्मयो ऽहं न संशयः ।
नावयोर्द्यिते भेदो वेदेष्वेवं विनिश्चयः ॥
1.25.m: I am his supreme form, identical with him—there is no doubt; / between the two of us no difference is seen: such is the conviction in the Vedas.

1.25.s:
eṣa devo mahādevaḥ sadā saṃsārabhīrubhiḥ /
dhyeyaḥ pūjyaśca vandyaśca jñeyo liṅge maheśvaraḥ //
1.25.d:
एष देवो महादेवः सदा संसारभीरुभिः ।
ध्येयः पूज्यश्च वन्द्यश्च ज्ञेयो लिङ्गे महेश्वरः ॥
1.25.m: This god, Mahādeva, Maheśvara in the liṅga, is always / to be meditated upon, worshiped, praised, and known by those afraid of saṃsāra.”

1.25.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
kiṃ talliṅgaṃ suraśreṣṭha liṅge saṃpūjyate ca kaḥ /
brūhi kṛṣṇa viśālākṣa gahanaṃ hyetaduttamam //
1.25.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
किं तल्लिङ्गं सुरश्रेष्ठ लिङ्गे संपूज्यते च कः ।
ब्रूहि कृष्ण विशालाक्ष गहनं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥
1.25.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / “What is that liṅga, O best of gods, and who is worshiped in the liṅga? / Tell me, large-eyed Kṛṣṇa, for this is profound and supreme.”

1.25.s:
avyaktaṃ liṅgamityāhurānandaṃ jyotirakṣaram /
vedā mahesvaraṃ devamāhurliṅginamavyayam //
1.25.d:
अव्यक्तं लिङ्गमित्याहुरानन्दं ज्योतिरक्षरम् ।
वेदा महेस्वरं देवमाहुर्लिङ्गिनमव्ययम् ॥
1.25.m: [Kṛṣṇa said:] / “They say the liṅga is the unmanifest, bliss, the imperishable light; / the Vedas declare the divine Maheśvara to be the imperishable possessor of the liṅga.

1.25.s:
purā caikārṇave ghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame /
prabodhārthaṃ brahmaṇo me prādurbhūtaḥ svayaṃ śivaḥ //
1.25.d:
पुरा चैकार्णवे घोरे नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे ।
प्रबोधार्थं ब्रह्मणो मे प्रादुर्भूतः स्वयं शिवः ॥
1.25.m: And formerly, when the immobile and mobile had perished in the terrible single ocean, / Śiva himself manifested for the awakening of Brahmā and me.

1.25.s:
tasmāt kālāt samārabhya brahmā cāhaṃ sadaiva hi /
pūjayāvo mahādevaṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
1.25.d:
तस्मात् कालात् समारभ्य ब्रह्मा चाहं सदैव हि ।
पूजयावो महादेवं लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
1.25.m: Beginning from that time, Brahmā and I indeed always / worship Mahādeva out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.”

1.25.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
kathaṃ liṅgamabhūt pūrvamaiśvaraṃ paramaṃ padam /
prabodhārthaṃ svayaṃ kṛṣṇa vaktumarhasi sāṃpratam //
1.25.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
कथं लिङ्गमभूत् पूर्वमैश्वरं परमं पदम् ।
प्रबोधार्थं स्वयं कृष्ण वक्तुमर्हसि सांप्रतम् ॥
1.25.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / “How did that supreme abode of the Lord, the liṅga, arise formerly? / For our enlightenment, Kṛṣṇa, you yourself deign to tell it now.”

1.25.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca
āsodekārṇavaṃ ghoramavibhāgaṃ tamomayam /
madhye caikārṇave tasmin śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ //
1.25.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
आसोदेकार्णवं घोरमविभागं तमोमयम् ।
मध्ये चैकार्णवे तस्मिन् शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ॥
1.25.m: The Blessed Lord said: / “There was a terrible, undivided single ocean filled with darkness; / and in the midst of that single ocean, the bearer of the conch, discus, and mace—”

1.25.s:
sahastraśīrṣā bhūtvāhaṃ sahastrākṣaḥ sahastrapāt
sahastrabāhuryuktātmā śayito 'haṃ sanātanaḥ //
1.25.d:
सहस्त्रशीर्षा भूत्वाहं सहस्त्राक्षः सहस्त्रपात्
सहस्त्रबाहुर्युक्तात्मा शयितो ऽहं सनातनः ॥
1.25.m: Becoming a thousand-headed, thousand-eyed, thousand-footed, / thousand-armed one, focused in self, I, the eternal one, lay sleeping.

1.25.s:
etasminnantare dūratā paśyami hyamitaprabham /
koṭisūryapratīkāśaṃ bhrājamānaṃ śriyāvṛtam //
1.25.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दूरता पश्यमि ह्यमितप्रभम् ।
कोटिसूर्यप्रतीकाशं भ्राजमानं श्रियावृतम् ॥
1.25.m: In the meantime, I saw from afar one of immeasurable splendor, / resembling ten million suns, shining forth and surrounded by fortune;

1.25.s:
caturvaraktraṃ mahāyogaṃ puruṣaṃ kāñcanaprabham /
kṛṣṇājiradharaṃ devamṛgyajuḥ sāmabhiḥ stutam //
1.25.d:
चतुर्वरक्त्रं महायोगं पुरुषं काञ्चनप्रभम् ।
कृष्णाजिरधरं देवमृग्यजुः सामभिः स्तुतम् ॥
1.25.m: a four-faced person of great yoga, possessing a golden luster, / wearing a black antelope skin, a god praised with the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas.

1.25.s:
nimeṣamātreṇa sa māṃ prāpto yogavidāṃ varaḥ /
vyājahāra svayaṃ brahmā smayamāno mahādyutiḥ //
1.25.d:
निमेषमात्रेण स मां प्राप्तो योगविदां वरः ।
व्याजहार स्वयं ब्रह्मा स्मयमानो महाद्युतिः ॥
1.25.m: In the twinkling of an eye, he, the best among knowers of yoga, reached me; / Brahmā himself, of great majesty, smiled and spoke:

1.25.s:
kastvaṃ kuto vā kiṃ ceha tiṣṭhase vaha me prabho /
ahaṃ kartā hi lokānāṃ svayaṃbhūḥ prapitāmahaḥ //
1.25.d:
कस्त्वं कुतो वा किं चेह तिष्ठसे वह मे प्रभो ।
अहं कर्ता हि लोकानां स्वयंभूः प्रपितामहः ॥
1.25.m: “Who are you, or whence [did you come], and why do you stay here? Tell me, O lord. / For I am the creator of the worlds, the self-born Great-Grandfather.”

1.25.s:
evamuktastadā tena brahmaṇāhamuvāca ha /
ahaṃ kartāsmi lokānāṃ saṃhartā ca punaḥ punaḥ //
1.25.d:
एवमुक्तस्तदा तेन ब्रह्मणाहमुवाच ह ।
अहं कर्तास्मि लोकानां संहर्ता च पुनः पुनः ॥
1.25.m: Thus addressed at that time by Brahmā, I spoke indeed: / “I am the creator of the worlds and the destroyer again and again.”

1.25.s:
evaṃ vivāde vitate māyayā parameṣṭhinaḥ /
prabodhārthaṃ paraṃ liṅgaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ śivātmakam //
1.25.d:
एवं विवादे वितते मायया परमेष्ठिनः ।
प्रबोधार्थं परं लिङ्गं प्रादुर्भूतं शिवात्मकम् ॥
1.25.m: While such a dispute was extended through the illusory creative power of Parameṣṭhin, / the supreme liṅga, whose nature is Śiva, manifested itself for our awakening;

1.25.s:
kālānalasamaprakhyaṃ jvālāmālāsamākulam /
kṣayavṛddhivinirmuktamādimadhyāntavarjitam //
1.25.d:
कालानलसमप्रख्यं ज्वालामालासमाकुलम् ।
क्षयवृद्धिविनिर्मुक्तमादिमध्यान्तवर्जितम् ॥
1.25.m: resembling the fire of cosmic dissolution, crowded with wreaths of flames, / free from decay and growth, devoid of beginning, middle, and end.

1.25.s:
tato māmāha bhagavānadho gaccha tvamāśu vai /
antamasya vijānīma ūrdhvaṃ gacche 'hamityajaḥ //
1.25.d:
ततो मामाह भगवानधो गच्छ त्वमाशु वै ।
अन्तमस्य विजानीम ऊर्ध्वं गच्छे ऽहमित्यजः ॥
1.25.m: Then the unborn lord said to me: “You go below quickly indeed; / let us find its end; I will go upward.”

1.25.s:
tadāśu samayaṃ kṛtvā gatāvūrdhvamadhaśca dvau /
pitāmaho 'pyahaṃ nāntaṃ jñātavantau samāḥ śatam //
1.25.d:
तदाशु समयं कृत्वा गतावूर्ध्वमधश्च द्वौ ।
पितामहो ऽप्यहं नान्तं ज्ञातवन्तौ समाः शतम् ॥
1.25.m: Then, having quickly made an agreement, the two of us went upward and downward; / yet neither the Grandfather nor I could find its end for a hundred years.

1.25.s:
tato vismayamāpannau bhītau devasya śūlinaḥ /
māyayā mohitau tasya dhyāyantau viśvamīśvaram //
1.25.d:
ततो विस्मयमापन्नौ भीतौ देवस्य शूलिनः ।
मायया मोहितौ तस्य ध्यायन्तौ विश्वमीश्वरम् ॥
1.25.m: Then, struck with wonder and frightened of the spear-bearing god, / bewildered by his illusory creative power, meditating on the Lord of the universe,

1.25.s:
proccārantau mahānādamoṅkāraṃ paramaṃ padam /
prahvāñjalipuṭopetau śaṃbhuṃ tuṣṭuvatuḥ param //
1.25.d:
प्रोच्चारन्तौ महानादमोङ्कारं परमं पदम् ।
प्रह्वाञ्जलिपुटोपेतौ शंभुं तुष्टुवतुः परम् ॥
1.25.m: pronouncing the great sound, the syllable Oṃ, the supreme state, / with hands joined respectfully, the two of them praised supreme Śambhu.

1.25.s:
brahmaviṣṇū ūcatuḥ /
anādimalasaṃsārarogavaidyāya śaṃbhave /
namaḥ śivāya śāntāya brahmaṇe liṅgamūrtaye //
1.25.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णू ऊचतुः ।
अनादिमलसंसाररोगवैद्याय शंभवे ।
नमः शिवाय शान्ताय ब्रह्मणे लिङ्गमूर्तये ॥
1.25.m: Brahmā and Viṣṇu said: / “To Śambhu, the physician for the disease of beginningless, impure worldly existence, / salutation to Śiva, the tranquil, to Brahman whose form is the liṅga;

1.25.s:
pralayārṇavasaṃsthāya pralayodbhūtihetave /
namaḥ śivāya śāntāya brahmaṇe liṅgamūrtaye //
1.25.d:
प्रलयार्णवसंस्थाय प्रलयोद्भूतिहेतवे ।
नमः शिवाय शान्ताय ब्रह्मणे लिङ्गमूर्तये ॥
1.25.m: to the one abiding in the ocean of dissolution, the cause of creation and dissolution, / salutation to Śiva, the tranquil, to Brahman whose form is the liṅga;

1.25.s:
jvālāmālāvṛtāṅgāya jvalanastambharūpiṇe /
namaḥ śivāya śāntāya brahmaṇe liṅgamūrtaye //
1.25.d:
ज्वालामालावृताङ्गाय ज्वलनस्तम्भरूपिणे ।
नमः शिवाय शान्ताय ब्रह्मणे लिङ्गमूर्तये ॥
1.25.m: to the one whose limbs are enveloped by garlands of flames, having the form of a pillar of fire, / salutation to Śiva, the tranquil, to Brahman whose form is the liṅga;

1.25.s:
ādimadhyāntahīnāya svabāvāmaladīptaye /
namaḥ śivāya śāntāya brahmaṇe liṅgamūrtaye //
1.25.d:
आदिमध्यान्तहीनाय स्वबावामलदीप्तये ।
नमः शिवाय शान्ताय ब्रह्मणे लिङ्गमूर्तये ॥
1.25.m: to the one devoid of beginning, middle, and end, possessing an inherently pure luster, / salutation to Śiva, the tranquil, to Brahman whose form is the liṅga;

1.25.s:
mahādevāya mahate jyotiṣe 'nantatejase /
namaḥ śivāya śāntāya brahmaṇe liṅgamūrtaye //
1.25.d:
महादेवाय महते ज्योतिषे ऽनन्ततेजसे ।
नमः शिवाय शान्ताय ब्रह्मणे लिङ्गमूर्तये ॥
1.25.m: to Mahādeva, the great light, of endless radiance, / salutation to Śiva, the tranquil, to Brahman whose form is the liṅga;

1.25.s:
pradhānapuruṣeśāya vyomarūpāya vedhase /
namaḥ śivāya śāntāya brahmaṇe liṅgamūrtaye //
1.25.d:
प्रधानपुरुषेशाय व्योमरूपाय वेधसे ।
नमः शिवाय शान्ताय ब्रह्मणे लिङ्गमूर्तये ॥
1.25.m: to the lord of primordial matter and the spirit, whose form is space, the creator, / salutation to Śiva, the tranquil, to Brahman whose form is the liṅga;

1.25.s:
nirvikārāya satyāya nityāyāmalatejase /
namaḥ śivāya śāntāya brahmaṇe liṅgamūrtaye //
1.25.d:
निर्विकाराय सत्याय नित्यायामलतेजसे ।
नमः शिवाय शान्ताय ब्रह्मणे लिङ्गमूर्तये ॥
1.25.m: to the changeless, true, eternal one of pure splendor, / salutation to Śiva, the tranquil, to Brahman whose form is the liṅga;

1.25.s:
vedāntasārarūpāya kālarūpāya dhīmate /
namaḥ śivāya śāntāya brahmaṇe liṅgamūrtaye //
1.25.d:
वेदान्तसाररूपाय कालरूपाय धीमते ।
नमः शिवाय शान्ताय ब्रह्मणे लिङ्गमूर्तये ॥
1.25.m: to the one whose form is the essence of Vedānta, whose form is Time, the wise one, / salutation to Śiva, the tranquil, to Brahman whose form is the liṅga!”

1.25.s:
evaṃ saṃstūyamānastu vyakto bhūtvā maheśvaraḥ /
bhāti devo mahāyogī sūryakoṭisamaprabhaḥ //
1.25.d:
एवं संस्तूयमानस्तु व्यक्तो भूत्वा महेश्वरः ।
भाति देवो महायोगी सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभः ॥
1.25.m: Being thus praised, Maheśvara became manifest; / the god, the great yogin, shone like ten million suns,

1.25.s:
vaktrakoṭisahastreṇa grasamāna ivāmbaram /
sahastrahastacaraṇaḥ sūryasomāgnilocanaḥ //
1.25.d:
वक्त्रकोटिसहस्त्रेण ग्रसमान इवाम्बरम् ।
सहस्त्रहस्तचरणः सूर्यसोमाग्निलोचनः ॥
1.25.m: as if swallowing the sky with ten million thousand mouths, / having a thousand hands and feet, with the sun, the moon, and fire as his eyes,

1.25.s:
pinākapāṇirbhagavān kṛttivāsāstriśūlabhṛt /
vyālayajñopavītaśca meghadundubhiniḥ svanaḥ //
1.25.d:
पिनाकपाणिर्भगवान् कृत्तिवासास्त्रिशूलभृत् ।
व्यालयज्ञोपवीतश्च मेघदुन्दुभिनिः स्वनः ॥
1.25.m: the lord holding the Pināka in his hand, clad in an animal hide, bearing a trident, / with a serpent as his sacred thread, his voice like the roar of clouds and kettledrums.

1.25.s:
athovāca mahādevaḥ prīto 'haṃ surasattamau /
paśyetaṃ māṃ mahādevaṃ bhayaṃ sarvaṃ pramucyatām //
1.25.d:
अथोवाच महादेवः प्रीतो ऽहं सुरसत्तमौ ।
पश्येतं मां महादेवं भयं सर्वं प्रमुच्यताम् ॥
1.25.m: Then Mahādeva said: “I am pleased, O two best of gods; / behold me, Mahādeva; let all fear be cast away!

1.25.s:
yuvāṃ prasūtau gātrebhyo mama pūrvaṃ sanātanau /
ayaṃ me dakṣiṇe pārśve brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ /
vāmapārśve ca me viṣṇuḥ pālako hṛdaye haraḥ //
1.25.d:
युवां प्रसूतौ गात्रेभ्यो मम पूर्वं सनातनौ ।
अयं मे दक्षिणे पार्श्वे ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ।
वामपार्श्वे च मे विष्णुः पालको हृदये हरः ॥
1.25.m: You two were previously born from my limbs, eternal ones: / this Brahmā on my right side is the Grandfather of the world, / on my left side is Viṣṇu the protector, and Hara is in my heart.

1.25.s:
prīto 'haṃ yuvayoḥ samyak varaṃ dadmi yathepsitam /
evamuktvātha māṃ devo mahādevaḥ svayaṃ śivaḥ /
āliṅgya devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ prasādābhimukho 'bhavat //
1.25.d:
प्रीतो ऽहं युवयोः सम्यक् वरं दद्मि यथेप्सितम् ।
एवमुक्त्वाथ मां देवो महादेवः स्वयं शिवः ।
आलिङ्ग्य देवं ब्रह्माणं प्रसादाभिमुखो ऽभवत् ॥
1.25.m: I am pleased with both of you; I grant a boon as desired.” / Having thus spoken to me, the god, Mahādeva, Śiva himself, / embraced the god Brahmā and turned to show grace.

1.25.s:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭamanasau praṇipatya maheśvaram /
ūcatuḥ prekṣya tadvaktraṃ nārāyaṇapitāmahau //
1.25.d:
ततः प्रहृष्टमनसौ प्रणिपत्य महेश्वरम् ।
ऊचतुः प्रेक्ष्य तद्वक्त्रं नारायणपितामहौ ॥
1.25.m: Then, their minds delighted, having bowed down before Maheśvara, / Nārāyaṇa and the Grandfather looked at his face and said:

1.25.s:
yadi prītiḥ samutpannā yadi deyo varaśca nau /
bhaktirbhavatu nau nityaṃ tvayi deva maheśvare //
1.25.d:
यदि प्रीतिः समुत्पन्ना यदि देयो वरश्च नौ ।
भक्तिर्भवतु नौ नित्यं त्वयि देव महेश्वरे ॥
1.25.m: “If pleasure has arisen [in you], and if a boon is to be given to us, / may our devotion ever be directed to you, O god Maheśvara!”

1.25.s:
tataḥ sa bhagavānīśaḥ prahasan parameśvaraḥ /
uvāca māṃ mahādevaḥ prītaḥ prītena cetasā //
1.25.d:
ततः स भगवानीशः प्रहसन् परमेश्वरः ।
उवाच मां महादेवः प्रीतः प्रीतेन चेतसा ॥
1.25.m: Then that lord, the ruler, smiling, the Supreme Lord, / Mahādeva, pleased, spoke to me with a glad heart.

1.25.s:
deva uvāca
pralayasthitisargāṇāṃ kartā tvaṃ dharaṇīpate /
vatsa vatsa hare viśvaṃ pālayaitaccarācaram //
1.25.d:
देव उवाच
प्रलयस्थितिसर्गाणां कर्ता त्वं धरणीपते ।
वत्स वत्स हरे विश्वं पालयैतच्चराचरम् ॥
1.25.m: The god said: / “You are the maker of dissolution, maintenance, and creation, O lord of the earth; / child, child Hari, protect this universe of moving and unmoving beings.

1.25.s:
tridhā bhinno 'smyahaṃ viṣṇo brahmaviṣṇuharākhyayā /
sargarakṣālayaguṇairnirguṇo 'pi nirañjanaḥ //
1.25.d:
त्रिधा भिन्नो ऽस्म्यहं विष्णो ब्रह्मविष्णुहराख्यया ।
सर्गरक्षालयगुणैर्निर्गुणो ऽपि निरञ्जनः ॥
1.25.m: I am divided threefold, O Viṣṇu, under the names Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Hara, / by the qualities of creation, preservation, and dissolution, though I am devoid of qualities and spotless.

1.25.s:
saṃmohaṃ tyaja bho viṣṇo pālayainaṃ pitāmaham /
bhaviṣyatyeṣa bhagavāṃstava putraḥ sanātanaḥ //
1.25.d:
संमोहं त्यज भो विष्णो पालयैनं पितामहम् ।
भविष्यत्येष भगवांस्तव पुत्रः सनातनः ॥
1.25.m: Cast away delusion, O Viṣṇu! Protect this Grandfather; / this venerable one will become your eternal son.

1.25.s:
ahaṃ ca bhavato vaktrāt kalpādau ghorarūpadhṛk /
śūlapāṇirbhaviṣyāmi krodhajastava putrakaḥ //
1.25.d:
अहं च भवतो वक्त्रात् कल्पादौ घोररूपधृक् ।
शूलपाणिर्भविष्यामि क्रोधजस्तव पुत्रकः ॥
1.25.m: And I, assuming a dreadful form, / bearing a trident in hand, will be born from your mouth at the beginning of the kalpa, born from wrath, as your son.”

1.25.s:
evamuktvā mahādevo brahmāṇaṃ munisattama /
anugṛhya ca māṃ devastatraivāntaradhīyata //
1.25.d:
एवमुक्त्वा महादेवो ब्रह्माणं मुनिसत्तम ।
अनुगृह्य च मां देवस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
1.25.m: Having spoken thus to Brahmā, O best of sages, / and having shown grace to me, the god disappeared right there.

1.25.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti lokeṣu liṅgārcā supratiṣṭhitā /
liṅga tallayanād brahman brahmaṇaḥ paramaṃ vapuḥ //
1.25.d:
ततः प्रभृति लोकेषु लिङ्गार्चा सुप्रतिष्ठिता ।
लिङ्ग तल्लयनाद् ब्रह्मन् ब्रह्मणः परमं वपुः ॥
1.25.m: From then on, the worship of the liṅga was well established in the worlds; / it is called a liṅga, O Brahman, because of dissolution into it; it is the supreme body of Brahman.

1.25.s:
etalliṅgasya māhātmyaṃ bhāṣitaṃ te mayānagha /
etad budhyanti yogajñā na devā na ca dānavāḥ //
1.25.d:
एतल्लिङ्गस्य माहात्म्यं भाषितं ते मयानघ ।
एतद् बुध्यन्ति योगज्ञा न देवा न च दानवाः ॥
1.25.m: This greatness of the liṅga has been proclaimed to you by me, O sinless one; / the knowers of yoga understand this, neither the gods nor the Dānavas [do].

1.25.s:
etaddhi paramaṃ jñānamavyaktaṃ śivasaṃjñitam /
yena sūkṣmamacintyaṃ tat paśyanti jñāna vakṣuṣaḥ //
1.25.d:
एतद्धि परमं ज्ञानमव्यक्तं शिवसंज्ञितम् ।
येन सूक्ष्ममचिन्त्यं तत् पश्यन्ति ज्ञान वक्षुषः ॥
1.25.m: For this is the supreme unmanifest knowledge called Śiva, / through which those with eyes of knowledge perceive that subtle, unthinkable [truth].

1.25.s:
tasmai bhagavate nityaṃ namaskāraṃ prakurmahe /
mahādevāya rudrāya devadevāya liṅgine //
1.25.d:
तस्मै भगवते नित्यं नमस्कारं प्रकुर्महे ।
महादेवाय रुद्राय देवदेवाय लिङ्गिने ॥
1.25.m: To that lord we constantly offer salutation: / to Mahādeva, to Rudra, the god of gods, the bearer of the liṅga;

1.25.s:
namo vedarahasyāya nīlakaṇṭhāya vai namaḥ /
vibhīṣaṇāya śāntāya sthāṇave hetave namaḥ //
1.25.d:
नमो वेदरहस्याय नीलकण्ठाय वै नमः ।
विभीषणाय शान्ताय स्थाणवे हेतवे नमः ॥
1.25.m: salutation to the secret of the Vedas, salutation indeed to the blue-necked one, / to the dreadful, the peaceful, the pillar-like, salutation to the cause;

1.25.s:
brahmaṇe vāmadevāya trinetrāya mahīyase /
śaṅkarāya maheśāya girīśāya śivāya ca //
1.25.d:
ब्रह्मणे वामदेवाय त्रिनेत्राय महीयसे ।
शङ्कराय महेशाय गिरीशाय शिवाय च ॥
1.25.m: to Brahman, to Vāmadeva, the three-eyed, the exceedingly great, / to Śaṅkara, to Maheśa, to the lord of mountains, and to Śiva.

1.25.s:
namaḥ kuruṣva satataṃ dhyāyasva manasā haram /
saṃsārasāgarādasmādacirāduttariṣyasi //
1.25.d:
नमः कुरुष्व सततं ध्यायस्व मनसा हरम् ।
संसारसागरादस्मादचिरादुत्तरिष्यसि ॥
1.25.m: Constantly offer salutations, meditate with your mind on Hara; / you will quickly cross over this ocean of worldly existence.”

1.25.s:
evaṃ sa vāsudevena vyāhṛto munipuṅgavaḥ /
jagāma manasā devamīśānaṃ viśvatomukham //
1.25.d:
एवं स वासुदेवेन व्याहृतो मुनिपुङ्गवः ।
जगाम मनसा देवमीशानं विश्वतोमुखम् ॥
1.25.m: Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, that eminent sage / went with his mind to the god Īśāna, facing every direction.

1.25.s:
praṇamya śirasā kṛṣṇamanujñāto mahāmuniḥ /
jagāma cepsitaṃ deśaṃ devadevasya śūlinaḥ //
1.25.d:
प्रणम्य शिरसा कृष्णमनुज्ञातो महामुनिः ।
जगाम चेप्सितं देशं देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ॥
1.25.m: Having bowed with his head to Kṛṣṇa, permitted [by him], the great sage / went to the desired place of the trident-bearing god of gods.

1.25.s:
ya imaṃ śrāvayennityaṃ liṅgādhyāyamanuttamam /
śṛṇuyād vā paṭhed vāpi sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
1.25.d:
य इमं श्रावयेन्नित्यं लिङ्गाध्यायमनुत्तमम् ।
शृणुयाद् वा पठेद् वापि सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
1.25.m: Whoever causes this incomparable chapter on the liṅga to be heard daily, / or hears it, or reads it, is released from all sins.

1.25.s:
śrutvā sakṛdapi hyetat tapaścaraṇamuttamam /
vāsudevasya viprendrāḥ pāpaṃ muñciti mānavaḥ //
1.25.d:
श्रुत्वा सकृदपि ह्येतत् तपश्चरणमुत्तमम् ।
वासुदेवस्य विप्रेन्द्राः पापं मुञ्चिति मानवः ॥
1.25.m: Even having heard once this supreme performance of austerities / by Vāsudeva, O best of brahmins, a person is freed from sin.

1.25.s:
japed vāharaharnityaṃ brahmaloke mahīyate /
evamāha mahāyogī kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge pañcaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.25.d:
जपेद् वाहरहर्नित्यं ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ।
एवमाह महायोगी कृष्णद्वैपायनः प्रभुः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे पञ्चविंशो ऽध्यायः
1.25.m:
Or if he recites it daily every day, he is magnified in the world of Brahmā. / Thus spoke the great yogin, the lord Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.26.s:
sūta uvāca
tato labdhavaraḥ kṛṣṇo jāmbavatyāṃ maheśvarāt /
ajījananmahātmānaṃ sāmbamātmajamuttamam //
1.26.d:
सूत उवाच
ततो लब्धवरः कृष्णो जाम्बवत्यां महेश्वरात् ।
अजीजनन्महात्मानं साम्बमात्मजमुत्तमम् ॥
1.26.m: Sūta said: / Then Kṛṣṇa, having obtained a boon from Maheśvara, begot upon Jāmbavatī / the great-souled Sāmba, his excellent son.

1.26.s:
pradyumnasyāpyabhūt putro hyaniruddho mahābalaḥ /
tāvubhau guṇasaṃpannau kṛṣṇasyaivāpare tanū //
1.26.d:
प्रद्युम्नस्याप्यभूत् पुत्रो ह्यनिरुद्धो महाबलः ।
तावुभौ गुणसंपन्नौ कृष्णस्यैवापरे तनू ॥
1.26.m: Pradyumna also had a son, the mighty Aniruddha. / Both of them, endowed with virtues, were other bodies of Kṛṣṇa himself.

1.26.s:
hatvā ca kaṃsaṃ narakamanyāṃśca śataśo 'surān /
vijitya līlayā śakraṃ jitvā bāṇaṃ mahāsuram //
1.26.d:
हत्वा च कंसं नरकमन्यांश्च शतशो ऽसुरान् ।
विजित्य लीलया शक्रं जित्वा बाणं महासुरम् ॥
1.26.m: Having slain Kaṃsa, Naraka, and hundreds of other asuras, / having playfully overcome Śakra, and having defeated the great asura Bāṇa,

1.26.s:
sthāpayitvā jagat kṛtsnaṃ loke dharmāṃśca śāśvatān /
cakre nārāyaṇo gantuṃ svasthānaṃ buddhimuttamām //
1.26.d:
स्थापयित्वा जगत् कृत्स्नं लोके धर्मांश्च शाश्वतान् ।
चक्रे नारायणो गन्तुं स्वस्थानं बुद्धिमुत्तमाम् ॥
1.26.m: and having established the entire world and the eternal duties among men, / Nārāyaṇa resolved to depart to his own realm.

1.26.s:
etasminnantare viprā bhṛgvādyāḥ kṛṣṇamīśvaram /
ājagmurdvārakāṃ draṣṭuṃ kṛtakāryaṃ sanātanam //
1.26.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे विप्रा भृग्वाद्याः कृष्णमीश्वरम् ।
आजग्मुर्द्वारकां द्रष्टुं कृतकार्यं सनातनम् ॥
1.26.m: In the meantime, O brāhmaṇas, Bhṛgu and other [sages] came to Dvārakā / to see the lord Kṛṣṇa, the eternal one who had accomplished his work.

1.26.s:
sa tānuvāca viśvātmā praṇipatyābhipūjya ca /
āsaneṣūpaviṣṭān vai saha rāmeṇa dhīmatā //
1.26.d:
स तानुवाच विश्वात्मा प्रणिपत्याभिपूज्य च ।
आसनेषूपविष्टान् वै सह रामेण धीमता ॥
1.26.m: He, the soul of all, bowing down and honoring them / as they sat on seats along with the wise Rāma, addressed them:

1.26.s:
gamiṣye tat paraṃ sthānaṃ svakīyaṃ viṣṇusaṃjñitam /
kṛtāni sarvakāryāṇi prasīdadhvaṃ munīśvarāḥ //
1.26.d:
गमिष्ये तत् परं स्थानं स्वकीयं विष्णुसंज्ञितम् ।
कृतानि सर्वकार्याणि प्रसीदध्वं मुनीश्वराः ॥
1.26.m: “I shall go to that supreme abode of mine called Viṣṇu. / All deeds have been accomplished; be gracious, O best of sages!

1.26.s:
idaṃ kaliyugaṃ ghoraṃ saṃprāptamadhunāśubham /
bhaviṣyanti janāḥ sarve hyasmin pāpānuvartinaḥ //
1.26.d:
इदं कलियुगं घोरं संप्राप्तमधुनाशुभम् ।
भविष्यन्ति जनाः सर्वे ह्यस्मिन् पापानुवर्तिनः ॥
1.26.m: This dreadful, inauspicious Kali age has now arrived; / in it all people will pursue sin.

1.26.s:
pravartayadhvaṃ majjñānaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ hitāvaham /
yeneme kalijaiḥ pāpairmucyante hi dvijottamāḥ //
1.26.d:
प्रवर्तयध्वं मज्ज्ञानं ब्राह्मणानां हितावहम् ।
येनेमे कलिजैः पापैर्मुच्यन्ते हि द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.26.m: Promote my knowledge, which brings welfare to brāhmaṇas, / so that these best of twice-born may indeed be freed from sins born of Kali.

1.26.s:
ye māṃ janāḥ saṃsmaranti kalau sakṛdapi prabhum /
teṣāṃ naśyatu tat pāpaṃ bhaktānāṃ puruṣottame //
1.26.d:
ये मां जनाः संस्मरन्ति कलौ सकृदपि प्रभुम् ।
तेषां नश्यतु तत् पापं भक्तानां पुरुषोत्तमे ॥
1.26.m: The people who remember me, the lord, even once in the Kali [age], / may the sins of those devotees of the Supreme Spirit be destroyed.

1.26.s:
yer'cayiṣyantimāṃ bhaktyā nityaṃ kaliyuge dvijāḥ /
vidhānā vedadṛṣṭena te gamiṣyanti tat padam //
1.26.d:
येर्ऽचयिष्यन्तिमां भक्त्या नित्यं कलियुगे द्विजाः ।
विधाना वेददृष्टेन ते गमिष्यन्ति तत् पदम् ॥
1.26.m: The twice-born who will worship me with devotion constantly in the Kali age / according to the rules perceived in the Veda, they will go to that realm.

1.26.s:
ye brāhmaṇā vaṃśajātā yuṣmākaṃ vai sahastraśaḥ /
teṣāṃ nārāyaṇe bhaktirbhaviṣyati kalau yuge //
1.26.d:
ये ब्राह्मणा वंशजाता युष्माकं वै सहस्त्रशः ।
तेषां नारायणे भक्तिर्भविष्यति कलौ युगे ॥
1.26.m: The thousands of brāhmaṇas born in your lineages, / will have devotion to Nārāyaṇa in the Kali age.

1.26.s:
parāt parataraṃ yānti nārāyaṇaparāyaṇāḥ /
na te tatra gamiṣyanti ye dviṣanti maheśvaram //
1.26.d:
परात् परतरं यान्ति नारायणपरायणाः ।
न ते तत्र गमिष्यन्ति ये द्विषन्ति महेश्वरम् ॥
1.26.m: Those devoted to Nārāyaṇa go to that which is higher than the highest; / but those who hate Maheśvara will not go there.

1.26.s:
dhyānaṃ homaṃ tapastaptaṃ jñānaṃ yajñādiko vidhiḥ /
teṣāṃ vinaśyati kṣipraṃ ye nindanti pinākinam //
1.26.d:
ध्यानं होमं तपस्तप्तं ज्ञानं यज्ञादिको विधिः ।
तेषां विनश्यति क्षिप्रं ये निन्दन्ति पिनाकिनम् ॥
1.26.m: Meditation, fire-offerings, austerity performed, knowledge, rites such as sacrifices— / all these quickly perish for those who revile the Wielder of the Pināka.

1.26.s:
yo māṃ samāśrayennityamekāntaṃ bhāvamāśritaḥ /
vinindya devamīśānaṃ sa yāti narakāyutam //
1.26.d:
यो मां समाश्रयेन्नित्यमेकान्तं भावमाश्रितः ।
विनिन्द्य देवमीशानं स याति नरकायुतम् ॥
1.26.m: He who takes refuge in me constantly, devoted with undivided sentiment, / but reviles the god Īśāna, goes to ten thousand hells.

1.26.s:
tasmāt sā parihartavyā nindā paśupatau dvijāḥ /
karmaṇā manasā vācā tadbhakteṣvapi yatnataḥ //
1.26.d:
तस्मात् सा परिहर्तव्या निन्दा पशुपतौ द्विजाः ।
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा तद्भक्तेष्वपि यत्नतः ॥
1.26.m: Therefore, O twice-born, reviling of Paśupati / in action, thought, and word—even towards his devotees—must be avoided with effort.

1.26.s:
ye tu dakṣādhvare śaptā dadhīyena dvijottamāḥ /
bhaviṣyanti kalau bhaktaiḥ parihāryāḥ prayatnataḥ //
1.26.d:
ये तु दक्षाध्वरे शप्ता दधीयेन द्विजोत्तमाः ।
भविष्यन्ति कलौ भक्तैः परिहार्याः प्रयत्नतः ॥
1.26.m: Those who were cursed by Dadhīca at the sacrifice of Dakṣa, O best of twice-born, / will exist in Kali; they should be avoided with effort by devotees.

1.26.s:
dviṣanto devamīśānaṃ yuṣmākaṃ vaṃśasaṃbhavāḥ /
śaptāśca gautamenorvyāṃ na saṃbhāṣyā dvijottamaiḥ //
1.26.d:
द्विषन्तो देवमीशानं युष्माकं वंशसंभवाः ।
शप्ताश्च गौतमेनोर्व्यां न संभाष्या द्विजोत्तमैः ॥
1.26.m: Those born in your lineage who hate the god Īśāna / and are cursed by Gautama on earth should not be spoken to by the best of twice-born.”

1.26.s:
ityevamuktāḥ kṛṣṇena sarva eva maharṣayaḥ /
omityuktvā yayustūrṇaṃsvāni sthānāni sattamāḥ //
1.26.d:
इत्येवमुक्ताः कृष्णेन सर्व एव महर्षयः ।
ओमित्युक्त्वा ययुस्तूर्णंस्वानि स्थानानि सत्तमाः ॥
1.26.m: Having been thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, all the great sages / said 'Om' and quickly departed to their own abodes, O best of men.

1.26.s:
tato nārāyaṇaḥ kṛṣṇo līlayaiva jaganmayaḥ /
saṃhṛtya svakulaṃ sarvaṃ yayau tat paramaṃ padam //
1.26.d:
ततो नारायणः कृष्णो लीलयैव जगन्मयः ।
संहृत्य स्वकुलं सर्वं ययौ तत् परमं पदम् ॥
1.26.m: Then Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, whose essence is the world, by mere play / destroyed his entire clan and went to that supreme abode.

1.26.s:
ityeṣa vaḥ samāsena rājñāṃ vaṃśo 'nukīrtitaḥ /
na śakyo vistarād vaktuṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchatha //
1.26.d:
इत्येष वः समासेन राज्ञां वंशो ऽनुकीर्तितः ।
