ध्यायन्ति चित्ते यतयो महेशम् ॥
1.30.m: Having attained in this world a birth among Brahmin families, / desired by all worlds and very difficult to attain, / ascetics recite Rudra with composure in meditation, / and meditate upon Maheśa in their mind.

1.30.s:
ārādhayanti prabhumīśitāraṃ
vārāṇasīmadhyagatā munindrāḥ /
yajanti yajñairabhisaṃdhihīnāḥ
stuvanti rudraṃ praṇamanti śaṃbhum //
1.30.d:
आराधयन्ति प्रभुमीशितारं
वाराणसीमध्यगता मुनिन्द्राः ।
यजन्ति यज्ञैरभिसंधिहीनाः
स्तुवन्ति रुद्रं प्रणमन्ति शंभुम् ॥
1.30.m: Residing in the midst of Vārāṇasī, the lords among sages worship the Lord, the sovereign; / free of personal motives, they sacrifice with sacrifices; / they praise Rudra and bow down to Śambhu:

1.30.s:
namo bhavāyāmalayogadhāmne
sthāṇuṃ prapadye giriśaṃ purāṇam /
smarāmi rudraṃ hṛdaye niviṣṭaṃ
jāne mahādevamanekarūpam //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāgetriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.30.d:
नमो भवायामलयोगधाम्ने
स्थाणुं प्रपद्ये गिरिशं पुराणम् ।
स्मरामि रुद्रं हृदये निविष्टं
जाने महादेवमनेकरूपम् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागेत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.30.m:
‘Homage to Bhava, the flawless abode of yoga! / I take refuge in Sthāṇu, Giriśa, the ancient one; / I remember Rudra seated in the heart; / I know Mahādeva of manifold forms.’ ”

Thus ends the thirtieth chapter in the first section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.31.s:
sūta uvāca
samābhāṣya munīn dhīmān devadevasya śūlinaḥ /
jagāma liṅgaṃ tad draṣṭuṃ kapardeśvaramavyayam //
1.31.d:
सूत उवाच
समाभाष्य मुनीन् धीमान् देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ।
जगाम लिङ्गं तद् द्रष्टुं कपर्देश्वरमव्ययम् ॥
1.31.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken to the sages, the wise one went / to see that imperishable liṅga Kapardeśvara of the trident-bearing God of gods.

1.31.s:
snātvā tatra vidhānena tarpayitvā pitṝn dvijāḥ /
piśācamocane tīrthe pūjayāmāsa śūlinam //
1.31.d:
स्नात्वा तत्र विधानेन तर्पयित्वा पितॄन् द्विजाः ।
पिशाचमोचने तीर्थे पूजयामास शूलिनम् ॥
1.31.m: Having bathed there according to rule and having made water-offerings to the ancestors, O twice-born, / he worshipped the trident-bearer at the sacred site of Piśācamocana.

1.31.s:
tatrāścaryamapaśyaṃste munayo guruṇā saha /
menire kṣetramāhātmyaṃ praṇemurgiriśaṃ haram //
1.31.d:
तत्राश्चर्यमपश्यंस्ते मुनयो गुरुणा सह ।
मेनिरे क्षेत्रमाहात्म्यं प्रणेमुर्गिरिशं हरम् ॥
1.31.m: There the sages together with their guru saw a wonder; / they acknowledged the greatness of the sacred precinct and bowed down to Giriśa Hara.

1.31.s:
kaścidabhyājagāmedaṃ śārdūlo ghorarūpadhṛk /
mṛgīmekāṃ bhakṣayituṃ kapardeśvaramuttamam //
1.31.d:
कश्चिदभ्याजगामेदं शार्दूलो घोररूपधृक् ।
मृगीमेकां भक्षयितुं कपर्देश्वरमुत्तमम् ॥
1.31.m: A certain tiger of terrible appearance came to this / excellent Kapardeśvara to devour a doe.

1.31.s:
tatra sā bhītahṛdayā kṛtvā kṛtvā pradakṣiṇam /
dhāvamānā susaṃbhrāntā vyāghrasya vaśamāgatā //
1.31.d:
तत्र सा भीतहृदया कृत्वा कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणम् ।
धावमाना सुसंभ्रान्ता व्याघ्रस्य वशमागता ॥
1.31.m: There, her heart filled with fear, having circumambulated again and again / as she ran, utterly bewildered, she fell into the power of the tiger.

1.31.s:
tāṃ vidārya nakhaistīkṣṇaiḥ śārdūlaḥ sumahābalaḥ /
jagāma cānyaṃ vijanaṃ deśaṃ dṛṣṭvā munīśvarān //
1.31.d:
तां विदार्य नखैस्तीक्ष्णैः शार्दूलः सुमहाबलः ।
जगाम चान्यं विजनं देशं दृष्ट्वा मुनीश्वरान् ॥
1.31.m: Having torn her apart with sharp claws, the tiger of very great strength, / seeing the lords among sages, went away to another, solitary place.

1.31.s:
mṛtamātrā ca sā bālā kapardeśāgrato mṛgī /
adṛśyata mahājvālā vyomni sūryasamaprabhā //
1.31.d:
मृतमात्रा च सा बाला कपर्देशाग्रतो मृगी ।
अदृश्यत महाज्वाला व्योम्नि सूर्यसमप्रभा ॥
1.31.m: And as soon as she died before Kapardeśa, that young doe / was seen in the sky as a great flame of light, with radiance equal to the sun,

1.31.s:
trinetrā nīlakaṇṭhā ca śaśāṅkāṅkitamūrdhajā /
vṛṣādhirūḍhā puruṣaistādṛśaireva saṃvṛtā //
1.31.d:
त्रिनेत्रा नीलकण्ठा च शशाङ्काङ्कितमूर्धजा ।
वृषाधिरूढा पुरुषैस्तादृशैरेव संवृता ॥
1.31.m: three-eyed, blue-throated, with the crescent moon marking her hair, / mounted on a bull, surrounded by beings just like herself.

1.31.s:
puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ vimuñcinti khecarāstasya mūrdhani /
gaṇeśvaraḥ svayaṃ bhūtvā na dṛṣṭastatkṣaṇāt tataḥ //
1.31.d:
पुष्पवृष्टिं विमुञ्चिन्ति खेचरास्तस्य मूर्धनि ।
गणेश्वरः स्वयं भूत्वा न दृष्टस्तत्क्षणात् ततः ॥
1.31.m: Sky-farers showered a rain of flowers upon its head; / having become a lord of the gaṇas himself, he was seen no more from that moment.

1.31.s:
dṛṣṭvaitadāścaryavaraṃ jaiminipramukhā dvijāḥ /
kapardeśvaramāhātmyaṃ papracchurgurumacyutam //
1.31.d:
दृष्ट्वैतदाश्चर्यवरं जैमिनिप्रमुखा द्विजाः ।
कपर्देश्वरमाहात्म्यं पप्रच्छुर्गुरुमच्युतम् ॥
1.31.m: Having seen this supreme wonder, the twice-born led by Jaimini / asked their infallible guru about the greatness of Kapardeśvara.

1.31.s:
teṣāṃ provāca bhagavān devāgre copaviśya saḥ /
kapardeśasya māhātmyaṃ praṇamya vṛṣabhadhvajam //
1.31.d:
तेषां प्रोवाच भगवान् देवाग्रे चोपविश्य सः ।
कपर्देशस्य माहात्म्यं प्रणम्य वृषभध्वजम् ॥
1.31.m: Sitting before the god and bowing to the one whose banner bears a bull, / the Lord told them the greatness of Kapardeśa:

1.31.s:
idaṃ devasya talliṅgaṃ kapardośvaramuttamam /
smṛtvaivāśeṣapāpaughaṃ kṣipramasya vimuñcati //
1.31.d:
इदं देवस्य तल्लिङ्गं कपर्दोश्वरमुत्तमम् ।
स्मृत्वैवाशेषपापौघं क्षिप्रमस्य विमुञ्चति ॥
1.31.m: “This is that excellent liṅga Kapardeśvara of the god; / merely by remembering it, one is quickly freed from an entire flood of sins.

1.31.s:
kāmakrodhādayo doṣā vārāṇasīnivāsinām /
vighnāḥ sarve vinaśyanti kapardeśvarapūjanāt //
1.31.d:
कामक्रोधादयो दोषा वाराणसीनिवासिनाम् ।
विघ्नाः सर्वे विनश्यन्ति कपर्देश्वरपूजनात् ॥
1.31.m: Flaws such as desire and anger among the dwellers of Vārāṇasī, / and all obstacles, are destroyed through the worship of Kapardeśvara.

1.31.s:
tasmāt sadaiva draṣṭavyaṃ kapardeśvaramuttamam /
pūjitavyaṃ prayatnena stotavyaṃ vaidikaiḥ stavaiḥ //
1.31.d:
तस्मात् सदैव द्रष्टव्यं कपर्देश्वरमुत्तमम् ।
पूजितव्यं प्रयत्नेन स्तोतव्यं वैदिकैः स्तवैः ॥
1.31.m: Therefore, the excellent Kapardeśvara should always be seen, / worshipped with exertion, and praised with Vedic hymns.

1.31.s:
dhyāyatāmatra niyataṃ yogināṃ śāntacetasām /
jāyate yogasaṃsiddhiḥ sā ṣaṇmāse na saṃśayaḥ //
1.31.d:
ध्यायतामत्र नियतं योगिनां शान्तचेतसाम् ।
जायते योगसंसिद्धिः सा षण्मासे न संशयः ॥
1.31.m: For yogins of peaceful mind who constantly meditate here, / the full success of yoga arises in six months; of this there is no doubt.

1.31.s:
brahmahatyādayaḥ pāpā vinaśyantyasya pūjanāt /
piśācamocane kuṇḍe snātasyātra samīpataḥ //
1.31.d:
ब्रह्महत्यादयः पापा विनश्यन्त्यस्य पूजनात् ।
पिशाचमोचने कुण्डे स्नातस्यात्र समीपतः ॥
1.31.m: Sins such as Brahmin-murder are destroyed through the worship of this [liṅga], / for one who has bathed here nearby in the pool of Piśācamocana.

1.31.s:
asmin kṣetre purā viprāstapasvī śaṃsitavrataḥ /
śaṅkukarṇa iti khyātaḥ pūjayāmāsa śaṅkaram /
jajāpa rudramaniśaṃ praṇavaṃ brahmarūpiṇam //
1.31.d:
अस्मिन् क्षेत्रे पुरा विप्रास्तपस्वी शंसितव्रतः ।
शङ्कुकर्ण इति ख्यातः पूजयामास शङ्करम् ।
जजाप रुद्रमनिशं प्रणवं ब्रह्मरूपिणम् ॥
1.31.m: In this sacred precinct of old, O twice-born, an ascetic of strict vows / renowned as Śaṅkukarṇa worshipped Śaṅkara; / he incessantly recited Rudra, the Praṇava whose nature is Brahman.

1.31.s:
puṣpadhūpādibhiḥ stotrairnamaskāraiḥ pradakṣiṇaiḥ /
uvāsa tatra yogātmā kṛtvā dīkṣāṃ tu naiṣṭhikīma //
1.31.d:
पुष्पधूपादिभिः स्तोत्रैर्नमस्कारैः प्रदक्षिणैः ।
उवास तत्र योगात्मा कृत्वा दीक्षां तु नैष्ठिकीम ॥
1.31.m: With flowers, incense, and the like, with hymns of praise, bowings, and circumambulations, / the yogic-souled one lived there, having undertaken the lifelong vow.

1.31.s:
kadācidāgataṃ pretaṃ paśyati sma kṣudhānvitam /
asthicarmapinaddhāṅgaṃ niḥ śvasantaṃ muhurmuhuḥ //
1.31.d:
कदाचिदागतं प्रेतं पश्यति स्म क्षुधान्वितम् ।
अस्थिचर्मपिनद्धाङ्गं निः श्वसन्तं मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
1.31.m: At one time he saw a hungry ghost who had come, / his limbs covered with only bone and skin, sighing again and again.

1.31.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sa muniśreṣṭhaḥ kṛpayā parayā yutaḥ /
provāca ko bhavān kasmād deśād deśamimaṃśritaḥ //
1.31.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा स मुनिश्रेष्ठः कृपया परया युतः ।
प्रोवाच को भवान् कस्माद् देशाद् देशमिमंश्रितः ॥
1.31.m: Seeing him, that best of sages, filled with supreme compassion, / said: ‘Who are you? From what country have you resorted to this place?’

1.31.s:
tasmai piśācaḥ kṣudhayā pīḍyamāno 'bravīd vacaḥ /
pūrvajanmanyahaṃ vipro dhanadhānyasamanvitaḥ /
putrapautrādibhiryuktaḥ kuṭumbabharaṇotsukaḥ //
1.31.d:
तस्मै पिशाचः क्षुधया पीड्यमानो ऽब्रवीद् वचः ।
पूर्वजन्मन्यहं विप्रो धनधान्यसमन्वितः ।
पुत्रपौत्रादिभिर्युक्तः कुटुम्बभरणोत्सुकः ॥
1.31.m: Tormented by hunger, the ghost spoke words to him: / ‘In my previous birth I was a Brahmin endowed with wealth and grain, / accompanied by sons, grandsons, and others, eager to maintain my family.

1.31.s:
na pūjitā mayā devā gāvo 'pyatithayastathā /
na kadācit kṛtaṃ puṇyamalpaṃ vā svalpameva vā //
1.31.d:
न पूजिता मया देवा गावो ऽप्यतिथयस्तथा ।
न कदाचित् कृतं पुण्यमल्पं वा स्वल्पमेव वा ॥
1.31.m: I did not worship the gods, nor cows, nor guests; / never was any merit made, whether small or very slight.

1.31.s:
ekadā bhagavān devo govṛṣeśvaravāhanaḥ /
viśveśvaro vārāṇasyāṃ dṛṣṭaḥ spṛṣṭe namaskṛtaḥ //
1.31.d:
एकदा भगवान् देवो गोवृषेश्वरवाहनः ।
विश्वेश्वरो वाराणस्यां दृष्टः स्पृष्टे नमस्कृतः ॥
1.31.m: Once the Lord, the god whose vehicle is the lord of bulls, / Viśveśvara, was seen, touched, and bowed to in Vārāṇasī.’

1.31.s:
tadācireṇa kālena pañcatvamahamāgataḥ /
na dṛṣṭaṃ nanmayā ghoraṃ yamasya vadanaṃ mune //
1.31.d:
तदाचिरेण कालेन पञ्चत्वमहमागतः ।
न दृष्टं नन्मया घोरं यमस्य वदनं मुने ॥
1.31.m:
Then, after a short time, I came to death.
Yet I did not see the terrifying face of Yama, O sage.

1.31.s:
īdṛśīṃ yonimāpannaḥ paiśācīṃ kṣudhayānvitaḥ /
pipāsayādhunākrānto na jānāmi hitāhitam //
1.31.d:
ईदृशीं योनिमापन्नः पैशाचीं क्षुधयान्वितः ।
पिपासयाधुनाक्रान्तो न जानामि हिताहितम् ॥
1.31.m:
Having obtained such an existence as a piśāca, overcome with hunger
and now overwhelmed by thirst, I do not know what is beneficial or harmful.

1.31.s:
yadi kañcit samuddhartumupāyaṃ paśyasi prabho /
kuruṣva taṃ namastubhyaṃ tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
1.31.d:
यदि कञ्चित् समुद्धर्तुमुपायं पश्यसि प्रभो ।
कुरुष्व तं नमस्तुभ्यं त्वामहं शरणं गतः ॥
1.31.m:
If you see any means to rescue me, O lord,
please perform it; reverence to you, I have come to you for refuge.

1.31.s:
ityuktaḥ śaṅkukarṇo 'tha piśācamidamabravīt /
tvādṛśo na hi loke 'smin vidyate puṇyakṛttamaḥ //
1.31.d:
इत्युक्तः शङ्कुकर्णो ऽथ पिशाचमिदमब्रवीत् ।
त्वादृशो न हि लोके ऽस्मिन् विद्यते पुण्यकृत्तमः ॥
1.31.m:
Addressed thus, Śaṅkukarṇa then said this to the piśāca:
“Indeed, there is no one in this world who has performed greater merit than you.

1.31.s:
yat tvayā bhagavān pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭo viśveśvaraḥ śivaḥ /
saṃspṛṣṭo vandito bhūyaḥ ko 'nyastvatsadṛśo bhuvi //
1.31.d:
यत् त्वया भगवान् पूर्वं दृष्टो विश्वेश्वरः शिवः ।
संस्पृष्टो वन्दितो भूयः को ऽन्यस्त्वत्सदृशो भुवि ॥
1.31.m:
Because earlier you beheld the Lord Viśveśvara, Śiva,
touched him, and repeatedly venerated him, who else on earth is your equal?

1.31.s:
tena karmavipākena deśametaṃ samāgataḥ /
snānaṃ kuruṣva śīghraṃ tvamasmin kuṇḍe samāhitaḥ /
yenemāṃ kutsitāṃ yoniṃ kṣiprameva prahāsyasi //
1.31.d:
तेन कर्मविपाकेन देशमेतं समागतः ।
स्नानं कुरुष्व शीघ्रं त्वमस्मिन् कुण्डे समाहितः ।
येनेमां कुत्सितां योनिं क्षिप्रमेव प्रहास्यसि ॥
1.31.m:
Through the ripening of that action, you have arrived at this place.
Bathe quickly in this pool with a concentrated mind,
whereby you will immediately cast off this vile birth.”

1.31.s:
sa evamukto muninā piśāco
dayālunā devavaraṃ trinetram /
smṛtvā kapardeśvaramīśitāraṃ
cakre samādhāya mano 'vagāham //
1.31.d:
स एवमुक्तो मुनिना पिशाचो
दयालुना देववरं त्रिनेत्रम् ।
स्मृत्वा कपर्देश्वरमीशितारं
चक्रे समाधाय मनो ऽवगाहम् ॥
1.31.m:
Spoken to thus by the compassionate sage, the piśāca,
remembering the supreme god, the three-eyed Lord Kapardeśvara,
concentrated his mind and took a plunge [into the water].

1.31.s:
tadāvagāḍho munisaṃnidhāne
mamāra divyābharaṇopapannaḥ /
adṛśyatārkapratime vimāne
śaśāṅkacihnāṅkitacārumauliḥ //
1.31.d:
तदावगाढो मुनिसंनिधाने
ममार दिव्याभरणोपपन्नः ।
अदृश्यतार्कप्रतिमे विमाने
शशाङ्कचिह्नाङ्कितचारुमौलिः ॥
1.31.m:
Having plunged then in the presence of the sage,
he died, endowed with celestial ornaments,
and was seen on a chariot like the sun,
his handsome crown adorned with the crescent moon mark.

1.31.s:
vibhāti rudrairabhito divasthaiḥ
samāvṛto yogibhairaprameyaiḥ /
sabālakhilyādibhireṣa devo
yathodaye bhānuraśeṣadevaḥ //
1.31.d:
विभाति रुद्रैरभितो दिवस्थैः
समावृतो योगिभैरप्रमेयैः ।
सबालखिल्यादिभिरेष देवो
यथोदये भानुरशेषदेवः ॥
1.31.m:
He shone, surrounded on all sides by Rudras dwelling in heaven,
by immeasurable yogins,
and by the Bālakhilyas and others, like the sun,
the god of all, rising at dawn.

1.31.s:
stuvanti siddhā divi devasaṅghā
nṛtyanti divyāpsaraso 'bhirāmāḥ /
muñcanti vṛṣṭiṃ kusumāmbumiśrāṃ
gandharvavidyādharakiṃnarādyāḥ //
1.31.d:
स्तुवन्ति सिद्धा दिवि देवसङ्घा
नृत्यन्ति दिव्याप्सरसो ऽभिरामाः ।
मुञ्चन्ति वृष्टिं कुसुमाम्बुमिश्रां
गन्धर्वविद्याधरकिंनराद्याः ॥

1.31.s:
saṃstūyamāno 'tha munīndrasaṅghai-
ravāpya bodhaṃ bhagavātprasādāt /
samāviśanmaṇḍalametadagryaṃ
trayīmayaṃ yatra vibhāti rudraḥ //
1.31.d:
संस्तूयमानो ऽथ मुनीन्द्रसङ्घै-
रवाप्य बोधं भगवात्प्रसादात् ।
समाविशन्मण्डलमेतदग्र्यं
त्रयीमयं यत्र विभाति रुद्रः ॥
1.31.m:
Then, praised by hosts of supreme sages,
attaining wisdom by the grace of the Lord,
he entered this foremost orb composed of the three Vedas,
where Rudra shines.

1.31.s:
dṛṣṭvā vimuktaṃ sa piśācabhūtaṃ
muniḥ prahṛṣṭo manasā maheśam /
vicintya rudraṃ kavimekamagniṃ
praṇamya tuṣṭāva kapardinaṃ tam //
1.31.d:
दृष्ट्वा विमुक्तं स पिशाचभूतं
मुनिः प्रहृष्टो मनसा महेशम् ।
विचिन्त्य रुद्रं कविमेकमग्निं
प्रणम्य तुष्टाव कपर्दिनं तम् ॥
1.31.m:
Seeing that creature freed from being a piśāca,
the sage was delighted in his mind; reflecting upon the Great Lord,
Rudra, the wise, the one fire,
he bowed and praised the Kapardin.

1.31.s:
śaṅkukarṇa uvāca
kapardinaṃ tvāṃ parataḥ parastād
goptāramekaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam /
vrajāmi yogeśvaramīśitāra-
mādityamagniṃ kapilādhirūḍham //
1.31.d:
शङ्कुकर्ण उवाच
कपर्दिनं त्वां परतः परस्ताद्
गोप्तारमेकं पुरुषं पुराणम् ।
व्रजामि योगेश्वरमीशितार-
मादित्यमग्निं कपिलाधिरूढम् ॥
1.31.m:
Śaṅkukarṇa said:
“To you, the Kapardin, beyond the beyond,
the sole guardian, the ancient spirit,
the lord of yoga, the ruler,
the sun, the fire mounted upon the tawny cow, I go [for refuge].

1.31.s:
tvāṃ brahmapāraṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭaṃ
hiraṇmayaṃ yoginamādimantam /
vrajāmi rudraṃ śaraṇaṃ divasthaṃ
mahāmuniṃ brahmamayaṃ pavitram //
1.31.d:
त्वां ब्रह्मपारं हृदि सन्निविष्टं
हिरण्मयं योगिनमादिमन्तम् ।
व्रजामि रुद्रं शरणं दिवस्थं
महामुनिं ब्रह्ममयं पवित्रम् ॥
1.31.m:
To you, the limit of Brahman, seated in the heart,
golden, the yogin, possessing beginning and end,
to Rudra who dwells in heaven, I go for refuge,
to the great sage, composed of Brahman, pure.

1.31.s:
sahastrapādākṣiśiro 'bhiyuktaṃ
sahastrabāhuṃ namasaḥ parastāt /
tvāṃ brahāmapāraṃ praṇamāmi śaṃbhuṃ
hiraṇyagarbhādhipatiṃ trinetram //
1.31.d:
सहस्त्रपादाक्षिशिरो ऽभियुक्तं
सहस्त्रबाहुं नमसः परस्तात् ।
त्वां ब्रहामपारं प्रणमामि शंभुं
हिरण्यगर्भाधिपतिं त्रिनेत्रम् ॥
1.31.m:
Possessing a thousand feet, eyes, and heads,
having a thousand arms, beyond darkness,
to you, the limit of Brahman, Śaṃbhu, I bow,
the lord of Hiraṇyagarbha, the three-eyed.

1.31.s:
yataḥ prasūtirjagato vināśo
yenāvṛtaṃ sarvamidaṃ śivena /
taṃ brahmapāraṃ bhagavantamīśaṃ
praṇamya nityaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye //
1.31.d:
यतः प्रसूतिर्जगतो विनाशो
येनावृतं सर्वमिदं शिवेन ।
तं ब्रह्मपारं भगवन्तमीशं
प्रणम्य नित्यं शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
1.31.m:
From whom is the birth and destruction of the universe,
by whom, Śiva, all this is pervaded,
to that Lord, the ruler, the limit of Brahman,
bowing constantly, I fly for refuge.

1.31.s:
aliṅgamālokavihīnarūpaṃ
svayaṃprabhaṃ citpatimekarudram /
taṃ brahmapāraṃ parameśvaraṃ tvāṃ
namaskariṣye na yato 'nyadasti //
1.31.d:
अलिङ्गमालोकविहीनरूपं
स्वयंप्रभं चित्पतिमेकरुद्रम् ।
तं ब्रह्मपारं परमेश्वरं त्वां
नमस्करिष्ये न यतो ऽन्यदस्ति ॥
1.31.m:
Without a mark, whose form is devoid of light,
self-luminous, the lord of consciousness, the sole Rudra,
to you, the Supreme Lord, the limit of Brahman,
I will offer reverence, since there is none other than you.

1.31.s:
yaṃ yoginastyaktasabījayogā
labdhvā samādhiṃ paramārthabhūtāḥ /
paśyanti devaṃ praṇato 'smi nityaṃ
taṃ brahmapāraṃ bhavataḥ svarūpam //
1.31.d:
यं योगिनस्त्यक्तसबीजयोगा
लब्ध्वा समाधिं परमार्थभूताः ।
पश्यन्ति देवं प्रणतो ऽस्मि नित्यं
तं ब्रह्मपारं भवतः स्वरूपम् ॥
1.31.m:
Whom yogins who have abandoned seeded yoga,
having attained absorption, becoming reality itself,
behold as God, I am eternally bowed;
to that real form of yours, the limit of Brahman.

1.31.s:
na yatra nāmādiviśeṣakḷpti-
r na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati yatsvarūpam /
taṃ brahmapāraṃ praṇato 'smi nityaṃ
svayaṃbhuvaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye //
1.31.d:
न यत्र नामादिविशेषकॢप्ति-
र् न संदृशे तिष्ठति यत्स्वरूपम् ।
तं ब्रह्मपारं प्रणतो ऽस्मि नित्यं
स्वयंभुवं त्वां शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
1.31.m:
Where there is no conceptualisation of names and the like,
whose real form does not remain within sight,
to that limit of Brahman I am eternally bowed;
to you, the self-existent, I fly for refuge.

1.31.s:
yad vedavādābhiratā videhaṃ
sabrahmavijñānamabhedamekam /
paśyantyanekaṃ bhavataḥ svarūpaṃ
sabrahmapāraṃ praṇato 'smi nityam //
1.31.d:
यद् वेदवादाभिरता विदेहं
सब्रह्मविज्ञानमभेदमेकम् ।
पश्यन्त्यनेकं भवतः स्वरूपं
सब्रह्मपारं प्रणतो ऽस्मि नित्यम् ॥
1.31.m:
Whom those devoted to the teachings of the Veda behold
as bodiless, united with the knowledge of Brahman, non-different, the one
and manifold real form of yours,
to that with the limit of Brahman I am eternally bowed.

1.31.s:
yataḥ pradhānaṃ puruṣaḥ purāṇo
vivartate yaṃ praṇamanti devāḥ /
namāmi taṃ jyotiṣi saṃniviṣṭaṃ
kālaṃ bṛhantaṃ bhavataḥ svarūpam //
1.31.d:
यतः प्रधानं पुरुषः पुराणो
विवर्तते यं प्रणमन्ति देवाः ।
नमामि तं ज्योतिषि संनिविष्टं
कालं बृहन्तं भवतः स्वरूपम् ॥
1.31.m:
From whom primordial nature [and] the ancient spirit
evolve, to whom the gods bow down,
to that great Time seated in light,
the real form of yours, I bow.

1.31.s:
vrajāmi nityaṃ śaraṇaṃ guheśaṃ
sthāṇuṃ prapadye giriśaṃ purārim /
śivaṃ prapadye haramindumauliṃ
pinākinaṃ tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajāmi //
1.31.d:
व्रजामि नित्यं शरणं गुहेशं
स्थाणुं प्रपद्ये गिरिशं पुरारिम् ।
शिवं प्रपद्ये हरमिन्दुमौलिं
पिनाकिनं त्वां शरणं व्रजामि ॥

1.31.s:
stutvaivaṃ śaṅkukarṇo 'sau bhagavantaṃ kapardinam /
papāta daṇḍavad bhūmau proccaran praṇavaṃ param //
1.31.d:
स्तुत्वैवं शङ्कुकर्णो ऽसौ भगवन्तं कपर्दिनम् ।
पपात दण्डवद् भूमौ प्रोच्चरन् प्रणवं परम् ॥
1.31.m:
Having thus praised the Lord Kapardin,
Śaṅkukarṇa fell upon the ground like a staff,
uttering aloud the supreme Praṇava.

1.31.s:
tatkṣaṇāt paramaṃ liṅgaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ śivātmakam /
jñānamānandamadvaitaṃ koṭikālāgnisannibham //
1.31.d:
तत्क्षणात् परमं लिङ्गं प्रादुर्भूतं शिवात्मकम् ।
ज्ञानमानन्दमद्वैतं कोटिकालाग्निसन्निभम् ॥
1.31.m:
At that moment, a supreme liṅga appeared, whose nature is Śiva,
knowledge, bliss, non-dual,
resembling millions of fires of cosmic dissolution.

1.31.s:
śaṅkukarṇo 'tha muktātmā tadātmā sarvago 'malaḥ /
nililye vimale liṅge tadbhutamivābhavat //
1.31.d:
शङ्कुकर्णो ऽथ मुक्तात्मा तदात्मा सर्वगो ऽमलः ।
निलिल्ये विमले लिङ्गे तद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥

1.31.s:
etad rahasyamākhyātaṃ māhātmyaṃ vaḥ kapardinaḥ /
na kaścid vetti tamasā vidvānapyatra muhyati //
1.31.d:
एतद् रहस्यमाख्यातं माहात्म्यं वः कपर्दिनः ।
न कश्चिद् वेत्ति तमसा विद्वानप्यत्र मुह्यति ॥
1.31.m:
This secret greatness of Kapardin has been told to you;
no one knows it through ignorance, and even a learned man is bewildered here.

1.31.s:
ya imāṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm /
bhaktaḥ pāpaviśuddhātmā rudrasāmīpyamāpnuyāt //
1.31.d:
य इमां शृणुयान्नित्यं कथां पापप्रणाशिनीम् ।
भक्तः पापविशुद्धात्मा रुद्रसामीप्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.31.m:
Whoever constantly hears this story that destroys sins,
devoted, his soul purified from sins, would attain proximity to Rudra.

1.31.s:
paṭhecca satataṃ śuddho brahmapāraṃ mahāstavam /
prātarmadhyāhnasamaye sa yogaṃ prāpnuyāt param //
1.31.d:
पठेच्च सततं शुद्धो ब्रह्मपारं महास्तवम् ।
प्रातर्मध्याह्नसमये स योगं प्राप्नुयात् परम् ॥
1.31.m:
And whoever, purified, constantly recites this great hymn, the Brahmapāra,
at morning and noon time, shall attain supreme yoga.

1.31.s:
ihaiva nityaṃ vatsyāmo devadevaṃ kapardinam /
drakṣyāmaḥ satataṃ devaṃ pūjayāmo 'tha śūlinam //
1.31.d:
इहैव नित्यं वत्स्यामो देवदेवं कपर्दिनम् ।
द्रक्ष्यामः सततं देवं पूजयामो ऽथ शूलिनम् ॥
1.31.m:
“Here alone we shall dwell constantly with Kapardin, the god of gods;
we shall behold the god constantly and worship the wielder of the trident.”

1.31.s:
ityuktvā bhagavān vyāsaḥ śiṣyaiḥ saha mahāmuniḥ /
uvāsa tatra yuktātmā pūjayan vai kapardinam //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge ekatriśodhyāyaḥ
1.31.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् व्यासः शिष्यैः सह महामुनिः ।
उवास तत्र युक्तात्मा पूजयन् वै कपर्दिनम् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे एकत्रिशोध्यायः
1.31.m:
Having spoken thus, the Lord Vyāsa, the great sage, together with his disciples,
dwelt there with controlled mind, worshipping Kapardin.

Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.32.s:
sūta uvāca
uṣitvā tatra bhagavān kapardeśāntike punaḥ /
draṣṭuṃ yayau madhyameśaṃ bahuvarṣagaṇān prabhuḥ //
1.32.d:
सूत उवाच
उषित्वा तत्र भगवान् कपर्देशान्तिके पुनः ।
द्रष्टुं ययौ मध्यमेशं बहुवर्षगणान् प्रभुः ॥
1.32.m:
Sūta said:
Having dwelt there near Kapardeśa for a host of many years,
the lord, the venerable one, went again to see Madhyameśa.

1.32.s:
tatra mandākinīṃ puṇyāmṛṣisaṅganiṣevitām /
nadīṃ vimalapānīyāṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭo 'bhavanmuniḥ //
1.32.d:
तत्र मन्दाकिनीं पुण्यामृषिसङ्गनिषेविताम् ।
नदीं विमलपानीयां दृष्ट्वा हृष्टो ऽभवन्मुनिः ॥
1.32.m:
Seeing the holy Mandākinī river there, frequented by hosts of sages,
having clear waters, the sage was delighted.

1.32.s:
sa tāmanvīkṣya munibhiḥ saha dvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ /
cakāra bhāvapūtātmā snānaṃ snānavidhānavit //
1.32.d:
स तामन्वीक्ष्य मुनिभिः सह द्वैपायनः प्रभुः ।
चकार भावपूतात्मा स्नानं स्नानविधानवित् ॥
1.32.m:
Looking upon it together with the sages, the lord Dvaipāyana,
his soul purified by devotion, knowing the rules of bathing, bathed.

1.32.s:
saṃtarpya vidhivad devānṛṣīn pitṛgaṇāṃstathā /
pūjayāmāsa lokādiṃ puṣpairnānāvidhairbhavam //
1.32.d:
संतर्प्य विधिवद् देवानृषीन् पितृगणांस्तथा ।
पूजयामास लोकादिं पुष्पैर्नानाविधैर्भवम् ॥
1.32.m:
Having duly offered water to the gods, the sages, and the hosts of ancestors,
he worshipped Bhava, the source of the world, with various kinds of flowers.

1.32.s:
praviśya śiṣyapravaraiḥ sārdhaṃ satyavatīsutaḥ /
madhyameśvaramīśānamarcayāmāsa śūlinam //
1.32.d:
प्रविश्य शिष्यप्रवरैः सार्धं सत्यवतीसुतः ।
मध्यमेश्वरमीशानमर्चयामास शूलिनम् ॥
1.32.m:
Entering together with his excellent disciples, the son of Satyavatī
worshipped Īśāna, Madhyameśvara, the wielder of the trident.

1.32.s:
tataḥ pāśupatāḥ śāntā bhasmoddhūlitavigrahāḥ /
draṣṭuṃ samāgatā rudraṃ madhyameśvaramīśvaram //
1.32.d:
ततः पाशुपताः शान्ता भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहाः ।
द्रष्टुं समागता रुद्रं मध्यमेश्वरमीश्वरम् ॥
1.32.m:
Then Pāśupatas, peaceful, their bodies smeared with ashes,
came to see Rudra, the Lord Madhyameśvara.

1.32.s:
oṅkārāsaktamanaso vedādhyayanatatparāḥ /
jaṭilā muṇḍitāścāpi śuklayajñopavītinaḥ //
1.32.d:
ओङ्कारासक्तमनसो वेदाध्ययनतत्पराः ।
जटिला मुण्डिताश्चापि शुक्लयज्ञोपवीतिनः ॥
1.32.m:
Their minds were attached to the syllable Oṃ, devoted to the study of the Vedas;
some had matted hair, some were shaved, and they wore white sacred threads.

1.32.s:
kaupīnavasanāḥ kecidapare cāpyavāsasaḥ /
brahmacaryaratāḥ śāntā vedāntajñānatatparāḥ //
1.32.d:
कौपीनवसनाः केचिदपरे चाप्यवाससः ।
ब्रह्मचर्यरताः शान्ता वेदान्तज्ञानतत्पराः ॥
1.32.m:
Some wore loincloths, and others were naked;
devoted to celibacy, peaceful, intent upon the knowledge of the Vedānta.

1.32.s:
dṛṣṭvā dvaipāyanaṃ viprāḥ śiṣyaiḥ parivṛtaṃ munim /
pūjayitvā yathānyāyamidaṃ vacanamabruvan //
1.32.d:
दृष्ट्वा द्वैपायनं विप्राः शिष्यैः परिवृतं मुनिम् ।
पूजयित्वा यथान्यायमिदं वचनमब्रुवन् ॥
1.32.m:
Seeing the sage Dvaipāyana surrounded by his disciples, the brahmins,
having worshipped him according to rule, spoke these words:

1.32.s:
ko bhavān kuta āyātaḥ saha śiṣyairmahāmune /
procuḥ pailādayaḥ śiṣyāstānṛṣīn brahmabhāvitān //
1.32.d:
को भवान् कुत आयातः सह शिष्यैर्महामुने ।
प्रोचुः पैलादयः शिष्यास्तानृषीन् ब्रह्मभावितान् ॥
1.32.m:
“Who are you, and whence have you come together with your disciples, O great sage?”
Paila and the other disciples replied to those sages contemplating Brahman:

1.32.s:
ayaṃ satyavatīsūnuḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano muniḥ /
vyāsaḥ svayaṃ hṛṣīkeśo yena vedāḥ pṛthak kṛtāḥ //
1.32.d:
अयं सत्यवतीसूनुः कृष्णद्वैपायनो मुनिः ।
व्यासः स्वयं हृषीकेशो येन वेदाः पृथक् कृताः ॥
1.32.m: This sage is Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, the son of Satyavatī, / Vyāsa, Hṛṣīkeśa himself, by whom the Vedas were divided.

1.32.s:
yasya devo mahādevaḥ sākṣādeva pinākadhṛk /
aṃśāṃśenābhavat putro nāmnā śuka iti prabhuḥ //
1.32.d:
यस्य देवो महादेवः साक्षादेव पिनाकधृक् ।
अंशांशेनाभवत् पुत्रो नाम्ना शुक इति प्रभुः ॥
1.32.m: The god Mahādeva himself, the wielder of the Pināka bow, / became his powerful son named Śuka by a portion of a portion.

1.32.s:
yaḥ sa sākṣānmahādevaṃ sarvabhāvena śaṅkaram /
prapannaḥ parayā bhaktyā yasya tajjñānamaiśvaram //
1.32.d:
यः स साक्षान्महादेवं सर्वभावेन शङ्करम् ।
प्रपन्नः परया भक्त्या यस्य तज्ज्ञानमैश्वरम् ॥
1.32.m: He took refuge in Mahādeva, Śaṅkara, directly with all his being, / through supreme devotion, whose sovereign knowledge that is.

1.32.s:
tataḥ pāśupatāḥ sarve hṛṣṭasarvatanūruhāḥ /
nemuravyagramanasaḥ procuḥ satyavatīsutam //
1.32.d:
ततः पाशुपताः सर्वे हृष्टसर्वतनूरुहाः ।
नेमुरव्यग्रमनसः प्रोचुः सत्यवतीसुतम् ॥
1.32.m: Then all the Pāśupatas, with every hair on their bodies standing on end with joy, / bowed with steady minds and addressed the son of Satyavatī:

1.32.s:
bhagavan bhavatā jñātaṃ vijñānaṃ parameṣṭhinaḥ /
prisādād devadevasya yat tanmāheśvaraṃ param //
1.32.d:
भगवन् भवता ज्ञातं विज्ञानं परमेष्ठिनः ।
प्रिसादाद् देवदेवस्य यत् तन्माहेश्वरं परम् ॥
1.32.m: “O blessed one, by you is known the higher wisdom of the supreme Lord, / that supreme wisdom relating to Maheśvara, through the grace of the God of gods.

1.32.s:
tadvadāsmākamavyaktaṃ rahasyaṃ guhyamuttamam /
kṣipraṃ paśyema taṃ devaṃ śrutvā bhagavato mukhāt //
1.32.d:
तद्वदास्माकमव्यक्तं रहस्यं गुह्यमुत्तमम् ।
क्षिप्रं पश्येम तं देवं श्रुत्वा भगवतो मुखात् ॥
1.32.m: Tell us that unmanifest, supreme, secret mystery, / so that having heard it from the blessed one’s mouth we may swiftly behold that God.”

1.32.s:
visarjayitvā tāñchiṣyān sumantupramukhāṃstataḥ /
provāca tatparaṃ jñānaṃ yogibhyo yogavittamaḥ //
1.32.d:
विसर्जयित्वा ताञ्छिष्यान् सुमन्तुप्रमुखांस्ततः ।
प्रोवाच तत्परं ज्ञानं योगिभ्यो योगवित्तमः ॥
1.32.m: Having dismissed those disciples led by Sumantu, / the greatest knower of yoga proclaimed that supreme knowledge to the yogins.

1.32.s:
tatkṣaṇādeva vimalaṃ saṃbhūtaṃ jyotiruttamam /
līnāstatraiva te viprāḥ kṣaṇādantaradhīyata //
1.32.d:
तत्क्षणादेव विमलं संभूतं ज्योतिरुत्तमम् ।
लीनास्तत्रैव ते विप्राः क्षणादन्तरधीयत ॥
1.32.m: At that very moment a spotless, supreme light arose; / the twice-born were absorbed right there, and in a moment it vanished.

1.32.s:
tataḥ śiṣyān samāhūya bhagavān brahmavittamaḥ /
provāca madhyameśasya māhātmyaṃ pailapūrvakān //
1.32.d:
ततः शिष्यान् समाहूय भगवान् ब्रह्मवित्तमः ।
प्रोवाच मध्यमेशस्य माहात्म्यं पैलपूर्वकान् ॥
1.32.m: Then, summoning his disciples led by Paila, the blessed one, / the greatest knower of Brahman, declared the majesty of Madhyameśa:

1.32.s:
asmin sthāne svayaṃ devo devyā saha maheśvaraḥ /
ramate bhagavān nityaṃ rudraiśca parivāritaḥ //
1.32.d:
अस्मिन् स्थाने स्वयं देवो देव्या सह महेश्वरः ।
रमते भगवान् नित्यं रुद्रैश्च परिवारितः ॥
1.32.m: “In this place, the blessed Lord Maheśvara himself, together with the Goddess, / constantly takes delight, surrounded by the Rudras.

1.32.s:
atra pūrvaṃ hṛṣīkeśo viśvātmā devakīsutaḥ /
uvāsa vatsaraṃ kṛṣṇaḥ sadā pāśupatairvṛtaḥ //
1.32.d:
अत्र पूर्वं हृषीकेशो विश्वात्मा देवकीसुतः ।
उवास वत्सरं कृष्णः सदा पाशुपतैर्वृतः ॥
1.32.m: Here formerly Hṛṣīkeśa Kṛṣṇa, the Soul of All, the son of Devakī, / dwelt for a year, constantly surrounded by Pāśupatas.

1.32.s:
bhasmoddhūlitasarvāṅgo rudrādhyayanatatparaḥ /
ārādhayan hariḥ śaṃbhuṃ kṛtvā pāśupataṃ vratam //
1.32.d:
भस्मोद्धूलितसर्वाङ्गो रुद्राध्ययनतत्परः ।
आराधयन् हरिः शंभुं कृत्वा पाशुपतं व्रतम् ॥
1.32.m: His whole body smeared with ashes, intent on reciting the Rudra hymns, / Hari worshipped Śambhu after undertaking the Pāśupata vow.

1.32.s:
tasya te bahavaḥ śiṣyā brahmacaryaparāyaṇāḥ /
labdhvā tadvacanājjñānaṃ dṛṣṭavanto maheśvaram //
1.32.d:
तस्य ते बहवः शिष्या ब्रह्मचर्यपरायणाः ।
लब्ध्वा तद्वचनाज्ज्ञानं दृष्टवन्तो महेश्वरम् ॥
1.32.m: His many disciples, devoted to celibacy, / having obtained knowledge from his words, beheld Maheśvara.

1.32.s:
tasya devo mahādevaḥ pratyakṣaṃ nīlalohitaḥ /
dadau kṛṣṇāsya bhagavāna varado varamuttamam //
1.32.d:
तस्य देवो महादेवः प्रत्यक्षं नीललोहितः ।
ददौ कृष्णास्य भगवान वरदो वरमुत्तमम् ॥
1.32.m: To him the blessed god Mahādeva, the blue-throated red one, / visibly appeared as the granter of boons and gave an excellent boon to Kṛṣṇa:

1.32.s:
yer'cayiṣyanti govindaṃ madbhaktā vidhipūrvakam /
teṣāṃ tadaiśvaraṃ jñānamutpatsyati jaganmaya //
1.32.d:
येर्ऽचयिष्यन्ति गोविन्दं मद्भक्ता विधिपूर्वकम् ।
तेषां तदैश्वरं ज्ञानमुत्पत्स्यति जगन्मय ॥
1.32.m: ‘Those devotees of mine who will worship Govinda according to the rules, / in them that sovereign knowledge will arise, O you who embody the world!

1.32.s:
namasyor'cayitavyaśca dhyātavyo matparairjanaiḥ /
bhaviṣyasi na saṃdeho matprasādād dvijātibhiḥ //
1.32.d:
नमस्योर्ऽचयितव्यश्च ध्यातव्यो मत्परैर्जनैः ।
भविष्यसि न संदेहो मत्प्रसादाद् द्विजातिभिः ॥
1.32.m: You shall be bowed to, worshipped, and meditated upon by people devoted to me, / by the twice-born through my grace; of this there is no doubt.

1.32.s:
ye 'tra drakṣyanti deveśaṃ snātvā rudraṃ pinākinam /
brahmahatyādikaṃ pāpaṃ teṣāmāśu vinaśyati //
1.32.d:
ये ऽत्र द्रक्ष्यन्ति देवेशं स्नात्वा रुद्रं पिनाकिनम् ।
ब्रह्महत्यादिकं पापं तेषामाशु विनश्यति ॥
1.32.m: Those who, having bathed here, behold Rudra, the wielder of the Pināka, the Lord of gods, / their sins such as the killing of a brahmin are swiftly destroyed.

1.32.s:
prāṇāṃstyajanti ye martyāḥ pāpakarmaratā api /
te yānti tat paraṃ sthānaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
1.32.d:
प्राणांस्त्यजन्ति ये मर्त्याः पापकर्मरता अपि ।
ते यान्ति तत् परं स्थानं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
1.32.m: The mortals who cast off their vital breaths [here], even if attached to sinful deeds, / they go to that supreme abode; there is no deliberation needed on this.

1.32.s:
dhanyāstu khalu te viprā mandākinyāṃ kṛtodakāḥ /
arcayanti mahādevaṃ madhyameśvaramīśvaram //
1.32.d:
धन्यास्तु खलु ते विप्रा मन्दाकिन्यां कृतोदकाः ।
अर्चयन्ति महादेवं मध्यमेश्वरमीश्वरम् ॥
1.32.m: Fortunate indeed are those twice-born who, having performed water-rites in the Mandākinī, / worship the Lord, Mahādeva, Madhyameśvara.

1.32.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ tapaḥ śrāddhaṃ piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ tviha /
ekaikaśaḥ kṛtaṃ viprāḥ punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam //
1.32.d:
स्नानं दानं तपः श्राद्धं पिण्डनिर्वपणं त्विह ।
एकैकशः कृतं विप्राः पुनात्यासप्तमं कुलम् ॥
1.32.m: Bathing, gift-giving, austerity, ancestral offering rites, and the offering of rice-balls, / each performed here, O twice-born, purifies the family up to the seventh generation.

1.32.s:
saṃnihatyāmupaspṛśya rāhugraste divākare /
yat phalaṃ labhate martyastasmād daśaguṇaṃ tviha //
1.32.d:
संनिहत्यामुपस्पृश्य राहुग्रस्ते दिवाकरे ।
यत् फलं लभते मर्त्यस्तस्माद् दशगुणं त्विह ॥
1.32.m: Whatever fruit a mortal attains by sipping water at Saṃnihitī / when the sun is seized by Rāhu, ten times that is gained here.’

1.32.s:
evamuktvā mahāyogī madhyameśānti ke prabhuḥ /
uvāsa suciraṃ kālaṃ pūjayan vai maheśvaram //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge dvātriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.32.d:
एवमुक्त्वा महायोगी मध्यमेशान्ति के प्रभुः ।
उवास सुचिरं कालं पूजयन् वै महेश्वरम् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे द्वात्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.32.m:
Having spoken thus, the master, the great yogin, dwelt for a very long time / near Madhyameśa, indeed worshipping Maheśvara.

Thus ends the thirty-second chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.33.s:
sūta uvāca
tataḥ sarvāṇi guhyāni tīrthānyāyatanāni ca /
jagāma bhagavān vyāso jaiminipramukhairvṛtaḥ //
1.33.d:
सूत उवाच
ततः सर्वाणि गुह्यानि तीर्थान्यायतनानि च ।
जगाम भगवान् व्यासो जैमिनिप्रमुखैर्वृतः ॥
1.33.m: Sūta said: / Then the blessed Vyāsa, surrounded by [disciples] led by Jaimini, / went to all the secret sacred bathing places and shrines:

1.33.s:
prayāgaṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ prayāgādadhikaṃ śubham /
viśvarūpaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ tālatīrthamanuttamam //
1.33.d:
प्रयागं परमं तीर्थं प्रयागादधिकं शुभम् ।
विश्वरूपं तथा तीर्थं तालतीर्थमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.33.m: The supreme sacred bathing place Prayāga, and the auspicious one superior to Prayāga, / likewise the sacred bathing place Viśvarūpa, and the unsurpassed Tālatīrtha;

1.33.s:
ākāśākhyaṃ mahātīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ caivārṣabhaṃ param /
svarnolaṃ ca mahātīrthaṃ gaurītīrthamanuttamam //
1.33.d:
आकाशाख्यं महातीर्थं तीर्थं चैवार्षभं परम् ।
स्वर्नोलं च महातीर्थं गौरीतीर्थमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.33.m: the great sacred bathing place named Ākāśa, and the supreme sacred bathing place Ārṣabha, / the great sacred bathing place Svarnola, and the unsurpassed Gaurītīrtha;

1.33.s:
prājāpatyaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ svargadvāraṃ tathaiva ca /
jambukeśvaramityuktaṃ dharmākhyaṃ tīrthamuttamam //
1.33.d:
प्राजापत्यं तथा तीर्थं स्वर्गद्वारं तथैव च ।
जम्बुकेश्वरमित्युक्तं धर्माख्यं तीर्थमुत्तमम् ॥
1.33.m: likewise the sacred bathing place Prājāpatya, and also Svargadvāra, / the one named Jambukeśvara, and the excellent sacred bathing place called Dharma;

1.33.s:
gayātīrthaṃ mahātīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ caiva mahānadī /
nārāyaṇaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ vāyutīrthamanuttamam //
1.33.d:
गयातीर्थं महातीर्थं तीर्थं चैव महानदी ।
नारायणं परं तीर्थं वायुतीर्थमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.33.m: the great sacred bathing place Gayātīrtha, and the sacred bathing place Mahānadī, / the supreme sacred bathing place Nārāyaṇa, and the unsurpassed Vāyutīrtha;

1.33.s:
jñānatīrthaṃ paraṃ guhyaṃ vārāhaṃ tīrthamuttamam /
yamatīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ tīrthaṃ saṃvartakaṃ śubham //
1.33.d:
ज्ञानतीर्थं परं गुह्यं वाराहं तीर्थमुत्तमम् ।
यमतीर्थं महापुण्यं तीर्थं संवर्तकं शुभम् ॥
1.33.m: the supreme, secret Jñānatīrtha, the excellent sacred bathing place Vārāha, / the greatly holy Yamatīrtha, and the auspicious sacred bathing place Saṃvartaka;

1.33.s:
agnitīrthaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ kalaśeśvaramuttamam /
nāgatīrthaṃ somatīrthaṃ sūryatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca //
1.33.d:
अग्नितीर्थं द्विजश्रेष्ठाः कलशेश्वरमुत्तमम् ।
नागतीर्थं सोमतीर्थं सूर्यतीर्थं तथैव च ॥
1.33.m: Agnitīrtha, O best of the twice-born, the excellent Kalaśeśvara, / Nāgatīrtha, Somatīrtha, and likewise Sūryatīrtha;

1.33.s:
parvatākhyaṃ mahāguhyaṃ maṇikarṇamanuttamam /
ghaṭotkacaṃ tīrthavaraṃ śrītīrthaṃ ca pitāmaham //
1.33.d:
पर्वताख्यं महागुह्यं मणिकर्णमनुत्तमम् ।
घटोत्कचं तीर्थवरं श्रीतीर्थं च पितामहम् ॥
1.33.m: the greatly secret one named Parvata, the unsurpassed Maṇikarṇa, / the superior sacred bathing place Ghaṭotkaca, Śrītīrtha, and Pitāmaha;

1.33.s:
gaṅgātīrthaṃ tu deveśaṃ yayātestīrthamuttamam /
kāpilaṃ caiva someśaṃ brahmatīrthamanuttamam //
1.33.d:
गङ्गातीर्थं तु देवेशं ययातेस्तीर्थमुत्तमम् ।
कापिलं चैव सोमेशं ब्रह्मतीर्थमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.33.m: Gaṅgātīrtha, Deveśa, the excellent sacred bathing place of Yayāti, / Kāpila, Someśa, and the unsurpassed Brahmatīrtha.

1.33.s:
atra liṅgaṃ purānīya brahmā snātuṃ yadā gataḥ /
tadānīṃ sthāpayāmāsa viṣṇustalliṅgamaiśvaram //
1.33.d:
अत्र लिङ्गं पुरानीय ब्रह्मा स्नातुं यदा गतः ।
तदानीं स्थापयामास विष्णुस्तल्लिङ्गमैश्वरम् ॥
1.33.m: Formerly, having brought a liṅga here, when Brahmā went to bathe, / at that time Viṣṇu installed that sovereign liṅga.

1.33.s:
tataḥ snātvā samāgatya brahmā provāca taṃ harim /
mayānītamidaṃ liṅgaṃ kasmāt sthāpitavānasi //
1.33.d:
ततः स्नात्वा समागत्य ब्रह्मा प्रोवाच तं हरिम् ।
मयानीतमिदं लिङ्गं कस्मात् स्थापितवानसि ॥
1.33.m: Then Brahmā, having bathed and returned, said to that Hari: / “Why have you installed this liṅga brought by me?”

1.33.s:
tamāha viṣṇustvatto 'pi rudre bhaktirdṛḍhā mama /
tasmāt pratiṣṭhitaṃ liṅgaṃnāmnā tava bhaviṣyati //
1.33.d:
तमाह विष्णुस्त्वत्तो ऽपि रुद्रे भक्तिर्दृढा मम ।
तस्मात् प्रतिष्ठितं लिङ्गंनाम्ना तव भविष्यति ॥
1.33.m: Viṣṇu said to him: “My devotion to Rudra is firmer even than yours; / therefore the installed liṅga shall be named after you.”

1.33.s:
bhūteśvaraṃ tathā tīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ dharmasamudbhavam /
gandharvatīrthaṃ paramaṃ vāhneyaṃ tīrthamuttamam //
1.33.d:
भूतेश्वरं तथा तीर्थं तीर्थं धर्मसमुद्भवम् ।
गन्धर्वतीर्थं परमं वाह्नेयं तीर्थमुत्तमम् ॥
1.33.m: Likewise the sacred bathing place Bhūteśvara, the sacred bathing place Dharmasamudbhava, / the supreme Gandharvatīrtha, and the excellent sacred bathing place Vāhneya;

1.33.s:
daurvāsikaṃ vyomatīrthaṃ candratīrthaṃ dvijottamāḥ /
citrāṅgadeśvaraṃ puṇyaṃ puṇyaṃ vidyādhareśvaram //
1.33.d:
दौर्वासिकं व्योमतीर्थं चन्द्रतीर्थं द्विजोत्तमाः ।
चित्राङ्गदेश्वरं पुण्यं पुण्यं विद्याधरेश्वरम् ॥
1.33.m: Daurvāsika, Vyomatīrtha, and Candratīrtha, O best of the twice-born, / the holy Citrāṅgadeśvara, and the holy Vidyādhareśvara;

1.33.s:
kedāratīrthamugrākhyaṃ kālañjaramanuttamam /
sārasvataṃ prabhāsaṃ ca bhadrakarṇaṃ hradaṃ śubham //
1.33.d:
केदारतीर्थमुग्राख्यं कालञ्जरमनुत्तमम् ।
सारस्वतं प्रभासं च भद्रकर्णं ह्रदं शुभम् ॥
1.33.m: the sacred bathing place Kedāra, the one named Ugra, the unsurpassed Kālañjara, / Sārasvata, Prabhāsa, and the auspicious Bhadrakarṇa pool;

1.33.s:
laukikākhyaṃ mahātīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ caiva vṛṣadhvajam /
hiraṇyagarbhaṃ goprekṣyaṃ tīrthaṃ caiva vṛṣadhvajam //
1.33.d:
लौकिकाख्यं महातीर्थं तीर्थं चैव वृषध्वजम् ।
हिरण्यगर्भं गोप्रेक्ष्यं तीर्थं चैव वृषध्वजम् ॥
1.33.m: the great sacred bathing place named Laukika, and the sacred bathing place Vṛṣadhvaja, / Hiraṇyagarbha, Goprekṣya, and the sacred bathing place Vṛṣadhvaja;

1.33.s:
upaśāntaṃ śivaṃ caiva vyāghreśvaramanuttamam /
trilocanaṃ mahātīrthaṃ lolārkaṃ cottarāhvayam //
1.33.d:
उपशान्तं शिवं चैव व्याघ्रेश्वरमनुत्तमम् ।
त्रिलोचनं महातीर्थं लोलार्कं चोत्तराह्वयम् ॥
1.33.m: Upaśānta, Śiva, and the unsurpassed Vyāghreśvara, / the great sacred bathing place Trilocana, and Lolārka, also called Uttara;

1.33.s:
kapālamocanaṃ tīrthaṃ brahmahatyāvināśanam /
śukreśvaraṃ mahāpuṇyamānandapuramuttamam //
1.33.d:
कपालमोचनं तीर्थं ब्रह्महत्याविनाशनम् ।
शुक्रेश्वरं महापुण्यमानन्दपुरमुत्तमम् ॥
1.33.m: the sacred bathing place Kapālamocana, which destroys [the sin of] brahmin-slaughter, / the greatly holy Śukreśvara, and the excellent Ānandapura.

1.33.s:
evamādīni tīrthāni prādhānyāt kathitāni tu /
na śakyaṃ vistarād vaktuṃ tīrthasaṃkhyā dvijāttamāḥ //
1.33.d:
एवमादीनि तीर्थानि प्राधान्यात् कथितानि तु ।
न शक्यं विस्तराद् वक्तुं तीर्थसंख्या द्विजात्तमाः ॥
1.33.m: These and other sacred bathing places have been spoken of according to their prominence; / it is not possible to state the full number of sacred bathing places in detail, O best of twice-born.

1.33.s:
teṣu sarveṣu tīrtheṣu snātvābhyarcya pinākinam /
upoṣya tatra tatrāsau pārāśaryo mahāmuniḥ //
1.33.d:
तेषु सर्वेषु तीर्थेषु स्नात्वाभ्यर्च्य पिनाकिनम् ।
उपोष्य तत्र तत्रासौ पाराशर्यो महामुनिः ॥
1.33.m: Having bathed in all those sacred bathing places, worshipped the wielder of the Pināka, / and fasted in each of those places, that great sage, the son of Parāśara,

1.33.s:
tarpayitvā pitṝn devān kṛtvā piṇḍapridānakam /
jagāma punarevāpi yatra viśveśvaraḥ śivaḥ //
1.33.d:
तर्पयित्वा पितॄन् देवान् कृत्वा पिण्डप्रिदानकम् ।
जगाम पुनरेवापि यत्र विश्वेश्वरः शिवः ॥
1.33.m: having offered libations to the ancestors and gods, and made offerings of rice-balls, / went back once again to where Viśveśvara Śiva is.

1.33.s:
snātvābhyarcya paraṃ liṅgaṃ śiṣyaiḥ saha mahāmuniḥ /
uvāca śiṣyān dharmātmā svān deśān gantumarhathā //
1.33.d:
स्नात्वाभ्यर्च्य परं लिङ्गं शिष्यैः सह महामुनिः ।
उवाच शिष्यान् धर्मात्मा स्वान् देशान् गन्तुमर्हथा ॥
1.33.m: Having bathed and worshipped the supreme liṅga together with his disciples, / the righteous-minded great sage said to his disciples: “You should go to your own lands.”

1.33.s:
te praṇamya mahātmānaṃ jagmuḥ pailādayo dvijāḥ /
vāsaṃ ca tatra niyato vārāṇasyāṃ cakāra saḥ //
1.33.d:
ते प्रणम्य महात्मानं जग्मुः पैलादयो द्विजाः ।
वासं च तत्र नियतो वाराणस्यां चकार सः ॥
1.33.m: Having bowed to the great-souled one, those twice-born led by Paila departed, / and he made his fixed abode right there in Vārāṇasī.

1.33.s:
śānto dāntastriṣavaṇaṃsnātvābhyarcya pinākinam /
bhaikṣāhāro viśuddhātmā brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.33.d:
शान्तो दान्तस्त्रिषवणंस्नात्वाभ्यर्च्य पिनाकिनम् ।
भैक्षाहारो विशुद्धात्मा ब्रह्मचर्यपरायणः ॥
1.33.m:
Calm, self-controlled, bathing at the three junctures of the day, worshipping the wielder of the Pināka,
living on alms, pure in mind, devoted to celibacy,

1.33.s:
kadācid vasatā tatra vyāsenāmitatejasā /
bhramamāṇena bhikṣā tu naiva labdhā dvijottamāḥ //
1.33.d:
कदाचिद् वसता तत्र व्यासेनामिततेजसा ।
भ्रममाणेन भिक्षा तु नैव लब्धा द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.33.m:
once, as Vyāsa of immeasurable splendour was living there,
wandering about, O best of the twice-born, he obtained no alms at all.

1.33.s:
tataḥ krodhāvṛtatanurnarāṇāmiha vāsinām /
vighnaṃ sṛjāmi sarveṣāṃ yena siddhirvihīyate //
1.33.d:
ततः क्रोधावृततनुर्नराणामिह वासिनाम् ।
विघ्नं सृजामि सर्वेषां येन सिद्धिर्विहीयते ॥
1.33.m:
Then, his body overcome by anger, [he thought]: "For the men dwelling here,
I shall create an obstacle for them all, whereby their spiritual attainment is ruined."

1.33.s:
tatkṣaṇe sā mahādevī śaṅkarārdhaśarīriṇī /
prādurāsīt svayaṃ prītyā veṣaṃ kṛtvā tu mānuṣam //
1.33.d:
तत्क्षणे सा महादेवी शङ्करार्धशरीरिणी ।
प्रादुरासीत् स्वयं प्रीत्या वेषं कृत्वा तु मानुषम् ॥
1.33.m:
At that instant the Great Goddess herself, making up half the body of Śaṅkara,
appeared out of affection, assuming a human form.

1.33.s:
bho bho vyāsa mahābuddhe śaptavyā bhavatā na hi /
gṛhāṇa bhikṣāṃ mattastvamuktvaivaṃ pradadau śivā //
1.33.d:
भो भो व्यास महाबुद्धे शप्तव्या भवता न हि ।
गृहाण भिक्षां मत्तस्त्वमुक्त्वैवं प्रददौ शिवा ॥
1.33.m:
"O Vyāsa of great intellect, you must not curse!
Accept alms from me." Having spoken thus, Śivā gave [them to him].

1.33.s:
uvāca ca mahādevī krodhanastvaṃ bhavān yataḥ /
iha kṣetre na vastavyaṃ kṛtaghno 'si tvayā sadā //
1.33.d:
उवाच च महादेवी क्रोधनस्त्वं भवान् यतः ।
इह क्षेत्रे न वस्तव्यं कृतघ्नो ऽसि त्वया सदा ॥
1.33.m:
And the Great Goddess said: "Since you are wrathful,
you must not dwell in this sacred field. You have ever been ungrateful."

1.33.s:
evamuktaḥ sa bhagavān dhyānājjñātvā parāṃ śivām /
uvāca praṇato bhūtvā stutvā ca pravaraiḥ stavaiḥ //
1.33.d:
एवमुक्तः स भगवान् ध्यानाज्ज्ञात्वा परां शिवाम् ।
उवाच प्रणतो भूत्वा स्तुत्वा च प्रवरैः स्तवैः ॥
1.33.m:
Spoken to thus, the blessed one, knowing through meditation that she was the supreme Śivā,
bowed down, praised her with the finest hymns of praise, and said:

1.33.s:
caturdaśyāmathāṣṭamyāṃ praveśaṃ dehi śāṅkari /
evamastvityanujñāya devī cāntaradhīyata //
1.33.d:
चतुर्दश्यामथाष्टम्यां प्रवेशं देहि शाङ्करि ।
एवमस्त्वित्यनुज्ञाय देवी चान्तरधीयत ॥
1.33.m:
"Grant me entry on the fourteenth day and on the eighth, O Śāṅkarī!"
Consenting with "May it be so," the goddess disappeared.

1.33.s:
evaṃ sa bhagavān vyāso mahāyogī purātanaḥ /
jñātvā kṣetraguṇān sarvān sthitastasyātha pārśvataḥ //
1.33.d:
एवं स भगवान् व्यासो महायोगी पुरातनः ।
ज्ञात्वा क्षेत्रगुणान् सर्वान् स्थितस्तस्याथ पार्श्वतः ॥
1.33.m:
Thus the blessed Vyāsa, the ancient great yogin,
knowing all the virtues of the sacred field, stayed on its perimeter.

1.33.s:
evaṃ vyāsaṃ sthitaṃ jñātvā kṣetraṃ sevanti paṇḍitāḥ /
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena vārāṇasyāṃ vasennaraḥ //
1.33.d:
एवं व्यासं स्थितं ज्ञात्वा क्षेत्रं सेवन्ति पण्डिताः ।
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन वाराणस्यां वसेन्नरः ॥
1.33.m:
Knowing that Vyāsa stays thus, wise men resort to the sacred field.
Therefore, with every effort, a man should dwell in Vārāṇasī.

1.33.s:
sūta uvāca
yaḥ paṭhedavimuktasya māhātmyaṃ śṛṇuyādapi /
śrāvayed vā dvijān śāntān so 'piyātiparāṅgatim //
1.33.d:
सूत उवाच
यः पठेदविमुक्तस्य माहात्म्यं शृणुयादपि ।
श्रावयेद् वा द्विजान् शान्तान् सो ऽपियातिपराङ्गतिम् ॥
1.33.m:
Sūta said:
Whoever reads the majesty of Avimukta, or even listens to it,
or recites it to calm twice-born men, he too goes to the supreme state.

1.33.s:
śrāddhe vā daivike kārye rātrāvahani vā dvijāḥ /
nadīnāṃ caiva tīreṣu devatāyataneṣu ca //
1.33.d:
श्राद्धे वा दैविके कार्ये रात्रावहनि वा द्विजाः ।
नदीनां चैव तीरेषु देवतायतनेषु च ॥
1.33.m:
At an ancestral offering rite or in a ritual for the gods, by night or by day, O twice-born ones,
and on the banks of rivers and in shrines of deities,

1.33.s:
snātvā samāhitamanā dambhamātsaryavarjitaḥ /
japedīśaṃ namaskṛtya sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge trayastriśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.33.d:
स्नात्वा समाहितमना दम्भमात्सर्यवर्जितः ।
जपेदीशं नमस्कृत्य स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे त्रयस्त्रिशो ऽध्यायः
1.33.m:
having bathed with concentrated mind, free from deceit and envy,
whoever recites [it], bowing to the Lord, attains the supreme state.

Thus ends the thirty-third chapter in the former section of the holy Kūrma Purāṇa, in the compilation of six thousand verses.

1.34.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
māhātmyamavimuktasya yathāvat tadudīritam /
idānīṃ tu prayāgasya māhātmyaṃ brūhi suvrata //
1.34.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
माहात्म्यमविमुक्तस्य यथावत् तदुदीरितम् ।
इदानीं तु प्रयागस्य माहात्म्यं ब्रूहि सुव्रत ॥
1.34.m:
The sages said:
The majesty of Avimukta has been proclaimed in full.
Now tell us, O one of good vows, the majesty of Prayāga.

1.34.s:
yāni tīrthāni tatraiva viśrutāni mahānti vai /
idānīṃ kathayāsmākaṃ sūta sarvārthavid bhavān //
1.34.d:
यानि तीर्थानि तत्रैव विश्रुतानि महान्ति वै ।
इदानीं कथयास्माकं सूत सर्वार्थविद् भवान् ॥
1.34.m:
Whatever great and famed sacred bathing places exist right there,
tell those to us now, O Sūta, for you know all subjects.

1.34.s:
sūta uvāca
śṛṇudhvamṛṣayaḥ sarve vistareṇa bravīmi vaḥ /
prayāgasya ca māhātmyaṃ yatra devaḥ pitāmahaḥ //
1.34.d:
सूत उवाच
शृणुध्वमृषयः सर्वे विस्तरेण ब्रवीमि वः ।
प्रयागस्य च माहात्म्यं यत्र देवः पितामहः ॥
1.34.m:
Sūta said:
Listen, all you sages; I shall tell you in detail
the majesty of Prayāga, where the divine Grandfather dwells.

1.34.s:
mārkaṇḍeyena kathitaṃ kaunteyāya mahātmane /
yathā yudhiṣṭhirāyaitat tadvakṣye bhavatāmaham //
1.34.d:
मार्कण्डेयेन कथितं कौन्तेयाय महात्मने ।
यथा युधिष्ठिरायैतत् तद्वक्ष्ये भवतामहम् ॥
1.34.m:
As it was told by Mārkaṇḍeya to the magnanimous son of Kuntī,
to Yudhiṣṭhira, so shall I tell it to you.

1.34.s:
nihatya kauravāna sarvān bhrātṛbhiḥ saha pārthivaḥ /
śokena mahātāviṣṭā mumoha sa yudhiṣṭhiraḥ //
1.34.d:
निहत्य कौरवान सर्वान् भ्रातृभिः सह पार्थिवः ।
शोकेन महाताविष्टा मुमोह स युधिष्ठिरः ॥
1.34.m:
Having slain all the Kauravas along with his brothers, the king,
overcome with great sorrow, that Yudhiṣṭhira fell into despair.

1.34.s:
acireṇātha kālena mārkaṇḍeyo mahātapāḥ /
saṃprāpto hāstinapuraṃ rājadvāre sa tiṣṭhati //
1.34.d:
अचिरेणाथ कालेन मार्कण्डेयो महातपाः ।
संप्राप्तो हास्तिनपुरं राजद्वारे स तिष्ठति ॥
1.34.m:
Then, before long, Mārkaṇḍeya of great ascetic heat
arrived at Hāstinapura and stood at the royal gate.

1.34.s:
dvārapālo 'pi taṃ dṛṣṭvā rājñaḥ kathitavān drutam /
mārkaṇḍeyo draṣṭumicchaṃstvāmāste dvāryasau muniḥ //
1.34.d:
द्वारपालो ऽपि तं दृष्ट्वा राज्ञः कथितवान् द्रुतम् ।
मार्कण्डेयो द्रष्टुमिच्छंस्त्वामास्ते द्वार्यसौ मुनिः ॥
1.34.m:
Seeing him, the doorkeeper promptly reported to the king:
"That sage Mārkaṇḍeya stands at the door, desiring to see you."

1.34.s:
tvarito dharmaputrastu dvārametyāha tatparam /
svāgataṃ te mahāprājña svāgataṃ te mahāmune //
1.34.d:
त्वरितो धर्मपुत्रस्तु द्वारमेत्याह तत्परम् ।
स्वागतं ते महाप्राज्ञ स्वागतं ते महामुने ॥
1.34.m:
Swiftly going to the gate, the son of Dharma then addressed him:
"Welcome to you, O very wise one! Welcome to you, O great sage!

1.34.s:
adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me tāritaṃ kulam /
adya me pitarastuṣṭāstvayi tuṣṭe mahāmune //
1.34.d:
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे तारितं कुलम् ।
अद्य मे पितरस्तुष्टास्त्वयि तुष्टे महामुने ॥
1.34.m:
Today my birth has borne fruit; today my family is delivered;
today my ancestors are pleased, when you are pleased, O great sage!"

1.34.s:
siṃhāsanamupasthāpya pādaśaucārcanādibhiḥ /
yudhiṣṭhiro mahātmeti pūjayāmāsa taṃ munim //
1.34.d:
सिंहासनमुपस्थाप्य पादशौचार्चनादिभिः ।
युधिष्ठिरो महात्मेति पूजयामास तं मुनिम् ॥
1.34.m:
Having offered a lion-throne, with washing of the feet, worship, and the like,
the magnanimous Yudhiṣṭhira honoured that sage.

1.34.s:
mārkaṇḍeyastatastuṣṭaḥ provāca sa yudhiṣṭhiram /
kimarthaṃ muhyase vidvan sarvaṃ jñātvāhamāgataḥ //
1.34.d:
मार्कण्डेयस्ततस्तुष्टः प्रोवाच स युधिष्ठिरम् ।
किमर्थं मुह्यसे विद्वन् सर्वं ज्ञात्वाहमागतः ॥
1.34.m:
Then Mārkaṇḍeya, being pleased, said to Yudhiṣṭhira:
"Why are you bewildered, wise one? Knowing everything, I have come."

1.34.s:
tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā praṇamyāha mahāmunim /
kathaya tvaṃ samāsena yena mucyeta kilbiṣaiḥ //
1.34.d:
ततो युधिष्ठिरो राजा प्रणम्याह महामुनिम् ।
कथय त्वं समासेन येन मुच्येत किल्बिषैः ॥
1.34.m:
Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, bowing, said to the great sage:
"Tell me in brief that whereby one may be freed from sins.

1.34.s:
nihatā vahavo yuddhe puṃso niraparādhinaḥ /
asmābhiḥ kauravaiḥ sārdhaṃ prasaṅgānmunipuṅgava //
1.34.d:
निहता वहवो युद्धे पुंसो निरपराधिनः ।
अस्माभिः कौरवैः सार्धं प्रसङ्गान्मुनिपुङ्गव ॥
1.34.m:
Many innocent men were slain in battle
by us together with the Kauravas as a consequence [of the conflict], O eminent sage.

1.34.s:
yena hiṃsāsamudbhūtājjanmāntarakṛtādapi /
mucyate pātakādasmāt tad bhavān vaktumarhati //
1.34.d:
येन हिंसासमुद्भूताज्जन्मान्तरकृतादपि ।
मुच्यते पातकादस्मात् तद् भवान् वक्तुमर्हति ॥
1.34.m:
That whereby one may be freed from this sin born of violence,
even if committed in another birth, you ought to tell that."

1.34.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
śṛṇu rājan mahābhāga yanmāṃ pṛcchasi bhārat /
prayāgagamanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ narāṇāṃ pāpanāśanam //
1.34.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
शृणु राजन् महाभाग यन्मां पृच्छसि भारत् ।
प्रयागगमनं श्रेष्ठं नराणां पापनाशनम् ॥
1.34.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Listen, O fortunate king, to what you ask of me, O descendant of Bharata:
journeying to Prayāga is the best, destroying the sins of men.

1.34.s:
tatra devo mahādevo rudro viśvāmareśvaraḥ /
samāste bhagavān brahmā svayaṃbhūrapi daivadaiḥ //
1.34.d:
तत्र देवो महादेवो रुद्रो विश्वामरेश्वरः ।
समास्ते भगवान् ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूरपि दैवदैः ॥
1.34.m:
There the god Mahādeva, Rudra, the lord of all immortals, dwells,
and the blessed Brahmā, the self-born one, also [dwells there] with the gods.

1.34.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca
bhagavañcchrotumicchāmi prayāgagamane phalam /
mṛtānāṃ kā gatistatra snātānāmapi kiṃ phalam //
1.34.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच
भगवञ्च्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि प्रयागगमने फलम् ।
मृतानां का गतिस्तत्र स्नातानामपि किं फलम् ॥
1.34.m:
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
O blessed one, I wish to hear the fruit of journeying to Prayāga.
What is the destination of those who die there, and what is the fruit for those who bathe?

1.34.s:
ye vasanti prayāge tu brūhi teṣāṃ tu kiṃ phalam /
bhavatā viditaṃ hyetat tanme brūhi namo 'stu te //
1.34.d:
ये वसन्ति प्रयागे तु ब्रूहि तेषां तु किं फलम् ।
भवता विदितं ह्येतत् तन्मे ब्रूहि नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.34.m:
For those who dwell in Prayāga, tell what is their fruit?
For this is known to you; tell it to me, homage be to you!"

1.34.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
kathayiṣyāmi te vatsa yā ceṣṭā yacca tatphalam /
purā maharṣibhiḥ samyak kathyamānaṃ mayā śrutam //
1.34.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
कथयिष्यामि ते वत्स या चेष्टा यच्च तत्फलम् ।
पुरा महर्षिभिः सम्यक् कथ्यमानं मया श्रुतम् ॥
1.34.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
"I shall tell you, my child, what is the practice and what is its fruit,
as it was properly recounted of old by the great sages and heard by me.

1.34.s:
etat prajāpatikṣetraṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam /
atra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste 'punarbhavāḥ //
1.34.d:
एतत् प्रजापतिक्षेत्रं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् ।
अत्र स्नात्वा दिवं यान्ति ये मृतास्ते ऽपुनर्भवाः ॥
1.34.m:
This sacred field of Prajāpati is renowned in the three worlds;
having bathed here, they go to heaven; those who die [here] do not return to rebirth.

1.34.s:
tatra brahmādayo devā rakṣāṃ kurvanti saṃgatāḥ /
bahūnyanyāni tīrthāni sarvapāpāpahāni tu //
1.34.d:
तत्र ब्रह्मादयो देवा रक्षां कुर्वन्ति संगताः ।
बहून्यन्यानि तीर्थानि सर्वपापापहानि तु ॥
1.34.m:
There Brahmā and the other gods assembled maintain protection.
Moreover, there are many other sacred bathing places that take away all sins.

1.34.s:
kathituṃ neha śaknomi bahuvarṣaśatairapi /
saṃkṣepeṇa pravakṣyāmi prayāgasyeha kīrtanam //
1.34.d:
कथितुं नेह शक्नोमि बहुवर्षशतैरपि ।
संक्षेपेण प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रयागस्येह कीर्तनम् ॥
1.34.m:
I cannot tell of them here even in many hundreds of years;
I shall proclaim in brief the praise of Prayāga here.

1.34.s:
ṣaṣṭirdhanuḥ sahastrāṇi yāni rakṣanti jāhnavīm /
yamunāṃ rakṣati sadā savitā saptavāhanaḥ //
1.34.d:
षष्टिर्धनुः सहस्त्राणि यानि रक्षन्ति जाह्नवीम् ।
यमुनां रक्षति सदा सविता सप्तवाहनः ॥
1.34.m:
Sixty thousand bow-lengths protect the Jāhnavī;
Savitar, who has seven steeds, always protects the Yamunā.

1.34.s:
prayāge tu viśeṣeṇa svayaṃ vasati vāsavaḥ /
maṇḍalaṃ rakṣati hariḥ sarvadevaiśca sammitam //
1.34.d:
प्रयागे तु विशेषेण स्वयं वसति वासवः ।
मण्डलं रक्षति हरिः सर्वदेवैश्च सम्मितम् ॥
1.34.m:
At Prayāga, however, Vāsava himself dwells especially;
Hari protects the circle, which is measured with all the gods.

1.34.s:
nyagrodhaṃ rakṣate nityaṃ śūlapāṇirmaheśvaraḥ /
sthānaṃ rakṣanti vai devāḥ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham //
1.34.d:
न्यग्रोधं रक्षते नित्यं शूलपाणिर्महेश्वरः ।
स्थानं रक्षन्ति वै देवाः सर्वपापहरं शुभम् ॥
1.34.m:
Maheśvara, holding the trident in hand, constantly protects the banyan tree;
the gods indeed protect the auspicious place that removes all sins.

1.34.s:
svakarmaṇāvṛto loko naiva gacchati tatpadam /
svalpaṃ svalpataraṃ pāpaṃ yadā tasya narādhipa /
prayāgaṃ smaramāṇasya sarvamāyāti saṃkṣayam //
1.34.d:
स्वकर्मणावृतो लोको नैव गच्छति तत्पदम् ।
स्वल्पं स्वल्पतरं पापं यदा तस्य नराधिप ।
प्रयागं स्मरमाणस्य सर्वमायाति संक्षयम् ॥
1.34.m:
Veiled by his own actions, a person never reaches that station.
When his sin is slight, very slight indeed, O ruler of men,
all of it goes to destruction for one who remembers Prayāga.

1.34.s:
darśanāt tasya tīrthasya nāma saṃkīrtanādapi /
muttikālambhanād vāpi naraḥ pāpāt pramucyate //
1.34.d:
दर्शनात् तस्य तीर्थस्य नाम संकीर्तनादपि ।
मुत्तिकालम्भनाद् वापि नरः पापात् प्रमुच्यते ॥
1.34.m:
From the sight of that sacred bathing place, from the recitation of its name,
or even from the application of its clay, a man is freed from sin.

1.34.s:
pañca kuṇḍāni rājendra yeṣāṃ madhye tu jāhnavī /
prayāgaṃ viśataḥ puṃsaḥ pāpaṃ naśyati tatkṣaṇāt //
1.34.d:
पञ्च कुण्डानि राजेन्द्र येषां मध्ये तु जाह्नवी ।
प्रयागं विशतः पुंसः पापं नश्यति तत्क्षणात् ॥
1.34.m:
There are five pools, O king of kings, in the midst of which is the Jāhnavī;
for a man entering Prayāga, sin is destroyed in that very instant.

1.34.s:
yojanānāṃ sahastreṣu gaṅgāṃ yaḥ smarate naraḥ /
api duṣkṛtakarmāsau labhate paramāṃ gatim //
1.34.d:
योजनानां सहस्त्रेषु गङ्गां यः स्मरते नरः ।
अपि दुष्कृतकर्मासौ लभते परमां गतिम् ॥
1.34.m:
The man who remembers the Gaṅgā across thousands of leagues,
even if he has performed evil actions, attains the supreme state.

1.34.s:
kīrtanānmucyate pāpād dṛṣṭvā bhadrāṇi paśyati /
tathopaspṛśya rājendra svargaloke mahīyate //
1.34.d:
कीर्तनान्मुच्यते पापाद् दृष्ट्वा भद्राणि पश्यति ।
तथोपस्पृश्य राजेन्द्र स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
1.34.m:
From praising [her] he is freed from sin; by seeing [her] he beholds auspicious things;
and by sipping her water, O lord of kings, he is honoured in the world of heaven.

1.34.s:
vyādhito yadi vā dīnaḥ krūddho vāpi bhavennaraḥ /
gaṅgāyamunamāsādya tyajet prāṇān prayatnataḥ //
1.34.d:
व्याधितो यदि वा दीनः क्रूद्धो वापि भवेन्नरः ।
गङ्गायमुनमासाद्य त्यजेत् प्राणान् प्रयत्नतः ॥
1.34.m:
Whether a man be diseased, afflicted, or angry,
reaching the Gaṅgā and Yamunā, he should cast off his life with diligence.

1.34.s:
dīptakāñcanavarṇābhairvimānairbhānuvarṇibhiḥ /
īpsitāṃllabhate kāmān vadanti munipuṅgavāḥ //
1.34.d:
दीप्तकाञ्चनवर्णाभैर्विमानैर्भानुवर्णिभिः ।
ईप्सितांल्लभते कामान् वदन्ति मुनिपुङ्गवाः ॥
1.34.m:
With aerial chariots possessing the brilliance of blazing gold, having the colour of the sun,
he obtains his desired wishes, so the foremost sages declare."

1.34.s:
sarvaratnamayairdivyairnānādhvajasamākulaiḥ /
varāṅganāsamākīrṇairmodate śubhalakṣaṇaḥ //
1.34.d:
सर्वरत्नमयैर्दिव्यैर्नानाध्वजसमाकुलैः ।
वराङ्गनासमाकीर्णैर्मोदते शुभलक्षणः ॥
1.34.m:
With [aerial cars] made of every jewel, celestial, crowded with varied banners,
filled with excellent women, he rejoices, possessing auspicious marks.

1.34.s:
gītavāditranirghoṣaiḥ prasuptaḥ pratibudhyate /
yāvanna smarate janma tāpat svarge mahīyate //
1.34.d:
गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषैः प्रसुप्तः प्रतिबुध्यते ।
यावन्न स्मरते जन्म तापत् स्वर्गे महीयते ॥
1.34.m:
He is awakened from sleep by sounds of singing and instrumental music;
so long as he does not recall his [previous] birth, so long is he honored in heaven.

1.34.s:
tasmāt svargāt paribhraṣṭaḥ kṣīṇakarmā narottama /
hiraṇyaratnasaṃpūrṇe samṛddhe jāyate kule //
1.34.d:
तस्मात् स्वर्गात् परिभ्रष्टः क्षीणकर्मा नरोत्तम ।
हिरण्यरत्नसंपूर्णे समृद्धे जायते कुले ॥
1.34.m:
Fallen from that heaven when his karma is exhausted, O best of men,
he is born in a wealthy family filled with gold and jewels.

1.34.s:
tadeva smarate tīrthaṃ smaraṇāt tatra gacchati /
deśastho yadi vāraṇye videśe yadi vā gṛhe //
1.34.d:
तदेव स्मरते तीर्थं स्मरणात् तत्र गच्छति ।
देशस्थो यदि वारण्ये विदेशे यदि वा गृहे ॥
1.34.m:
He remembers that very ford; by remembering, he goes there,
whether he is in his own country, in the forest, abroad, or in his home.

1.34.s:
prayāgaṃ smaramāṇastu yastu prāṇān parityajet /
brahmalokamavāpnoti vadanti munipuṅgavāḥ //
1.34.d:
प्रयागं स्मरमाणस्तु यस्तु प्राणान् परित्यजेत् ।
ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नोति वदन्ति मुनिपुङ्गवाः ॥
1.34.m:
Remembering Prayāga, whoever gives up his life
attains the world of Brahmā, say the foremost sages.

1.34.s:
sarvakāmaphalā vṛkṣā mahī yatra hiraṇmayī /
ṛṣayo munayaḥ siddhāstatra loke sa gacchati //
1.34.d:
सर्वकामफला वृक्षा मही यत्र हिरण्मयी ।
ऋषयो मुनयः सिद्धास्तत्र लोके स गच्छति ॥
1.34.m:
Where trees yield all desired fruits and the ground is golden,
where there are seers, sages, and accomplished beings—to that world he goes.

1.34.s:
strīsahastrākule ramye mandākinyāstaṭe śubhe /
modate munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ svakṛteneha karmaṇā //
1.34.d:
स्त्रीसहस्त्राकुले रम्ये मन्दाकिन्यास्तटे शुभे ।
मोदते मुनिभिः सार्धं स्वकृतेनेह कर्मणा ॥
1.34.m:
On the charming, auspicious bank of the Mandākinī, crowded with thousands of women,
he rejoices together with sages by virtue of his own deed done here.

1.34.s:
siddhacāraṇagandharvaiḥ pūjyate divi daivataiḥ /
tataḥ svargāt paribhraṣṭo jambudvīpapatirbhavet //
1.34.d:
सिद्धचारणगन्धर्वैः पूज्यते दिवि दैवतैः ।
ततः स्वर्गात् परिभ्रष्टो जम्बुद्वीपपतिर्भवेत् ॥
1.34.m:
He is worshipped in heaven by Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, and deities;
then, falling from that heaven, he becomes the ruler of Jambūdvīpa.

1.34.s:
tataḥ śubhāni karmāṇi cintayānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ /
guṇavān vittasaṃpanno bhavatīha na saṃśayaḥ /
karmaṇā manasā vācā satyadharmapratiṣṭhitaḥ //
1.34.d:
ततः शुभानि कर्माणि चिन्तयानः पुनः पुनः ।
गुणवान् वित्तसंपन्नो भवतीह न संशयः ।
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा सत्यधर्मप्रतिष्ठितः ॥
1.34.m:
Thereupon, continually reflecting on auspicious deeds,
he undoubtedly becomes virtuous and wealthy in this world,
established in truth and righteousness in deed, mind, and speech.

1.34.s:
gaṅgāyamunayormadhye yastu grāmaṃ pratīcchati /
suvarṇamatha muktāṃ vā tathaivānyān pratigrahān //
1.34.d:
गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये यस्तु ग्रामं प्रतीच्छति ।
सुवर्णमथ मुक्तां वा तथैवान्यान् प्रतिग्रहान् ॥
1.34.m:
He who accepts a village between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā,
or gold, or pearls, or likewise other gifts,

1.34.s:
svakārye pitṛkārye vā devatābhyarcane 'pi vā /
niṣphalaṃ tasya tat tīrthaṃ yāvat tatphalamaśnute //
1.34.d:
स्वकार्ये पितृकार्ये वा देवताभ्यर्चने ऽपि वा ।
निष्फलं तस्य तत् तीर्थं यावत् तत्फलमश्नुते ॥
1.34.m:
for his own sake, for ancestral rites, or for the worship of deities—
fruitless for him is that holy ford as long as he enjoys that fruit.

1.34.s:
atastīrthe na gṛhṇīyāt puṇyeṣvāyataneṣu ca /
nimitteṣu ca sarveṣu apramatto dvijo bhavet //
1.34.d:
अतस्तीर्थे न गृह्णीयात् पुण्येष्वायतनेषु च ।
निमित्तेषु च सर्वेषु अप्रमत्तो द्विजो भवेत् ॥
1.34.m:
Therefore, let him not receive [gifts] at a holy ford, or in sacred shrines;
in all circumstances a twice-born should be vigilant.

1.34.s:
kapilāṃ pāṭalāvarṇāṃ yastu dhenuṃ prayacchati /
svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ cailakaṇṭhāṃ payasvinīm //
1.34.d:
कपिलां पाटलावर्णां यस्तु धेनुं प्रयच्छति ।
स्वर्णशृङ्गीं रौप्यखुरां चैलकण्ठां पयस्विनीम् ॥
1.34.m:
Whoever gives away a brown, tawny-colored cow
with golden horns, silver hooves, a cloth around her neck, and yielding milk—

1.34.s:
yāvad romāṇi tasyā vai santi gātreṣu sattama /
tāvad varṣasahastrāṇi rudraloke mahīyate //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge catustriśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.34.d:
यावद् रोमाणि तस्या वै सन्ति गात्रेषु सत्तम ।
तावद् वर्षसहस्त्राणि रुद्रलोके महीयते ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे चतुस्त्रिशो ऽध्यायः
1.34.m:
as many hairs as are on her body, O best of beings,
for that many thousands of years he is glorified in the world of Rudra.

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the holy Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.35.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
kathayiṣyāmi te vatsa tīrthayātrāvidhikramam /
ārṣeṇa tu vidhānena yathā dṛṣṭaṃ yathā śrutam //
1.35.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
कथयिष्यामि ते वत्स तीर्थयात्राविधिक्रमम् ।
आर्षेण तु विधानेन यथा दृष्टं यथा श्रुतम् ॥
1.35.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I shall describe to you, dear one, the sequence of rules for pilgrimage to holy fords,
according to the traditional ordinance, as it has been seen and as it has been heard.

1.35.s:
prayāgatīrthayātrārtho yaḥ prayāti naraḥ kvacit /
balīvardaṃ samārūḍhaḥ śṛṇu tasyāpi yatphalam //
1.35.d:
प्रयागतीर्थयात्रार्थो यः प्रयाति नरः क्वचित् ।
बलीवर्दं समारूढः शृणु तस्यापि यत्फलम् ॥
1.35.m:
Whoever sets out for a pilgrimage to the ford of Prayāga
mounted on an ox, hear also the consequence of that:

1.35.s:
narake vasate ghore samāḥ kalpaśatāyutam /
tato nivartate ghoro gavāṃ krodho hi dāruṇaḥ /
salilaṃ ca na gṛhṇanti pitarastasya dehinaḥ //
1.35.d:
नरके वसते घोरे समाः कल्पशतायुतम् ।
ततो निवर्तते घोरो गवां क्रोधो हि दारुणः ।
सलिलं च न गृह्णन्ति पितरस्तस्य देहिनः ॥

1.35.s:
yastu putrāṃstathā bālān snāpayet pāyayet tathā /
yathātmanā tathā sarvān dānaṃ vipreṣu dāpayet //
1.35.d:
यस्तु पुत्रांस्तथा बालान् स्नापयेत् पाययेत् तथा ।
यथात्मना तथा सर्वान् दानं विप्रेषु दापयेत् ॥
1.35.m:
Whoever bathes his sons and children, and gives them drink,
and causes gifts to be given to Brahmins for all of them just as for himself—

1.35.s:
aiśvaryāllobhamohād vā gacched yānena yo naraḥ /
niṣphalaṃ tasya tat tīrthaṃ tasamādyānaṃ vivarjayet //
1.35.d:
ऐश्वर्याल्लोभमोहाद् वा गच्छेद् यानेन यो नरः ।
निष्फलं तस्य तत् तीर्थं तसमाद्यानं विवर्जयेत् ॥
1.35.m:
the man who goes by a vehicle out of opulence, greed, or delusion,
fruitless for him is that holy ford; therefore, let him avoid a vehicle.

1.35.s:
gaṅgāyamunayormadhye yastu kanyāṃ prayacchati /
ārṣeṇa tu vivāhena yathā vibhavavistaram //
1.35.d:
गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये यस्तु कन्यां प्रयच्छति ।
आर्षेण तु विवाहेन यथा विभवविस्तरम् ॥
1.35.m:
Whoever gives away a maiden between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā
according to the traditional rite of marriage, according to the extent of his wealth,

1.35.s:
na sa paśyati taṃ ghoraṃ narakaṃ tena karmaṇā /
uttarān sa kurūn gatvā modate kālamakṣayam //
1.35.d:
न स पश्यति तं घोरं नरकं तेन कर्मणा ।
उत्तरान् स कुरून् गत्वा मोदते कालमक्षयम् ॥
1.35.m:
he does not see that dreadful hell by virtue of that deed;
having gone to the Northern Kurus, he rejoices for an imperishable time.

1.35.s:
vaṭamūlaṃ samāśritya yastu prāṇān parityajet /
sarvalokānatikramya rudralokaṃ sa gacchati //
1.35.d:
वटमूलं समाश्रित्य यस्तु प्राणान् परित्यजेत् ।
सर्वलोकानतिक्रम्य रुद्रलोकं स गच्छति ॥
1.35.m:
Whoever gives up his life resorting to the root of the banyan tree,
transcending all the worlds, he goes to the world of Rudra.

1.35.s:
tatra brahmādayo devā diśaśca sadigīśvarāḥ /
lokapālāśca siddhāśca pitaro lokasaṃmatāḥ //
1.35.d:
तत्र ब्रह्मादयो देवा दिशश्च सदिगीश्वराः ।
लोकपालाश्च सिद्धाश्च पितरो लोकसंमताः ॥
1.35.m:
There Brahmā and the other gods, the directions along with their guardians,
the world-protectors, the Siddhas, and the ancestors honored by the worlds,

1.35.s:
sanatkumārapramukhāstathā brahmarṣayo 'pare /
nāgāḥ supārṇāḥ siddhāśca tathā nityaṃ samāsate /
hariśca bhagavānāste prajāpatipuraskṛtaḥ //
1.35.d:
सनत्कुमारप्रमुखास्तथा ब्रह्मर्षयो ऽपरे ।
नागाः सुपार्णाः सिद्धाश्च तथा नित्यं समासते ।
हरिश्च भगवानास्ते प्रजापतिपुरस्कृतः ॥

1.35.s:
gaṅgāyamunayormadhye pṛthivyā jaghanaṃ smṛtam /
prayāgaṃ rājaśārdūla triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam //
1.35.d:
गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये पृथिव्या जघनं स्मृतम् ।
प्रयागं राजशार्दूल त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् ॥
1.35.m:
The region between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā is declared to be the loins of the earth;
[it is] Prayāga, O tiger among kings, renowned in the three worlds.

1.35.s:
tatrābhiṣekaṃ yaḥ kuryāt saṃgame saṃśitavrataḥ /
tulyaṃ phalavāpnoti rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ //
1.35.d:
तत्राभिषेकं यः कुर्यात् संगमे संशितव्रतः ।
तुल्यं फलवाप्नोति राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः ॥
1.35.m:
Whoever performs ablution there at the confluence, firm in his vow,
attains a fruit equal to [that of] the royal consecration and the horse sacrifice.

1.35.s:
na mātṛvacanāt tāta na lokavacanādapi /
matirutkramaṇīyā te prayāgagāmanaṃ prati //
1.35.d:
न मातृवचनात् तात न लोकवचनादपि ।
मतिरुत्क्रमणीया ते प्रयागगामनं प्रति ॥
1.35.m:
Neither on the words of a mother, O dear one, nor on the words of people,
should your intention to go to Prayāga be set aside.

1.35.s:
daśa tīrtha sahastrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭyastathāpare /
teṣāṃ sānnidhyamatraiva tīrthānāṃ kurunandana //
1.35.d:
दश तीर्थ सहस्त्राणि षष्टिकोट्यस्तथापरे ।
तेषां सान्निध्यमत्रैव तीर्थानां कुरुनन्दन ॥
1.35.m:
Ten thousand holy fords, and sixty crores of others—
the presence of these fords is right here, O delight of the Kurus.

1.35.s:
yā gatiryogayuktasya sattvasthasya manīṣiṇaḥ /
sā gatistyajataḥ prāṇān gaṅgāyamunasaṃgame //
1.35.d:
या गतिर्योगयुक्तस्य सत्त्वस्थस्य मनीषिणः ।
सा गतिस्त्यजतः प्राणान् गङ्गायमुनसंगमे ॥
1.35.m:
The state attained by the wise man devoted to yoga and abiding in purity
is the state attained by one who gives up his life at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and Yamunā.

1.35.s:
na te jīvanti loke 'smin yatra tatra yudhiṣṭhira /
ye prayāgaṃ na saṃprāptāstriṣu lokeṣu viśrutam //
1.35.d:
न ते जीवन्ति लोके ऽस्मिन् यत्र तत्र युधिष्ठिर ।
ये प्रयागं न संप्राप्तास्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् ॥
1.35.m:
They do not truly live in this world anywhere, O Yudhiṣṭhira,
who have not reached Prayāga, renowned in the three worlds.

1.35.s:
evaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu tat tīrthaṃ prayāgaṃ paramaṃ padam /
mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ śaśāṅka iva rāhuṇā //
1.35.d:
एवं दृष्ट्वा तु तत् तीर्थं प्रयागं परमं पदम् ।
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यः शशाङ्क इव राहुणा ॥
1.35.m:
Having thus beheld that holy ford, Prayāga, the supreme abode,
one is freed from all sins like the moon from Rāhu.

1.35.s:
kambalāśvatarau nāgau yamunādakṣiṇe taṭe /
tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ //
1.35.d:
कम्बलाश्वतरौ नागौ यमुनादक्षिणे तटे ।
तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ॥
1.35.m:
The two serpent-deities Kambala and Aśvatara are on the southern bank of the Yamunā;
having bathed there and drunk [its water], one is freed from all sins.

1.35.s:
tatra gatvā naraḥ sthānaṃ mahādevasya dhīmataḥ /
ātmānaṃ tārayet pūrvaṃ daśātītān daśāparān //
1.35.d:
तत्र गत्वा नरः स्थानं महादेवस्य धीमतः ।
आत्मानं तारयेत् पूर्वं दशातीतान् दशापरान् ॥
1.35.m:
A man having gone there to the abode of the wise Mahādeva
saves himself, ten ancestors before him, and ten descendants after him.

1.35.s:
kṛtvābhiṣekaṃ tu naraḥ so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet /
svargalokamavāpnoti yāvadāhūtasaṃplavam //
1.35.d:
कृत्वाभिषेकं तु नरः सो ऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ।
स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नोति यावदाहूतसंप्लवम् ॥
1.35.m:
Having performed ablution, a man obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice;
he attains the heavenly world until the dissolution of beings.

1.35.s:
pūrvapārśve tu gaṅgāyāstrailokyakhyātimān nṛpa /
avacaḥ sarvasāmudraḥ pratiṣṭhānaṃ ca viśrutam //
1.35.d:
पूर्वपार्श्वे तु गङ्गायास्त्रैलोक्यख्यातिमान् नृप ।
अवचः सर्वसामुद्रः प्रतिष्ठानं च विश्रुतम् ॥
1.35.m:
On the eastern bank of the Gaṅgā, celebrated in the three worlds, O king,
is celebrated Pratiṣṭhāna, where the ocean is accessible to all.

1.35.s:
brahmacārī jitakrodhastrirātraṃ yadi tiṣṭhati /
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet //
1.35.d:
ब्रह्मचारी जितक्रोधस्त्रिरात्रं यदि तिष्ठति ।
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा सो ऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥
1.35.m:
If a student of the Veda, having conquered anger, stays there for three nights
with his soul purified of all sins, he obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

1.35.s:
uttareṇa pratiṣṭhānaṃ bhāgīrathyāstu savyataḥ /
haṃsaprapatanaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam //
1.35.d:
उत्तरेण प्रतिष्ठानं भागीरथ्यास्तु सव्यतः ।
हंसप्रपतनं नाम तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ॥
1.35.m:
North of Pratiṣṭhāna and on the left side of the Bhāgīrathī
is the holy ford named Haṃsaprapatana, renowned in the three worlds.

1.35.s:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ tatra smṛtamātrāt tu jāyate /
yāvaccandraśca sūryaśca tāvat svarge mahīyate //
1.35.d:
अश्वमेधफलं तत्र स्मृतमात्रात् तु जायते ।
यावच्चन्द्रश्च सूर्यश्च तावत् स्वर्गे महीयते ॥
1.35.m:
The fruit of a horse sacrifice arises there merely by being remembered;
as long as the moon and sun endure, so long is he honored in heaven.

1.35.s:
urvaśīpuline ramye vipule haṃsapāṇḍure /
parityajatiyaḥ prāṇān śṛṇu tasyāpi yat phalam //
1.35.d:
उर्वशीपुलिने रम्ये विपुले हंसपाण्डुरे ।
परित्यजतियः प्राणान् शृणु तस्यापि यत् फलम् ॥
1.35.m:
On the charming, broad sandbank of Urvaśī, white like a swan,
whoever gives up his life, hear also the fruit thereof:

1.35.s:
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahastrāṇi ṣaṣṭivarṣaśatāni ca /
āste sa pitṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ svargaloke narādhipa //
1.35.d:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्त्राणि षष्टिवर्षशतानि च ।
आस्ते स पितृभिः सार्धं स्वर्गलोके नराधिप ॥
1.35.m:
For sixty thousand and six hundred years,
he dwells together with his ancestors in the heavenly world, O lord of men.

1.35.s:
athaṃ saṃdhyāvaṭe ramye brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ /
naraḥ śucirupāsīta brahmalokamavāpnuyāt //
1.35.d:
अथं संध्यावटे रम्ये ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः ।
नरः शुचिरुपासीत ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.35.m:
Now, at the charming evening banyan tree, chaste and with subdued senses,
let a man worship in purity; he shall attain the world of Brahmā.

1.35.s:
koṭitīrthaṃ samāśritya yastu prāṇān parityajet /
koṭivarṣasahastrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate //
1.35.d:
कोटितीर्थं समाश्रित्य यस्तु प्राणान् परित्यजेत् ।
कोटिवर्षसहस्त्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
1.35.m:
Whoever gives up his life resorting to Koṭitīrtha
is glorified in the heavenly world for a thousand crores of years.

1.35.s:
yatra gaṅgā mahābhāgā bahutīrthatapovanā /
siddhakṣetraṃ hi tajjñeyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā //
1.35.d:
यत्र गङ्गा महाभागा बहुतीर्थतपोवना ।
सिद्धक्षेत्रं हि तज्ज्ञेयं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
1.35.m:
Where the illustrious Gaṅgā has many holy fords and penance groves,
that should indeed be known as an accomplished field; here no doubt should be entertained.

1.35.s:
kṣitau tārayate martyān nāgāṃstārayate 'pyadhaḥ /
divi tārayate devāṃstena tripathagā smṛtā //
1.35.d:
क्षितौ तारयते मर्त्यान् नागांस्तारयते ऽप्यधः ।
दिवि तारयते देवांस्तेन त्रिपथगा स्मृता ॥
1.35.m:
She delivers mortals on earth, and she delivers serpents below;
she delivers the gods in heaven; therefore she is known as the Three-Pathed River.

1.35.s:
yāvadasthīni gaṅgāyāṃ tiṣṭhanti puruṣasya tu /
tāvad varṣasahastrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate //
1.35.d:
यावदस्थीनि गङ्गायां तिष्ठन्ति पुरुषस्य तु ।
तावद् वर्षसहस्त्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
1.35.m:
As long as the bones of a man remain in the Gaṅgā,
for that many thousands of years he is honored in the heavenly world.

1.35.s:
tīrthānāṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ nadīnāṃ paramā nadī /
mokṣadā sarvabhūtānāṃ mahāpātakināmapi //
1.35.d:
तीर्थानां परमं तीर्थं नदीनां परमा नदी ।
मोक्षदा सर्वभूतानां महापातकिनामपि ॥
1.35.m: It is the supreme pilgrimage site among pilgrimage sites, the supreme river among rivers, / granting liberation to all beings, even to the greatest sinners.

1.35.s:
sarvatra sulabhā gaṅgā triṣu sthāneṣu durlabhā /
gaṅgādvāre prayāge ca gaṅgāsāgarasaṃgame //
1.35.d:
सर्वत्र सुलभा गङ्गा त्रिषु स्थानेषु दुर्लभा ।
गङ्गाद्वारे प्रयागे च गङ्गासागरसंगमे ॥
1.35.m: Everywhere the Gaṅgā is easy of access, [but] difficult of access in three places: / at Gaṅgādvāra, at Prayāga, and at the confluence of the Gaṅgā with the ocean.

1.35.s:
sarveṣāme bhūtānāṃ pāpopahatacetasām /
gatimanveṣamāṇānāṃ nāsti gaṅgāsamā gatiḥ //
1.35.d:
सर्वेषामे भूतानां पापोपहतचेतसाम् ।
गतिमन्वेषमाणानां नास्ति गङ्गासमा गतिः ॥
1.35.m: For all beings whose minds are afflicted by sin / and who seek a refuge, there is no refuge equal to the Gaṅgā.

1.35.s:
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ ca maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam /
māheśvarāt paribhraṣṭā sarvapāpaharā śubhā //
1.35.d:
पवित्राणां पवित्रं च मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ।
माहेश्वरात् परिभ्रष्टा सर्वपापहरा शुभा ॥
1.35.m: The purifier of purifiers and the auspiciousness of auspicious things, / fallen from the Great Lord, destroying all sins, she is auspicious.

1.35.s:
kṛte yuge tu tīrthāni tretāyāṃ puṣkaraṃ param /
dvāpare tu kurukṣetraṃ kalau gaṅgāṃ viśiṣyate //
1.35.d:
कृते युगे तु तीर्थानि त्रेतायां पुष्करं परम् ।
द्वापरे तु कुरुक्षेत्रं कलौ गङ्गां विशिष्यते ॥
1.35.m: In the Kṛta Yuga [all] pilgrimage sites [are foremost], in the Tretā Puṣkara is supreme, / in the Dvāpara Kurukṣetra, [and] in the Kali the Gaṅgā is distinguished.

1.35.s:
gaṅgāmeva niṣeveta prayāge tu viśeṣataḥ /
nānyat kaliyugodbhūtaṃ malaṃ hantuṃ suduṣkṛtam //
1.35.d:
गङ्गामेव निषेवेत प्रयागे तु विशेषतः ।
नान्यत् कलियुगोद्भूतं मलं हन्तुं सुदुष्कृतम् ॥
1.35.m: One should resort only to the Gaṅgā, especially at Prayāga; / there is nothing else to destroy the very wicked stain born of the Kali age.

1.35.s:
akāmo vā sakāmo vā gaṅgāyāṃ yo vipadyate /
sa mṛto jāyate svarge narakaṃ ca na paśyati //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge pañcatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.35.d:
अकामो वा सकामो वा गङ्गायां यो विपद्यते ।
स मृतो जायते स्वर्गे नरकं च न पश्यति ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे पञ्चत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.35.m:
Whether without desire or with desire, whoever meets his end in the Gaṅgā, / he is born in heaven upon death and never sees hell.

Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the auspicious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.36.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
ṣaṣṭistīrthasahastrāṇi ṣaṣṭistīrthaśatāni ca /
māghamāse gamiṣyanti gaṅgāyamunasaṃgamam //
1.36.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
षष्टिस्तीर्थसहस्त्राणि षष्टिस्तीर्थशतानि च ।
माघमासे गमिष्यन्ति गङ्गायमुनसंगमम् ॥
1.36.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Sixty thousand pilgrimage sites and six hundred pilgrimage sites / will go in the month of Māgha to the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā.

1.36.s:
gavāṃ śatasahastrasya samyag dattasya yat phalam /
prayāge māghamāse tu tryahaṃ snātasya tat phalam //
1.36.d:
गवां शतसहस्त्रस्य सम्यग् दत्तस्य यत् फलम् ।
प्रयागे माघमासे तु त्र्यहं स्नातस्य तत् फलम् ॥
1.36.m: Whatever fruit is attained from giving a hundred thousand cows properly, / that same fruit belongs to one who bathes for three days at Prayāga in the month of Māgha.

1.36.s:
gaṅgāyamunayormadhye kārṣāgniṃ yastu sādhayet /
ahīnāṅgo 'pyarogaśca pañcendriyasamanvitaḥ //
1.36.d:
गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये कार्षाग्निं यस्तु साधयेत् ।
अहीनाङ्गो ऽप्यरोगश्च पञ्चेन्द्रियसमन्वितः ॥
1.36.m: Whoever, between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, practices the dried cow-dung fire ritual, / with unmaimed limbs, free from disease, and possessing his five senses,

1.36.s:
yāvanti romakūpāṇi tasya gātreṣu mānada /
tāvad varṣasahastrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate //
1.36.d:
यावन्ति रोमकूपाणि तस्य गात्रेषु मानद ।
तावद् वर्षसहस्त्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
1.36.m: As many pores of the skin as there are on his body, O giver of honor, / for that many thousands of years he is glorified in the heavenly world.

1.36.s:
tataḥ svargāt paribhraṣṭo jambūdvīpapatirbhavet /
sa bhuktvā vipulān bhogāṃstat tīrthaṃ bhajate punaḥ //
jalapraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryāt saṃgame lokaviśrute /
rāhugrasto yathā somo vimuktaḥ sarvapātakaiḥ //
1.36.d:
ततः स्वर्गात् परिभ्रष्टो जम्बूद्वीपपतिर्भवेत् ।
स भुक्त्वा विपुलान् भोगांस्तत् तीर्थं भजते पुनः ॥
जलप्रवेशं यः कुर्यात् संगमे लोकविश्रुते ।
राहुग्रस्तो यथा सोमो विमुक्तः सर्वपातकैः ॥
1.36.m:
Then, having descended from heaven, he becomes the ruler of Jambūdvīpa; / having enjoyed extensive pleasures, he resorts to that pilgrimage site again.

Whoever enters the water at that world-renowned confluence, / freed from all sins like the moon seized by Rāhu,

1.36.s:
somalokamavāpnoti somena saha modate /
ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣasahastrāṇi ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣaśatāni ca //
1.36.d:
सोमलोकमवाप्नोति सोमेन सह मोदते ।
षष्टिं वर्षसहस्त्राणि षष्टिं वर्षशतानि च ॥
1.36.m: Attains the world of the Moon and rejoices with Soma / for sixty thousand years and sixty hundred years.

1.36.s:
svargataḥ śakraloke 'sau munigandharvasevitaḥ /
tato bhraṣṭastu rājendra samṛddhe jāyate kule //
1.36.d:
स्वर्गतः शक्रलोके ऽसौ मुनिगन्धर्वसेवितः ।
ततो भ्रष्टस्तु राजेन्द्र समृद्धे जायते कुले ॥
1.36.m: Having gone to heaven, he [dwells] in Śakra's world, attended by sages and Gandharvas; / then, having fallen [from there], O king of kings, he is born in a prosperous family.

1.36.s:
adhaḥ śirāstvayodhārāmurdhvapādaḥ pibennaraḥ /
śataṃ varṣasahastrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate //
1.36.d:
अधः शिरास्त्वयोधारामुर्ध्वपादः पिबेन्नरः ।
शतं वर्षसहस्त्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
1.36.m: If a man, head downward and feet upward, drinks water, / he is glorified in the heavenly world for a hundred thousand years.

1.36.s:
tasmād bhraṣṭastu rājendra agnihotrī bhavennaraḥ /
bhuktvā tu vipulān bhogāṃstat tīrthaṃ bhajate punaḥ //
1.36.d:
तस्माद् भ्रष्टस्तु राजेन्द्र अग्निहोत्री भवेन्नरः ।
भुक्त्वा तु विपुलान् भोगांस्तत् तीर्थं भजते पुनः ॥
1.36.m: Falling from there, O king of kings, the man becomes a maintainer of the sacred fire; / having enjoyed extensive pleasures, he resorts to that pilgrimage site again.

1.36.s:
yaḥ svadehaṃ vikarted vā śakunibhyaḥ prayacchati /
vihagairupabhuktasya śṛṇu tasyāpi yatphalam //
1.36.d:
यः स्वदेहं विकर्तेद् वा शकुनिभ्यः प्रयच्छति ।
विहगैरुपभुक्तस्य शृणु तस्यापि यत्फलम् ॥
1.36.m: Or whoever carves off his own body and offers it to birds— / hear the fruit of him whose [flesh] has been consumed by birds:

1.36.s:
śataṃ varṣasahastrāṇi somaloke mahīyate /
tatastasmāt paribhraṣṭo rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ //
1.36.d:
शतं वर्षसहस्त्राणि सोमलोके महीयते ।
ततस्तस्मात् परिभ्रष्टो राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥
1.36.m: He is glorified in the world of the Moon for a hundred thousand years; / then, falling from there, he becomes a righteous king,

1.36.s:
guṇavān rūpasaṃpanno vidvān supriyavākyavān /
bhuktvā tu vipulān bhogāṃstatatīrthaṃ bhajate punaḥ //
1.36.d:
गुणवान् रूपसंपन्नो विद्वान् सुप्रियवाक्यवान् ।
भुक्त्वा तु विपुलान् भोगांस्तततीर्थं भजते पुनः ॥
1.36.m: Virtuous, endowed with beauty, learned, and speaking very pleasant words; / having enjoyed extensive pleasures, he resorts to that pilgrimage site again.

1.36.s:
uttare yamunātīre prayāgasya tu dakṣiṇe /
ṛṇapramocanaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ tu paramaṃ smṛtam //
1.36.d:
