उत्तरे यमुनातीरे प्रयागस्य तु दक्षिणे ।
ऋणप्रमोचनं नाम तीर्थं तु परमं स्मृतम् ॥
1.36.m: On the northern bank of the Yamunā, but to the south of Prayāga, / the pilgrimage site named Ṛṇapramocana is traditionally regarded as supreme.

1.36.s:
ekarātroṣitaḥ snātvā ṛṇaistatra pramucyate /
sūryalokamavāpnoti anṛṇaśca sadā bhavet //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge ṣaṭtriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.36.d:
एकरात्रोषितः स्नात्वा ऋणैस्तत्र प्रमुच्यते ।
सूर्यलोकमवाप्नोति अनृणश्च सदा भवेत् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे षट्त्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.36.m:
Having fasted for one night and bathed, he is released from debts there; / he attains the world of the Sun and becomes forever free of debt.

Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the auspicious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.37.s:
mārkaṇḍaya uvāca
tapanasya sutā devī triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā /
samāgatā mahābhāgā yamunā yatra nimnagā //
1.37.d:
मार्कण्डय उवाच
तपनस्य सुता देवी त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता ।
समागता महाभागा यमुना यत्र निम्नगा ॥
1.37.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The divine daughter of the Sun, renowned in the three worlds, / the fortunate river Yamunā, has arrived where [the Gaṅgā flows].

1.37.s:
yenaiva niḥ sṛtā gaṅgā tenaiva yamunā gatā /
yojanānāṃ sahastreṣu kīrtanāt pāpanāśanī //
1.37.d:
येनैव निः सृता गङ्गा तेनैव यमुना गता ।
योजनानां सहस्त्रेषु कीर्तनात् पापनाशनी ॥
1.37.m: Along the very path the Gaṅgā came forth, along that path the Yamunā has gone; / she destroys sin through being glorified across thousands of leagues.

1.37.s:
tatra snātvā ca pītvā ca yamunāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira /
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam /
prāṇāṃstyajati yastatra sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
1.37.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा च पीत्वा च यमुनायां युधिष्ठिर ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः पुनात्यासप्तमं कुलम् ।
प्राणांस्त्यजति यस्तत्र स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
1.37.m: Having bathed and drunk there in the Yamunā, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / completely freed from all sins, one purifies one's lineage up to the seventh generation; / whoever abandons his life-breaths there goes to the supreme state.

1.37.s:
agnitīrthamiti khyātaṃ yamunādakṣiṇa taṭe /
paścime dharmarājasya tīrthaṃ tvanarakaṃ smṛtam /
tatra snātvā divaṃ yānti ye mṛtāste 'punarbhavāḥ //
1.37.d:
अग्नितीर्थमिति ख्यातं यमुनादक्षिण तटे ।
पश्चिमे धर्मराजस्य तीर्थं त्वनरकं स्मृतम् ।
तत्र स्नात्वा दिवं यान्ति ये मृतास्ते ऽपुनर्भवाः ॥
1.37.m: There is [the site] renowned as Agnitīrtha on the southern bank of the Yamunā; / to the west of Dharmarāja's [abode], the pilgrimage site is remembered as Anaraka; / having bathed there, they go to heaven; those who die [there] have no rebirth.

1.37.s:
kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ snātvā saṃtarpayecchuciḥ /
dharmarājaṃ mahāpāpairmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
1.37.d:
कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां स्नात्वा संतर्पयेच्छुचिः ।
धर्मराजं महापापैर्मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
1.37.m: Having bathed on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, pure, one should offer libations / to Dharmarāja; he is freed from great sins, there is no doubt of this.

1.37.s:
daśa tīrthasahastrāṇi triṃśatkoṭyastathāparāḥ /
prayāge saṃsthitāni syurevamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ //
1.37.d:
दश तीर्थसहस्त्राणि त्रिंशत्कोट्यस्तथापराः ।
प्रयागे संस्थितानि स्युरेवमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
1.37.m: Ten thousand pilgrimage sites and thirty crores more / are situated at Prayāga; so say the wise.

1.37.s:
tistraḥ koṭyor'dhakoṭī ca tīrthānāṃ vāyurabravīt /
divi bhūmyantarikṣe ca tatsarvaṃ jāhnavī smṛtā //
1.37.d:
तिस्त्रः कोट्योर्ऽधकोटी च तीर्थानां वायुरब्रवीत् ।
दिवि भूम्यन्तरिक्षे च तत्सर्वं जाह्नवी स्मृता ॥
1.37.m: Vāyu spoke of three and a half crores of pilgrimage sites / in heaven, on earth, and in the mid-region; all that is traditionally known as the Jāhnavī.

1.37.s:
yatra gaṅgā mahābhāgā sa deśastat tapovanam /
siddhikṣetraṃ tu tajjñeyaṃ gaṅgātīrasamāśritam //
1.37.d:
यत्र गङ्गा महाभागा स देशस्तत् तपोवनम् ।
सिद्धिक्षेत्रं तु तज्ज्ञेयं गङ्गातीरसमाश्रितम् ॥
1.37.m: Where the illustrious Gaṅgā is, that region is an ascetic grove; / that which is situated on the bank of the Gaṅgā should be known as a realm of attainment.

1.37.s:
yatra devo mahādevo devyā saha maheśvaraḥ /
āste vaṭeśvaro nityaṃ tat tīrthaṃ tat tapovanam //
1.37.d:
यत्र देवो महादेवो देव्या सह महेश्वरः ।
आस्ते वटेश्वरो नित्यं तत् तीर्थं तत् तपोवनम् ॥
1.37.m: Where the god Mahādeva, the Great Lord, resides eternally / as Vaṭeśvara along with the goddess, that is a pilgrimage site, that is an ascetic grove.

1.37.s:
idaṃ satyaṃ dvijātīnāṃ sādhūnāmātmajasya ca /
suhṛdāṃ ca japet karṇe śiṣyasyānugatasya tu //
1.37.d:
इदं सत्यं द्विजातीनां साधूनामात्मजस्य च ।
सुहृदां च जपेत् कर्णे शिष्यस्यानुगतस्य तु ॥
1.37.m: One should whisper this truth into the ear of twice-born people, of virtuous men, of one's own son, / of friends, and of an obedient disciple.

1.37.s:
idaṃ dhanyamidaṃ svargyamidaṃ medhyamidaṃ sukham /
idaṃ puṇyamidaṃ ramyaṃ pāvanaṃ dharmyamuttamam //
1.37.d:
इदं धन्यमिदं स्वर्ग्यमिदं मेध्यमिदं सुखम् ।
इदं पुण्यमिदं रम्यं पावनं धर्म्यमुत्तमम् ॥
1.37.m: This brings prosperity, this leads to heaven, this is pure, this brings happiness, / this is meritorious, this is delightful, purifying, lawful, and supreme.

1.37.s:
maharṣoṇāmidaṃ guhyaṃ sarvapāpapramocanam /
atrādhītya dvijo 'dhyāyaṃ nirmalatvamavāpnuyāt //
1.37.d:
महर्षोणामिदं गुह्यं सर्वपापप्रमोचनम् ।
अत्राधीत्य द्विजो ऽध्यायं निर्मलत्वमवाप्नुयात् ॥
1.37.m: This is a secret of the great sages, releasing from all sins; / having recited this chapter here, a twice-born person attains purity.

1.37.s:
yaścedaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ tīrthaṃ puṇyaṃ sadā śuciḥ /
jātismaritvaṃ labhate nākapṛṣṭhe ca modate //
1.37.d:
यश्चेदं शृणुयान्नित्यं तीर्थं पुण्यं सदा शुचिः ।
जातिस्मरित्वं लभते नाकपृष्ठे च मोदते ॥
1.37.m: And whoever, always pure, constantly hears of this holy pilgrimage site, / attains memory of past lives and rejoices in the vault of heaven.

1.37.s:
prāpyante tānitīrthāni sadbhiḥ śiṣṭānudarśibhiḥ /
snāhi tīrtheṣu kauravya na ca vakramatirbhava //
1.37.d:
प्राप्यन्ते तानितीर्थानि सद्भिः शिष्टानुदर्शिभिः ।
स्नाहि तीर्थेषु कौरव्य न च वक्रमतिर्भव ॥
1.37.m: Those pilgrimage sites are reached by the virtuous who follow the cultured; / bathe in the pilgrimage sites, O descendant of Kuru, and do not be crooked-minded.

1.37.s:
evamuktvā sa bhagavān mārkaṇḍeyo mahāmuniḥ /
tīrtāni kathayāmāsa pṛthivyāṃ yāni kānicit //
1.37.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स भगवान् मार्कण्डेयो महामुनिः ।
तीर्तानि कथयामास पृथिव्यां यानि कानिचित् ॥
1.37.m: Having spoken thus, the venerable Mārkaṇḍeya, the great sage, / told of whatever pilgrimage sites there are on earth,

1.37.s:
bhūsamudrādisaṃsthānaṃ pramāṇaṃ jyotiṣāṃ sthitam /
pṛṣṭaḥ provāca sakalamuktvātha prayayo muniḥ //
1.37.d:
भूसमुद्रादिसंस्थानं प्रमाणं ज्योतिषां स्थितम् ।
पृष्टः प्रोवाच सकलमुक्त्वाथ प्रययो मुनिः ॥
1.37.m: The layout of the earth, the oceans, and so forth, and the established measure of the heavenly luminaries; / questioned, the sage explained everything, and having spoken, he departed.

1.37.s:
ya idaṃ kalyamutthāya paṭhate 'tha śṛṇoti vā /
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo rudralokaṃ sa gacchati //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ purvavibhāge saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.37.d:
य इदं कल्यमुत्थाय पठते ऽथ शृणोति वा ।
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो रुद्रलोकं स गच्छति ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पुर्वविभागे सप्तत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.37.m:
Whoever, having risen at dawn, recites or hears this, / is freed from all sins and goes to the world of Rudra.

Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the auspicious Kūrma Purāṇa.
